featuredPapers.title: Can Multi-modal (reasoning) LLMs work as deepfake detectors?
featuredPapers.authors: Simiao Ren (Dennis), Yao Yao (Dennis), Kidus Zewde (Dennis)
featuredPapers.summary:
Deepfake detection remains a critical challenge in the era of advanced generative models, particularly as synthetic media becomes more sophisticated.
In this study, we explore the potential of state of the art multi-modal (reasoning) large language models (LLMs) for deepfake image detection such as (OpenAI O1/4o, Gemini thinking Flash 2, Deepseek Janus, Grok 3, llama 3.2, Qwen 2/2.5 VL, Mistral Pixtral, Claude 3.5/3.7 sonnet) . 在这项研究中，我们探讨了最先进的多模态（推理）大型语言模型（ LLM ）用于深度伪造图像检测的潜力，例如（ OpenAI O1/4o ， Gemini thinking Flash 2 ， Deepseek Janus ， Grok 3 ， llama 3.2 ， Qwen 2/2 .5 VL ， Mistral Pixtral ， Claude 3.5/3 .7 sonnet ）。
We benchmark 12 latest multi-modal LLMs against traditional deepfake detection methods across multiple datasets, including recently published real-world deepfake imagery. 我们将12个最新的多模态LLM与多个数据集的传统deepfake检测方法进行对比，包括最近发布的真实世界deepfake图像。
To enhance performance, we employ prompt tuning and conduct an in-depth analysis of the models' reasoning pathways to identify key contributing factors in their decision-making process.
Our findings indicate that best multi-modal LLMs achieve competitive performance with promising generalization ability with zero shot, even surpass traditional deepfake detection pipelines in out-of-distribution datasets while the rest of the LLM families performs extremely disappointing with some worse than random guess. 我们的研究结果表明，最好的多模态LLM在零拍摄的情况下通过有希望的泛化能力实现了竞争性能，甚至在分布外的数据集中超过了传统的deepfake检测管道，而其余的LLM系列在比随机猜测更差的情况下表现非常令人失望。
Furthermore, we found newer model version and reasoning capabilities does not contribute to performance in such niche tasks of deepfake detection while model size do help in some cases. 此外，我们发现较新的模型版本和推理能力对deepfake检测等利基任务的性能没有贡献，而模型大小在某些情况下确实有所帮助。
This study highlights the potential of integrating multi-modal reasoning in future deepfake detection frameworks and provides insights into model interpretability for robustness in real-world scenarios. 本研究强调了在未来的deepfake检测框架中集成多模态推理的潜力，并提供了对现实场景中鲁棒性的模型可解释性的见解。

featuredPapers.title: Can Multi-modal (reasoning) LLMs detect document manipulation?
featuredPapers.authors: Zisheng Liang, Kidus Zewde, Rudra Pratap Singh
featuredPapers.summary:
Document fraud poses a significant threat to industries reliant on secure and verifiable documentation, necessitating robust detection mechanisms.
This study investigates the efficacy of state-of-the-art multi-modal large language models (LLMs)-including OpenAI O1, OpenAI 4o, Gemini Flash (thinking), Deepseek Janus, Grok, Llama 3.2 and 4, Qwen 2 and 2.5 VL, Mistral Pixtral, and Claude 3.5 and 3.7 Sonnet-in detecting fraudulent documents. 本研究调查了最先进的多模态大型语言模型（ LLM ） （包括OpenAI O1、OpenAI 4o、Gemini Flash （思维）、Deepseek Janus、Grok、Llama 3.2和4、Qwen 2和2.5 VL、Mistral Pixtral以及Claude 3.5和3.7 Sonnet ）在检测欺诈性文档方面的功效。
We benchmark these models against each other and prior work on document fraud detection techniques using a standard dataset with real transactional documents. 我们使用具有真实交易文档的标准数据集，将这些模型相互对比，并先前在文档欺诈检测技术方面的工作。
Through prompt optimization and detailed analysis of the models' reasoning processes, we evaluate their ability to identify subtle indicators of fraud, such as tampered text, misaligned formatting, and inconsistent transactional sums.
Our results reveal that top-performing multi-modal LLMs demonstrate superior zero-shot generalization, outperforming conventional methods on out-of-distribution datasets, while several vision LLMs exhibit inconsistent or subpar performance.
Notably, model size and advanced reasoning capabilities show limited correlation with detection accuracy, suggesting task-specific fine-tuning is critical. 值得注意的是，模型大小和高级推理能力与检测准确性的相关性有限，这表明特定任务的微调至关重要。
This study underscores the potential of multi-modal LLMs in enhancing document fraud detection systems and provides a foundation for future research into interpretable and scalable fraud mitigation strategies. 本研究强调了多模式LLM在增强文档欺诈检测系统方面的潜力，并为未来研究可解释和可扩展的欺诈缓解策略奠定了基础。
highlights: outperforming conventional methods on out-of-distribution datasets

featuredPapers.title: Asking the World: Generalist Physical Reasoning through Agentic World Modeling and Probing
featuredPapers.authors: Shenxiang Zeng, Chen Yang, Peiyao Chen
featuredPapers.summary:
Physical reasoning from video requires inferring latent physical properties and dynamics beyond direct observation.
Direct VLM inference remains unreliable on complex physical tasks without explicit modeling and validation, while predefined tool pipelines rely on task- and domain-specific priors that limit generalization across materials, dynamics, and reasoning tasks. 在没有明确建模和验证的情况下，直接VLM推理在复杂的物理任务上仍然不可靠，而预定义的工具管道依赖于特定于任务和领域的先验，这些先验限制了跨材料、动态和推理任务的泛化。
We introduce Asking the World (ATW), a generalist agent that constructs and interrogates task-relevant executable worlds through two adaptive stages: World Modeling calibrates a world from video, while World Probing queries, simulates, and intervenes on it to obtain question-relevant evidence.
Rather than prescribing the operations in either stage, ATW determines how to model and probe according to the scene and question. ATW不是规定任何一个阶段的操作，而是根据场景和问题确定如何建模和探测。
We develop PolyWorld Engine, a lightweight and highly programmable Warp-based multiphysics simulator for constructing and probing worlds with rigid bodies, soft bodies, cloth, ropes, fluids, and their coupled interactions. 我们开发了PolyWorld Engine ，这是一款轻量级、高度可编程的基于扭曲的多物理场模拟器，用于构建和探测具有刚体、软体、布、绳索、流体及其耦合相互作用的世界。
CEM-based system identification recovers task-relevant dynamics during World Modeling. 基于CEM的系统识别在世界建模过程中恢复与任务相关的动态。
The resulting world becomes an active workspace for question-directed physical experiments rather than a predetermined downstream tool.
We evaluate ATW on CLEVRER, ContPhy, and three real-world scenarios.
Using Gemini-3-Flash as its base VLM, ATW achieves 80.82% overall per-question accuracy on CLEVRER, improving direct Gemini-3-Flash by 46.50 points, GPT-5.5 by 13.58 points, and PhysMind by 8.27 points. 使用Gemini-3-Flash作为其基础VLM ， ATW在CLEVRER上实现了80.82 ％的整体每次提问准确率，将直接Gemini-3-Flash提高了46.50分， GPT-5.5提高了13.58分， PhysMind提高了8.27分。
On ContPhy, it reaches 70.56% overall accuracy, surpassing Gemini-3-Flash by 28.10 points and GPT-5.5 by 3.53 points.
Across the three real-world scenarios, ATW achieves 71.67% accuracy, 28.33 points above GPT-5.5.
These results establish agentic world modeling and probing as an effective, execution-grounded approach to generalist physical reasoning.

featuredPapers.title: RSI-Opt: Recursive Self-Improvement Optimizer Agents For Model Training
featuredPapers.authors: Binghang Lu, Yige Sun, Guang Lin
featuredPapers.summary:
Conventional neural-network training typically follows a predefined optimization recipe, motivating a LLM agent that monitors training dynamics and adjusts optimizer settings as training progresses, but a fixed agent policy does not accumulate experience across runs.
We introduce RSI-Opt, a plug-and-play Recursive Self-Improvement Optimizer Agents which evolves the knowledge that guides this process: a prompt, a playbook of procedures, a library of tested optimizer code, and a decision cadence.
A meta-agent rewrites this policy using evidence from earlier runs, and an archive retains evaluated policies for further evolution.
Across 5 generations on three training tasks, the meta-agents develop reusable procedures and code and conduct their own CPU proxy experiments.
RSI-Opt substantially improves optimizer-agent performance, with representative raw-space summary $z$-scores increasing from $+10.48$ to $+14.33$ on the evolution suite with Opus 5.5 and from $-0.36$ to $+3.11$ on held-out tasks with GPT-5.5 through cross-model policy transfer.
On the Burgers PDE, it reduces mean relative $L_2$ error by approximately 2.7-fold with Opus 5.5 and 8.8-fold with GPT-6.1 over the fixed-prompt agent baseline, although PDE transfer varies across LLMs and tasks.
Controlled comparisons show that the evolved policy combines reusable optimization knowledge with adaptation to each task: initial decisions capture most observed gains on seen tasks, while continued adaptation improves outcomes on unseen tasks.
These findings demonstrate how procedures and executable tools accumulated across training runs can improve optimizer-agent performance and support transfer to scientific machine learning.

featuredPapers.title: TGR-EvoDAG: A DAG-based Multi-Agent Code Evolution Framework for Generative Recommendation on Tencent
featuredPapers.authors: Junlin He, Junzhang Zhu, Yudong Li
featuredPapers.summary:
Large Language Model (LLM) agents have enabled automated code evolution for algorithm discovery.
However, current recursive self-improvement (RSI) research for sequential recommendation faces a dilemma: general-purpose frameworks lack domain-specific feedback, while recommender-specific frameworks rely on linear evolution.
Crucially, naively integrating them fails when applied to Generative Recommendation (GR).
Unlike end-to-end models, GR relies on a module-cascaded pipeline (tokenization, pre-training, and alignment).
In this paradigm, existing evolution methods suffer from: i) cost blindness, squandering budgets by ignoring stage-asymmetric retraining overheads; and ii) short-sighted evaluation, discarding promising upstream innovations that temporarily regress metrics before downstream adaptation.
To bridge these gaps, we propose TGR-EvoDAG, a multi-agent code evolution framework tailored for GR.
TGR-EvoDAG models code evolution as a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) to maintain multiple evolution branches and merge complementary innovations, unifying advanced search with rich GR diagnostic feedback.
We further introduce stage-aware cost planning to optimize GPU-hour budgets, and active downstream co-adaptation to navigate temporary regressions and unlock cross-stage gains.
On public Amazon datasets, TGR-EvoDAG enables the first autonomous evolution of a complete GR pipeline, improving offline metrics by up to 37.4% and Agent4Rec simulated user satisfaction by 19.7% over the strongest baseline.
Furthermore, in industrial deployment on Tencent's large-scale commercial media platform, the evolved GR achieves a 12.16% relative improvement in offline Hit@1 and a statistically significant 0.40% increase in online click-through rate (CTR).
highlights: first autonomous evolution of a complete GR pipeline

featuredPapers.title: HarnessMM: Recursive Self-Improvement for Harness Token Efficiency
featuredPapers.authors: Yuhua Jiang, Chang Xu, Feifei Gao
featuredPapers.summary:
Agent harnesses repeatedly invoke reasoning after tool feedback, even when an earlier call has already fixed the next action.
We introduce HarnessMM (Harness Minus Minus), a method for improving harness token efficiency through guarded decision reuse and recursive self-improvement (RSI).
RSI iteratively refines companion harness configurations from training feedback, with validation selecting the configuration for deployment.
A controller at the model-tool boundary reuses resolved decisions to replace later reasoning callbacks while actor weights remain fixed.
Executable Decision Graphs store exact actions, literal arguments, causal dependencies, and public guards.
Guarded Decision Reuse activates these persistent decisions from observed receipts; Certified Callback Substitution executes them through the native interface and records removal of the registered slow callback.
New semantic decisions, unsupported evidence, and selector abstention invoke the original actor again.
The representation restricts what feedback may change, while complete-task measurements establish quality and cost.
On HumanEval, HarnessMM preserves Codex success at 90.82\% while reducing Tokens/task (k) from 66.72 to 47.02 (29.54\% saving).
For DeepSeek Harness, success rises from 71.43\% to 85.71\% while Tokens/task (k) fall from 96.28 to 11.62 (87.93\% saving).
A separate MBPP ablation measures 26.91\% lower cost than single-use graphs and 19.52\% lower cost than retained callbacks.
These results establish guarded decision reuse as a practical way to reduce repeated reasoning in existing harnesses.

featuredPapers.title: An Agentic Approach with Evidence-Grounded Verification for Multimodal Emotion Reasoning in Conversation
featuredPapers.authors: Elyas Rashno, Farhana Zulkernine
featuredPapers.summary:
LLM-based multimodal emotion reasoning systems perform well on standard benchmarks, but improving them through instruction tuning can be computationally expensive.
Agentic pipelines built from frozen models avoid this cost, but introduce a different challenge: when a prediction is wrong, the system must identify which agent or stage caused the error.
We address this problem with an agentic framework for traceable multimodal emotion reasoning and prompt-space adaptation.
Modality-specific perception agents analyze visual, acoustic, and lexical inputs and post evidence-cited observations to a shared board.
An integration agent combines these observations with retrieved multimodal examples to produce an emotion description, label set, and supporting citations, while an MLLM critic can request one revision before the output is finalized.
For incorrect predictions, a separate evidence-grounded verification stage applies deterministic checks to verify that cited evidence and references are valid, and an entailment check to determine whether the final claims are supported by that evidence.
Detected failures are then grouped by the responsible component and failure type, converted into targeted prompt patches, and accepted only after validation on a held-out set.
This adapts the agent prompts without updating model weights.
On the MER2025 dataset, targeted prompt adaptation outperforms the frozen static pipeline on all four MLLMs, ranging from 2B to 38B parameters, and matches or outperforms undifferentiated reflection baselines on each of them: VideoLLaMA3-2B, Phi-3.5-vision-instruct, Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct, and InternVL2.5-38B.
It improves F-score by 0.6--2.2 points depending on the backbone, including an increase from 52.3 to 54.5 on Qwen2.5-VL-7B.
highlights: outperforms the frozen static pipeline on all four MLLMs

featuredPapers.title: Compact-Bench: Measuring What Context Compaction Costs Long-Horizon Coding Agents
featuredPapers.authors: Ruopei Sun, Jianfeng Cai, Kangwen Zhao
featuredPapers.summary:
Context compaction lets long-horizon coding agents continue beyond their context windows, but can erase the state needed to finish a task.
Prior evaluations measure efficiency, retained information, or end-to-end success, leaving the effect of a specific history replacement difficult to isolate.
Compact-Bench pairs full-history and summary-only continuations from a shared repository state, and evaluates recurring details and successive production compactions.
It covers 35 SWE-bench repairs, 146 agentic sessions, and 106 production chains.
Across 14 summarizer backbones, stable damage ranges from 5-64% of 22 full-history successes: Claude Opus 4.8 preserves the most repairs, while DeepSeek-Flash damages the most.
With Kimi-K3 as summarizer, the Kimi Code prompt preserves the most task continuations (19/22), whereas Claude Code retains the most recurring details (15.0%).
LLM summaries retain at most 16.0% of recurring details, compared with 79.1% for mechanical extraction; production summaries retain 15.7% at the first boundary.
Failures recur across methods: one repair is damaged by 13/14 backbones, and another by all 5 prompts.
These results show that reliable compaction requires preserving the progress needed to complete a task, and that retaining relevant information alone does not ensure successful continuation.
Code is available at https://github.com/cai-jianfeng/compact-bench and data is available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/caijanfeng/compact-bench.

featuredPapers.title: ImageRSI: Verification-Driven Recursive Self-Improvement for Agentic Image Generation
featuredPapers.authors: Shuo Han, Zhilin Wang, Peng Ling
featuredPapers.summary:
Complex text-to-image requests remain difficult to satisfy reliably.
Verifying and repairing an image can fix an individual output, but a successful repair does not necessarily carry over to other requests.
We present ImageRSI, a framework that keeps the image generator frozen and combines three components: five-dimensional verification and repair within each task, an experience library shared across tasks, and offline updating of the judge.
Candidate experiences enter the library only after paired A/B validation, and the judge is updated with supervised fine-tuning and GRPO on accumulated image-judgment records and evaluated before reuse.
We also introduce ImageReq-Bench, a benchmark of 961 requests built around hard cases in real-world image-generation requests, each paired with an evaluation checklist.
ImageRSI achieves a Checklist Strict Accuracy (CSA) of 52.6% on MindBench (with Nano Banana Pro as the generator) and 65.66% on ImageReq-Bench, and we compare system outcomes across judge-training configurations.
highlights: Complex text-to-image requests remain difficult to satisfy reliably.

featuredPapers.title: Tool-Calling LLM Agents Under Realistic MCP Faults: Scale Does Not Purchase Fault Tolerance
featuredPapers.authors: Antonio Ken Iannillo, Joshua Segun Owotogbe, Roberto Natella
featuredPapers.summary:
LLM agents increasingly rely on external tools exposed via the Model Context Protocol (MCP), yet current benchmarks assume tools respond correctly and on time, leaving agent resilience to realistic tool failures untested.
We introduce MCP-Injector, a drop-in, protocol-aware fault-injection middleware that interposes on the MCP tool-call path with controlled persistence (permanent, transient, intermittent) and seedable schedules.
Its fault model is calibrated to the observed incident distribution (failure mode x persistence) of the public MCP ecosystem, mined from 57,240 issue and pull-request threads across 1,774 open-source MCP repositories.
In a 1,350-cell experiment crossing two backbone sizes (20B, 120B), three agent stacks (custom multi-round plan-and-execute, OpenAI Agents SDK, LangChain), and three fault injection conditions, we find that faults drawn from this permanent-heavy stress profile cause severe quality degradation (task-completion score falls by 60%, from 8.08 to 3.23 out of 10), and that scale does not purchase fault tolerance for the two gpt-oss backbones we test: the 120B retains no larger share of its fault-free score under faults (resilience-ratio model, $p = 0.96$), and its completion rate under faults is, if anything, lower (91.1% vs.
95.6%; difference 4.4 points, 95% CI $[-0.2, 9.3]$).
Agent stacks differ in how well they absorb faults, which suggests that framework-level error handling matters more than model scale.
These results demonstrate that capability benchmarks alone can mask operational brittleness, motivating protocol-aware fault injection as a complementary evaluation dimension for tool-calling agents.

featuredPapers.title: AM-Bench: A Unified Taxonomy and Evaluation Suite for Agentic Misalignment
featuredPapers.authors: Eric Zhang, Terry Jingchen Zhang, Chijioke Ugwuanyi
featuredPapers.summary:
As LLM-based agents are deployed with increasing autonomy in real-world environments, a critical failure mode emerges: agentic misalignment, where agents choose harmful actions over failure.
However, existing safety benchmarks primarily evaluate whether agents comply with explicitly harmful instructions, leaving the conditions that cause agents to choose harmful actions poorly understood.
To address this limitation, we propose AM-Bench, a unified taxonomy and 35 scenario evaluation benchmark spanning seven industries for agentic misalignment grounded in the fraud triangle, a well-established criminological framework explaining goal-directed misconduct.
We adapt this framework to agentic environments and construct our evaluation suite and detection systems along three dimensions: perceived threat, perceived opportunity, and reasoning.
We operationalize each dimension into structured subcategories rooted in prior theory: five threat categories derived from the instrumental convergence thesis, seven opportunity categories drawn from the Emergent Strategic Reasoning Risks (ESRR) taxonomy, and a novel four-question binary reasoning framework synthesized from prior literature.
Our evaluation of 10 frontier models reveals a 62-percentage-point gap in misalignment across scenarios, with Gemini 3 Flash and Gemini 3.1 Pro exhibiting the highest levels of agentic misalignment while Claude Sonnet 4.6 displays near-zero rates across all conditions.
Our reasoning framework further reveals that models may exhibit harmful behaviours without explicit situational awareness or explanation, complicating both mitigation and detection.
AM-Bench scenarios and code are available at https://github.com/AI4Collaboration/Agentic-Misalignment-Bench

featuredPapers.title: daVinci-Env: Open SWE Environment Synthesis at Scale
featuredPapers.authors: Dayuan Fu, Shenyu Wu, Yunze Wu
featuredPapers.summary:
Training capable software engineering (SWE) agents demands large-scale, executable, and verifiable environments that provide dynamic feedback loops for iterative code editing, test execution, and solution refinement.
However, existing open-source datasets remain limited in scale and repository diversity, while industrial solutions are opaque with unreleased infrastructure, creating a prohibitive barrier for most academic research groups.
We present OpenSWE, the largest fully transparent framework for SWE agent training in Python, comprising 45,320 executable Docker environments spanning over 12.8k repositories, with all Dockerfiles, evaluation scripts, and infrastructure fully open-sourced for reproducibility.
OpenSWE is built through a multi-agent synthesis pipeline deployed across a 64-node distributed cluster, automating repository exploration, Dockerfile construction, evaluation script generation, and iterative test analysis.
Beyond scale, we propose a quality-centric filtering pipeline that characterizes the inherent difficulty of each environment, filtering out instances that are either unsolvable or insufficiently challenging and retaining only those that maximize learning efficiency.
With $891K spent on environment construction and an additional $576K on trajectory sampling and difficulty-aware curation, the entire project represents a total investment of approximately $1.47 million, yielding about 13,000 curated trajectories from roughly 9,000 quality guaranteed environments.
Extensive experiments validate OpenSWE's effectiveness: OpenSWE-32B and OpenSWE-72B achieve 62.4% and 66.0% on SWE-bench Verified, establishing SOTA among Qwen2.5 series.
Moreover, SWE-focused training yields substantial out-of-domain improvements, including up to 12 points on mathematical reasoning and 5 points on science benchmarks, without degrading factual recall.

featuredPapers.title: CASE: Confusion-Aware Skill Evolution for Frozen Multimodal Emotion Models
featuredPapers.authors: Siyu Wu, Zeyu Liang, Linghao Wang
featuredPapers.summary:
Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have substantially advanced Multimodal Emotion Recognition (MER) by enabling fine-grained emotion understanding through reasoning over multimodal evidence.
However, they still exhibit systematic confusion between semantically adjacent emotions with highly overlapping multimodal cues.
Existing approaches typically address these errors through global parameter adaptation, making confusion correction costly and inflexible.
We instead observe that emotion confusion is highly localized and therefore better addressed through reusable pair-specific expertise.
Building on this insight, we propose Confusion-Aware Skill Evolution (CASE), the first agent-skill framework for MER.
CASE maintains a sparse, self-evolving library of pair-specific EmotionSkills that externalize affective expertise from model parameters, enabling the learned expertise to be continuously refined and readily transferred across diverse frozen MLLM backbones.
During inference, CASE dynamically retrieves the appropriate EmotionSkill to reinforce boundary-aware reasoning while keeping the MLLM backbone frozen.
Extensive experiments on CA-MER, DFEW, and EMER demonstrate the effectiveness and transferability of CASE across both general-purpose and emotion-specialized MLLMs.
Notably, CASE improves the average accuracy of Qwen3-VL-8B on the CA-MER benchmark from 46.80% to 59.13%, while achieving consistent gains across MLLMs.

featuredPapers.title: PlaceReasoner-Beta: Reasoning-Driven Macro Placement and Benchmarking
featuredPapers.authors: Qiufeng Li, Chengxuan Wang, Rongqian Chen
featuredPapers.summary:
Automated macro placement remains a fundamental challenge in VLSI physical design.
Despite decades of research, existing approaches predominantly optimize hand-crafted proxy objectives, such as estimated wirelength, and typically produce placements through one-shot numerical optimization, limiting their ability to incorporate visual layout context, codified design expertise, and downstream physical-design feedback in a unified loop.
We present PlaceReasoner-Beta, a verifier-guided multi-agent framework that reformulates macro placement as a closed-loop reasoning problem rather than black-box optimization.
A vision-language model (VLM) planner generates candidate placements from the floorplan image, macro specifications, and connectivity structure; a geometric verifier enforces physical legality and expert placement principles; a physical verifier refines candidates using early implementation feedback; and a post-route optimizer further improves promising layouts using final PPA.
To enable reproducible evaluation, we introduce PlaceReasoner-Bench, a fully open end-to-end benchmark built from open RTL designs, EDA tools, and technology libraries.
It comprises 8 designs at two aspect ratios, yielding 16 tasks with fixed floorplans and I/O assignments, so methods differ only in macro positions and orientations and are evaluated using routed PPA and DRC rather than pre-route proxies.
Across the benchmark, PlaceReasoner-Beta achieves the best timing among DRC-clean methods on all square tasks, reducing post-route TNS by 61.2% at 1:1 and 53.0% at 2:1 relative to the classical baseline field.

featuredPapers.title: GaP: A Graph-as-Policy Multi-Agent Self-Learning Harness For Variational Automation Tasks
featuredPapers.authors: Kaiyuan Chen, Shuangyu Xie, Letian Fu
featuredPapers.summary:
For robots to work reliably in commercial and industrial applications, recent advances in agentic coding systems have potential to combine interpretable robot programming with the open-world adaptability of model-free policies.
We focus on "Variational Automation" (VA), a class of tasks that have larger variations in object geometry and pose than fixed automation.
Model-free policies often struggle to close the reliability gap for VA tasks, which must be executed persistently and reliably in commercial and industrial applications.
Motivated by prior work on Task and Motion Planning (TAMP) and the Robot Operating System (ROS), we introduce Graph-as-Policy (GaP), a multi-agent coding harness that generates directed computation graphs with perception, planning, and control nodes from a Modular Open Robot Skill Library (MORSL).
GaP generates an internal simulation environment to rehearse task instances with different graphs in parallel to iteratively refine the graph structure and parameters to improve success rates and throughput.
Evaluation with 8 new open VA task benchmarks, 4 in simulation and 4 in real-world, suggests that GaP can achieve success rates that significantly outperform baselines.

featuredPapers.title: RoboDoctor: Training-Free Recursive Self-Improvement for Robot Policies
featuredPapers.authors: Heyang Yu, Haomin Li, Sihang Li

We study execution as a locus of adaptation: feedback guides the current action and supplies evidence for revising subsequent decisions under fixed model weights.
We introduce RoboDoctor, a training-free framework that connects diagnosis, grounded action, and persistent experience across three revision targets.
The harness allocates control between policy and agent; intervention determines when to assist while preserving useful policy behavior; and operation refines physical methods through observed effects.
Linked experience records retain the reason for a decision, the attempted method, its outcome, and conditions for reuse.
On a curated archive of 54 RoboDojo-Sim task entries, RoboDoctor achieves a five-dimension mean score of 57.10, with a native success rate of 49.44%.
Recorded interactions illustrate strategy changes, selective correction, and grasp revision.
These findings characterize execution-time adaptation in the evaluated system; controlled trials remain necessary to isolate the contribution of cross-episode experience.

featuredPapers.title: Benchmarks Are Surprisingly Compaction-Friendly
featuredPapers.authors: Jeanne Salle, Hardik Bhatnagar, Matthias Bethge
featuredPapers.summary:
Long horizon agentic tasks are now pushing LLM agents past their context window.
To continue the task, the agent scaffold has to free up the context window, a process known as context compaction.
Compaction is generally lossy by design: agents can silently lose task constraints, instructions, or their reasoning behind earlier decisions.
Although compaction is a standard component of coding agent scaffolds, it has not been studied systematically with frontier models on realistic, long horizon agentic tasks.
Previous work evaluate smaller open weight models on toy or synthetic trajectories.
We fix the agent scaffold (OpenCode), implement five compaction strategies inside it, and evaluate three frontier models on three long horizon benchmarks (PaperBench, ProgramBench, PostTrainBench).
For the two 1M context models, the compaction threshold does not measurably affect the task performance, whereas GPT-5.3-Codex, the model with the smallest context window, performs worse at lower thresholds on PaperBench and, less clearly, on PostTrainBench.
No compaction method outperforms default self-summarization, and methods that discard more content cost some models up to 20 points while leaving other models the same.
Compaction can, however, silently remove task constraints: on ProgramBench, the first compaction summary already drops about one third of the task's anticheating rules on average, and this rises monotonically with the number of compactions.
On real user-agent sessions from SWE-chat, instructions about how the agent should work and what it should not do are dropped around 6 times more than specifications of what to build.
We argue that current benchmarks are compaction-friendly: i.e., the objective is fixed and the agent's progress stays on disk, so most of what compaction discards can be recovered, except constraints that don't exist anywhere else.
highlights: first compaction summary already drops about one third of the task's anticheating rules on average
Long horizon agentic tasks are now pushing LLM agents past their context window.

featuredPapers.title: CEMIR vs. FISER: a comparative study of reasoning-based and enrichment-based approaches to pragmatic intent recognition
featuredPapers.authors: Ziya Hosseynzadeh, Farjad Fallah, Farnoosh Fallah
featuredPapers.summary:
Intent recognition in human-robot interaction requires agents to resolve ambiguous natural language instructions by inferring the speaker's underlying goals.
Research has increasingly focused on two notable paradigms for addressing this task: structured symbolic reasoning and multimodal input enrichment.
However, it remains unclear whether enrichment-based methods provide benefit in settings where the ambiguity concerns unstated human intent rather than missing observable scene information.
In this paper, we present a comparative and diagnostic study benchmarking FISER - a framework utilizing structured social and embodied reasoning - against CEMIR (Context-Enriched Multimodal Intent Recognition), a method that performs multimodal enrichment by synthesizing narratives and photorealistic images from textual prompts.
By evaluating both approaches across four Large Language Models (LLMs), ranging from Qwen2.5-Omni-3B to GPT-5, on the HandMeThat v2 benchmark, we analyze their capability to resolve pragmatic ambiguities.
Our statistical analysis, employing multiple-comparison correction, reveals no statistically significant difference in performance between FISER and CEMIR across any model or difficulty level.
This pattern holds across all sixteen model-by-difficulty comparisons, as well as in a targeted ablation isolating CEMIR's narrative and visual components.
Instead, performance is primarily associated with backbone capability and the inherent difficulty of the ambiguity.
These findings suggest a boundary condition for text-derived multimodal enrichment: when the relevant task constraints are already available in the textual instruction, synthetic multimodal augmentation may not provide measurable benefit over structured reasoning on the same text.
highlights: present a comparative and diagnostic study benchmarking FISER - a framework

featuredPapers.title: Before the Ticket: Grounding HPC User Support in Documentation and Resolved Tickets with an Agentic LLM Assistant
featuredPapers.authors: Elham J. Barezi, Primus C Kabuo, Niveditha Nerella
featuredPapers.summary:
Most questions that reach an HPC help desk have already been answered in the center's user guides or in a ticket someone else filed last semester; users still file new tickets because the guides are hard to navigate and the ticket history is not theirs to search.
We present an assistant that answers from both sources: an orchestrator calls two tools over the Model Context Protocol, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) over the live documentation and a Llama-3-8B model fine-tuned with QLoRA on 11,244 query-resolution pairs mined from historical tickets, and merges their answers.
Every model runs on-premises or on the university's hosted LLM service because ticket data may not leave the institution.
On 400 held-out tickets from Purdue's Rosen Center for Advanced Computing, disjoint from training and free of near-duplicates, and evaluated by two judges from model families that generated none of the answers, fine-tuning on resolutions rewritten into self-service guidance is the clear winner in agreement with RCAC's resolutions (BERTScore F1 improves from 0.06 to 0.27 over the base model) and is judged most correct on average.
The end-to-end system does not improve on its tools, although they are complementary: choosing the better answer per question would exceed either tool (judged correctness 3.41 versus 3.20, an oracle bound), while the merge follows the documentation tool in 78% of answers.
Returning one tool's answer instead recovers the fine-tuned tool's quality (3.19 versus 2.66), but neither a learned selector nor an LLM verifier beats that tool alone.

featuredPapers.title: S$^2$-MAS: A Society-Scale Multi-Agent Simulation Framework with 500 Million Household Persona Agents
featuredPapers.authors: Yang Li, Yike Wang, Di Wan
featuredPapers.summary:
Simulating economic responses at society scale requires agents whose decisions reflect household circumstances.
We introduce S$^2$-MAS, a society-scale multi-agent simulation framework built on 500 million synthetic household personas grounded in real-survey data.
Its Genese engine separates decisions from state updates, while reusable financial scenarios and application ledgers track consumption, cash, debt and payments.
Trained with SFT + RLCD on 2.93 million examples, sharp-421m-mlx achieves 74.55% accuracy and 38.37% question-macro F1 on one-shot consumer financial-choice tasks derived from held-out survey responses.
Its accuracy exceeds GLM-5.3-Flash, Jev 1.13, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, GPT-6-Luna and GPT-6-Astra in the common benchmark (full test for the first four; matched 500-group sample for Astra).
We evaluate eight financial task families and simulate 12 million distinct household agents in paired purchase-funding conditions.
Jointly raising purchase goals and approved credit limits increases consumption, with responses differing across age and income groups.
Education, employment and household-size differences persist after age-income standardization and mainly reflect transitions from deferral to purchase.
Asset and debt groups differ in cash drawdown, repayment and closing debt.
S$^2$-MAS links heterogeneous household decisions to evolving consumption, cash and repayment paths, supporting economic experiments across household groups and population scales.

papers.title: Can Multi-modal (reasoning) LLMs work as deepfake detectors?
papers.summary:
Deepfake detection remains a critical challenge in the era of advanced generative models, particularly as synthetic media becomes more sophisticated.
In this study, we explore the potential of state of the art multi-modal (reasoning) large language models (LLMs) for deepfake image detection such as (OpenAI O1/4o, Gemini thinking Flash 2, Deepseek Janus, Grok 3, llama 3.2, Qwen 2/2.5 VL, Mistral Pixtral, Claude 3.5/3.7 sonnet) . 在这项研究中，我们探讨了最先进的多模态（推理）大型语言模型（ LLM ）用于深度伪造图像检测的潜力，例如（ OpenAI O1/4o ， Gemini thinking Flash 2 ， Deepseek Janus ， Grok 3 ， llama 3.2 ， Qwen 2/2 .5 VL ， Mistral Pixtral ， Claude 3.5/3 .7 sonnet ）。
We benchmark 12 latest multi-modal LLMs against traditional deepfake detection methods across multiple datasets, including recently published real-world deepfake imagery. 我们将12个最新的多模态LLM与多个数据集的传统deepfake检测方法进行对比，包括最近发布的真实世界deepfake图像。
To enhance performance, we employ prompt tuning and conduct an in-depth analysis of the models' reasoning pathways to identify key contributing factors in their decision-making process.
Our findings indicate that best multi-modal LLMs achieve competitive performance with promising generalization ability with zero shot, even surpass traditional deepfake detection pipelines in out-of-distribution datasets while the rest of the LLM families performs extremely disappointing with some worse than random guess. 我们的研究结果表明，最好的多模态LLM在零拍摄的情况下通过有希望的泛化能力实现了竞争性能，甚至在分布外的数据集中超过了传统的deepfake检测管道，而其余的LLM系列在比随机猜测更差的情况下表现非常令人失望。
Furthermore, we found newer model version and reasoning capabilities does not contribute to performance in such niche tasks of deepfake detection while model size do help in some cases. 此外，我们发现较新的模型版本和推理能力对deepfake检测等利基任务的性能没有贡献，而模型大小在某些情况下确实有所帮助。
This study highlights the potential of integrating multi-modal reasoning in future deepfake detection frameworks and provides insights into model interpretability for robustness in real-world scenarios. 本研究强调了在未来的deepfake检测框架中集成多模态推理的潜力，并提供了对现实场景中鲁棒性的模型可解释性的见解。
highlights: surpass traditional deepfake detection pipelines in out-of-distribution datasets while the rest of the LLM families perf

papers.title: Can Multi-modal (reasoning) LLMs detect document manipulation?
papers.summary:
Document fraud poses a significant threat to industries reliant on secure and verifiable documentation, necessitating robust detection mechanisms.
This study investigates the efficacy of state-of-the-art multi-modal large language models (LLMs)-including OpenAI O1, OpenAI 4o, Gemini Flash (thinking), Deepseek Janus, Grok, Llama 3.2 and 4, Qwen 2 and 2.5 VL, Mistral Pixtral, and Claude 3.5 and 3.7 Sonnet-in detecting fraudulent documents. 本研究调查了最先进的多模态大型语言模型（ LLM ） （包括OpenAI O1、OpenAI 4o、Gemini Flash （思维）、Deepseek Janus、Grok、Llama 3.2和4、Qwen 2和2.5 VL、Mistral Pixtral以及Claude 3.5和3.7 Sonnet ）在检测欺诈性文档方面的功效。
We benchmark these models against each other and prior work on document fraud detection techniques using a standard dataset with real transactional documents. 我们使用具有真实交易文档的标准数据集，将这些模型相互对比，并先前在文档欺诈检测技术方面的工作。
Through prompt optimization and detailed analysis of the models' reasoning processes, we evaluate their ability to identify subtle indicators of fraud, such as tampered text, misaligned formatting, and inconsistent transactional sums.
Our results reveal that top-performing multi-modal LLMs demonstrate superior zero-shot generalization, outperforming conventional methods on out-of-distribution datasets, while several vision LLMs exhibit inconsistent or subpar performance.
Notably, model size and advanced reasoning capabilities show limited correlation with detection accuracy, suggesting task-specific fine-tuning is critical. 值得注意的是，模型大小和高级推理能力与检测准确性的相关性有限，这表明特定任务的微调至关重要。
This study underscores the potential of multi-modal LLMs in enhancing document fraud detection systems and provides a foundation for future research into interpretable and scalable fraud mitigation strategies. 本研究强调了多模式LLM在增强文档欺诈检测系统方面的潜力，并为未来研究可解释和可扩展的欺诈缓解策略奠定了基础。
highlights: outperforming conventional methods on out-of-distribution datasets

papers.title: Asking the World: Generalist Physical Reasoning through Agentic World Modeling and Probing
papers.summary:
Physical reasoning from video requires inferring latent physical properties and dynamics beyond direct observation.
Direct VLM inference remains unreliable on complex physical tasks without explicit modeling and validation, while predefined tool pipelines rely on task- and domain-specific priors that limit generalization across materials, dynamics, and reasoning tasks. 在没有明确建模和验证的情况下，直接VLM推理在复杂的物理任务上仍然不可靠，而预定义的工具管道依赖于特定于任务和领域的先验，这些先验限制了跨材料、动态和推理任务的泛化。
We introduce Asking the World (ATW), a generalist agent that constructs and interrogates task-relevant executable worlds through two adaptive stages: World Modeling calibrates a world from video, while World Probing queries, simulates, and intervenes on it to obtain question-relevant evidence.
Rather than prescribing the operations in either stage, ATW determines how to model and probe according to the scene and question. ATW不是规定任何一个阶段的操作，而是根据场景和问题确定如何建模和探测。
We develop PolyWorld Engine, a lightweight and highly programmable Warp-based multiphysics simulator for constructing and probing worlds with rigid bodies, soft bodies, cloth, ropes, fluids, and their coupled interactions. 我们开发了PolyWorld Engine ，这是一款轻量级、高度可编程的基于扭曲的多物理场模拟器，用于构建和探测具有刚体、软体、布、绳索、流体及其耦合相互作用的世界。
CEM-based system identification recovers task-relevant dynamics during World Modeling. 基于CEM的系统识别在世界建模过程中恢复与任务相关的动态。
The resulting world becomes an active workspace for question-directed physical experiments rather than a predetermined downstream tool.
We evaluate ATW on CLEVRER, ContPhy, and three real-world scenarios.
Using Gemini-3-Flash as its base VLM, ATW achieves 80.82% overall per-question accuracy on CLEVRER, improving direct Gemini-3-Flash by 46.50 points, GPT-5.5 by 13.58 points, and PhysMind by 8.27 points. 使用Gemini-3-Flash作为其基础VLM ， ATW在CLEVRER上实现了80.82 ％的整体每次提问准确率，将直接Gemini-3-Flash提高了46.50分， GPT-5.5提高了13.58分， PhysMind提高了8.27分。
On ContPhy, it reaches 70.56% overall accuracy, surpassing Gemini-3-Flash by 28.10 points and GPT-5.5 by 3.53 points.
Across the three real-world scenarios, ATW achieves 71.67% accuracy, 28.33 points above GPT-5.5.
These results establish agentic world modeling and probing as an effective, execution-grounded approach to generalist physical reasoning.
Project page: https://asking-the-world.github.io/

papers.title: RSI-Opt: Recursive Self-Improvement Optimizer Agents For Model Training
papers.summary:
Conventional neural-network training typically follows a predefined optimization recipe, motivating a LLM agent that monitors training dynamics and adjusts optimizer settings as training progresses, but a fixed agent policy does not accumulate experience across runs.
We introduce RSI-Opt, a plug-and-play Recursive Self-Improvement Optimizer Agents which evolves the knowledge that guides this process: a prompt, a playbook of procedures, a library of tested optimizer code, and a decision cadence.
A meta-agent rewrites this policy using evidence from earlier runs, and an archive retains evaluated policies for further evolution.
Across 5 generations on three training tasks, the meta-agents develop reusable procedures and code and conduct their own CPU proxy experiments.
RSI-Opt substantially improves optimizer-agent performance, with representative raw-space summary $z$-scores increasing from $+10.48$ to $+14.33$ on the evolution suite with Opus 5.5 and from $-0.36$ to $+3.11$ on held-out tasks with GPT-5.5 through cross-model policy transfer.
On the Burgers PDE, it reduces mean relative $L_2$ error by approximately 2.7-fold with Opus 5.5 and 8.8-fold with GPT-6.1 over the fixed-prompt agent baseline, although PDE transfer varies across LLMs and tasks.
Controlled comparisons show that the evolved policy combines reusable optimization knowledge with adaptation to each task: initial decisions capture most observed gains on seen tasks, while continued adaptation improves outcomes on unseen tasks.
These findings demonstrate how procedures and executable tools accumulated across training runs can improve optimizer-agent performance and support transfer to scientific machine learning.

papers.title: TGR-EvoDAG: A DAG-based Multi-Agent Code Evolution Framework for Generative Recommendation on Tencent
papers.summary:
Large Language Model (LLM) agents have enabled automated code evolution for algorithm discovery.
However, current recursive self-improvement (RSI) research for sequential recommendation faces a dilemma: general-purpose frameworks lack domain-specific feedback, while recommender-specific frameworks rely on linear evolution.
Crucially, naively integrating them fails when applied to Generative Recommendation (GR).
Unlike end-to-end models, GR relies on a module-cascaded pipeline (tokenization, pre-training, and alignment).
In this paradigm, existing evolution methods suffer from: i) cost blindness, squandering budgets by ignoring stage-asymmetric retraining overheads; and ii) short-sighted evaluation, discarding promising upstream innovations that temporarily regress metrics before downstream adaptation.
To bridge these gaps, we propose TGR-EvoDAG, a multi-agent code evolution framework tailored for GR.
TGR-EvoDAG models code evolution as a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) to maintain multiple evolution branches and merge complementary innovations, unifying advanced search with rich GR diagnostic feedback.
We further introduce stage-aware cost planning to optimize GPU-hour budgets, and active downstream co-adaptation to navigate temporary regressions and unlock cross-stage gains.
On public Amazon datasets, TGR-EvoDAG enables the first autonomous evolution of a complete GR pipeline, improving offline metrics by up to 37.4% and Agent4Rec simulated user satisfaction by 19.7% over the strongest baseline.
Furthermore, in industrial deployment on Tencent's large-scale commercial media platform, the evolved GR achieves a 12.16% relative improvement in offline Hit@1 and a statistically significant 0.40% increase in online click-through rate (CTR).
highlights: first autonomous evolution of a complete GR pipeline

papers.title: HarnessMM: Recursive Self-Improvement for Harness Token Efficiency
papers.summary:
Agent harnesses repeatedly invoke reasoning after tool feedback, even when an earlier call has already fixed the next action.
We introduce HarnessMM (Harness Minus Minus), a method for improving harness token efficiency through guarded decision reuse and recursive self-improvement (RSI).
RSI iteratively refines companion harness configurations from training feedback, with validation selecting the configuration for deployment.
A controller at the model-tool boundary reuses resolved decisions to replace later reasoning callbacks while actor weights remain fixed.
Executable Decision Graphs store exact actions, literal arguments, causal dependencies, and public guards.
Guarded Decision Reuse activates these persistent decisions from observed receipts; Certified Callback Substitution executes them through the native interface and records removal of the registered slow callback.
New semantic decisions, unsupported evidence, and selector abstention invoke the original actor again.
The representation restricts what feedback may change, while complete-task measurements establish quality and cost.
On HumanEval, HarnessMM preserves Codex success at 90.82\% while reducing Tokens/task (k) from 66.72 to 47.02 (29.54\% saving).
For DeepSeek Harness, success rises from 71.43\% to 85.71\% while Tokens/task (k) fall from 96.28 to 11.62 (87.93\% saving).
A separate MBPP ablation measures 26.91\% lower cost than single-use graphs and 19.52\% lower cost than retained callbacks.
These results establish guarded decision reuse as a practical way to reduce repeated reasoning in existing harnesses.
