A response-stratified 24-month panel varies purchase goals under a common credit product, with repayment and arrears updating subsequent offers.
S$^2$-MAS links heterogeneous household decisions to evolving consumption, cash and repayment paths, supporting economic experiments across household groups, population scales and time horizons.
highlights: first four; matched 500-group sample for Astra)
Simulating economic responses at society scale requires agents whose decisions reflect household circumstances and the e

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: TRCA: Transition-wise Rubric Credit Assignment for Long-horizon LLM Agents
papers.summary:
Long-horizon large language model (LLM) agents are typically optimized with sparse terminal outcomes, making fine-grained credit assignment across multi-step interactions difficult.
Existing approaches either rely on process evaluators, which incur annotation and inference costs, or derive step-level credit from successful trajectories.
However, successful trajectories are extremely scarce during early-stage reinforcement learning, substantially weakening anchor-based methods.
We propose Transition-wise Rubric Credit Assignment (TRCA), which derives step-level supervision directly from action-induced transitions without learned evaluators or successful anchors.
TRCA evaluates each transition using Evidence, Execution, and Invalidity rubrics to capture task-relevant information acquisition, valid task execution, and invalid or regressive behavior.
From these judgments, Foundational Rubric Reward measures local transition quality, while Breakthrough Rubric Reward tracks newly covered Evidence and Execution conditions to reward incremental task progress.
Combined with terminal outcomes, these signals produce fine-grained step-level advantages for policy optimization.
Experiments on ALFWorld, WebShop, and seven search-augmented question-answering benchmarks show consistent improvements over the evaluated baselines.
With Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, TRCA improves the WebShop score by 6.0%-12.6%; with Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, it improves the average SearchQA score by 1.9%-18.3%.
These results demonstrate the effectiveness of transition-wise rubric credit assignment for long-horizon tasks with sparse successful anchors.
highlights: However, successful trajectories are extremely scarce during early-stage reinforcement learning, substantially weakening

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: MemMux: Runtime Verification and Honest Resource Attribution for Fleets of Parallel Coding Agents
papers.summary:
Developers increasingly run a fleet of coding agents side by side on one workstation.
Terminal multiplexers like tmux and a new generation of agent managers were built to arrange windows, not to govern memory.
When ten agents each spawn language servers, test runners, and browsers, no standard tool can say how much memory belongs to which agent, confirm that a terminated agent's descendants are gone, notice a child that has escaped its agent, or keep the machine off the swap cliff when an out-of-memory (OOM) kill would silently discard uncommitted work.
We treat these as runtime-verification problems: a hosting substrate should emit signals an operator can check while agents run.
We present MemMux, an unprivileged local runtime (no kernel control groups) turning resource governance into checkable signals: per-agent attribution, complete reclamation, escaped-process visibility, bounded footprint under overcommit, and monitoring overhead.
A claims-disciplined benchmark measures each against tmux and a raw-process baseline on identical workloads.
Under a binding memory budget on a Linux host, MemMux holds the fleet under budget (7500 MiB) with zero swap by admitting a subset and reclaiming under pressure, while the ungoverned tools run every agent, pin the machine at its RAM ceiling (2x over budget), and spill about 2 GiB into swap.
MemMux reclaims 100% of a terminated agent's process subtree where the raw baseline strands half of it (tmux matches us here; the raw baseline does not), and it is the only launcher we compare against that surfaces escaped children (10 of 10 detected).
The cost: the always-on 1 Hz monitoring loop runs near 0.6% CPU at one agent but 2.7% at ten, above our 2% target.
Running the harness on real Claude Code sessions shows 100% attribution and low overhead carry over to live agent trees.
We release the engine, benchmark, and reproducer.
highlights: Developers increasingly run a fleet of coding agents side by side on one workstation.

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: AgenticRoboRL: Bringing Coding-Agent Post-Training to Agentic Robotics
papers.summary:
Agentic robotics systems combine planners with robot harnesses to perform complex manipulation tasks.
Recent work improves these systems through better harnesses and external memory, but relies on powerful closed-source models as planners and does not improve the planners' own capabilities.
In contrast, coding agents have improved substantially by post-training the model itself.
We therefore investigate whether post-training can also improve robot planners.
However, applying it across robot harnesses requires accommodating different execution mechanisms, including VLA skill invocation and control-code generation.
To this end, we introduce AgenticRoboRL, a framework for post-training robot planners across different harnesses.
The training recipe combines supervised fine-tuning with multi-turn reinforcement learning.
To accommodate different execution mechanisms, harness-specific adapters connect recorded planner interactions with task outcomes, enabling a common RL training pipeline while keeping execution components fixed.
On LIBERO-PRO, AgenticRoboRL raises the success rate of a 9B-parameter planner from 18.1% to 71.0% without external memory, approaching the 72.1% achieved by Codex (GPT-5.5) with external memory.
These results demonstrate post-training as an effective approach for improving robot planners.
We will release the framework and trained planner checkpoints.
highlights: Agentic robotics systems combine planners with robot harnesses to perform complex manipulation tasks.

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: Amplifying Latency and Cost of LLM Inference via Rowhammer Attack
papers.summary:
Large language models (LLMs) achieve high inference efficiency using optimized GPU kernels generated by just-in-time (JIT) compilation frameworks such as Triton.
Triton compiles GPU kernels through an MLIR/LLVM-based pipeline.
We investigate whether a Rowhammer-induced bit-flip in the CPU's DRAM can degrade GPU-based LLM inference performance while preserving output correctness.
We present LLVMhammer, the first Rowhammer attack that causes LLM inference slowdown by inducing a bit-flip in Triton's compilation pipeline.
A bit-flip in a performance-critical optimization pass causes Triton to generate a functionally identical but suboptimal GPU kernel.
Since Triton caches the generated kernel on disk, a single successful bit-flip causes persistent slowdown across subsequent inference executions.
Triton's target-independent stages are shared across GPU vendors, which makes our attack GPU vendor-agnostic.
To identify exploitable bit-flip locations without manual inspection, we build Karnage, a tool that isolates useful bit-flip locations in Triton's target-independent compilation pipeline.
We evaluate LLVMHammer across a diverse set of LLMs, including Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3, and Deepseek-llm-7B-chat, across NVIDIA RTX 4090 and AMD RX 7900 XTX GPUs.
LLVMhammer increases inference latency of an LLM inference server running on a single GPU by 4-16\%, which, in turn, can translate into additional annual operating costs at the scale of multi-GPU deployments.
We further show that LLVMhammer can also corrupt LLM outputs across different GPU vendors, reducing BERTScore to as low as 25\%, illustrating the broader security implications of bit-flips in Triton's compilation pipeline.
highlights: first Rowhammer attack that causes LLM inference slowdown by inducing a bit-flip in Triton's compilation pipeline
Triton compiles GPU kernels through an MLIR/LLVM-based pipeline.

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: When Self-Consistency Backfires: Majority Vote Hurts the Majority of Hard Science Problems for Small LLMs
papers.summary:
Majority-vote self-consistency (SC) lowers per-problem accuracy on most GPQA Diamond problems for small instruction-tuned models: on 56.6% of problems for Qwen2.5-7B and 65.7% for Llama-3-8B.
An obvious fix is a verifier-free confidence gate that decides which problems to vote on.
We report that the most natural version of that fix also fails, and we separate three signal failures that v1 treated as one.
The token-entropy gate fails for a measurement reason: averaged over a chain of 602 tokens, entropy mostly measures fluency.
The chain average sits 0.0005 nats from the non-answer average and 0.1695 nats from the answer token.
So we measure confidence at the answer token itself.
On Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-Turbo (198 problems, 64 samples each), a sample that disagrees with its problem's plurality still emits its answer at a median margin of at least 20.4 nats, and at least 75.5% of such samples exceed 10 nats.
Both quantities were pre-registered and tested once on 69 problems that no exploratory analysis had seen; both passed.
The unit matters.
Pooled across the benchmark, the margin does separate correct from incorrect samples: the fraction above 10 nats differs by +0.0586 [+0.0160, +0.0994].
Within a problem, paired, it does not: -0.0142 [-0.0501, +0.0215].
Token log-probabilities do carry information, but not for the within-question choice that self-consistency makes.
The agreement gate's failure has no mechanism we can identify, and we leave it open.
The new claims rest on one model: a registered replication on a second model was sampled but could not be evaluated, and we report that instead.
Separately, three reasoning models could not be evaluated on hosted serverless inference at a small budget, each for a different measured reason.
All three are downloadable, so this is a limit of metered APIs, not of what can be known.

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: PointerBench: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Fine-Grained GUI Grounding
papers.summary:
Multimodal Large Language Models have shown promising performance in computer-use tasks, from planning user workflows to grounding natural-language actions to precise UI targets.
Existing end-to-end benchmarks primarily emphasize long-horizon task completion, while GUI grounding benchmarks remain focused on conventional controls and a limited set of professional interfaces.
We introduce POINTERBENCH, a diagnostic suite of 1,500 screenshot-instruction pairs probing three complementary capabilities: thin sub-element identification and geometric grounding in spreadsheets (POINTERBENCH-Sheets), character-level grounding in long-text documents (POINTERBENCH-Text), and mixed GUI grounding across 100 professional applications (POINTERBENCH-Pro).
We carefully curate each task with pixel-exact target geometry and evaluate both general-purpose multimodal models and 39 specialist GUI grounding configurations.
We find text grounding to be the most challenging setting, with Claude Fable 5, GPT-5.6 Sol, and the leading native specialist UI-Venus-2-9B achieving 69.6%, 53.4%, and 25.8% success on POINTERBENCH-Text despite respective 83.2%, 77.7%, and 54.5% average success across POINTERBENCH.
These results reveal substantial headroom in fine-grained GUI grounding across frontier and specialist models.
We publicly release the benchmark and evaluation code at https://github.com/warmwindOS/pointerbench.
highlights: These results reveal substantial headroom in fine-grained GUI grounding across frontier and specialist models.

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: SpatialScout: Can VLM Agents Actively Explore and Map 3D Scenes?
papers.summary:
Spatial intelligence requires agents to actively acquire visual evidence and integrate observations into a coherent representation of the three-dimensional world.
Yet spatial question answering offers limited evidence of whether models can construct accurate metric maps through autonomous exploration.
We introduce SpatialScout, a benchmark for evaluating vision-language model (VLM) agents on active object-level 3D mapping.
SpatialScout comprises 80 diverse indoor scenes containing 3,140 target objects.
Given an object inventory, RGB observations, camera calibration, and camera poses, agents control a camera to explore each scene and estimate object centers in a shared coordinate frame.
The task requires coordinating viewpoint selection, cross-view association, geometric estimation, and map revision under bounded interaction budgets.
Evaluation jointly measures localization accuracy and target coverage through object-scale overlap scores that penalize missing predictions.
Experiments with frontier VLMs reveal substantial limitations: the strongest evaluated model, Claude Opus 5.5, achieves a mean overlap score of 41.71%, with 47.23% of targets exceeding an intersection-over-union (IoU) threshold of 0.5 and only 3.25% exceeding 0.9.
These results reveal a substantial gap between recovering coarse object layouts and constructing complete, precise metric maps.
SpatialScout provides a quantitative testbed for developing agents that build reliable 3D spatial representations through active perception.
Code is available at https://github.com/JesseZZZZZ/SpatialScout.

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: Measuring the Permission Gate: A Stress-Test Evaluation of Claude Code's Auto Mode
papers.summary:
Claude Code's auto mode is the first deployed permission system for AI coding agents, using a two-stage transcript classifier to gate dangerous tool calls.
Anthropic reports a 0.4% false positive rate and 17% false negative rate on production traffic.
We present the first independent evaluation of this system on deliberately ambiguous authorization scenarios, i.e., tasks where the user's intent is clear but the target scope, blast radius, or risk level is underspecified.
Using AmPermBench, a 128-prompt benchmark spanning four DevOps task families and three controlled ambiguity axes, we evaluate 253 state-changing actions at the individual action level against oracle ground truth.
Our findings characterize auto mode's scope-escalation coverage under this stress-test workload.
The end-to-end false negative rate is 81.0% (95% CI: 73.8%-87.4%), substantially higher than the 17% reported on production traffic, reflecting a fundamentally different workload rather than a contradiction.
Notably, 36.8% of all state-changing actions fall outside the classifier's scope via Tier 2 (in-project file edits), contributing to the elevated end-to-end FNR.
Even restricting to the 160 actions the classifier actually evaluates (Tier 3), the FNR remains 70.3%, while the FPR rises to 31.9%.
The Tier 2 coverage gap is most pronounced on artifact cleanup (92.9% FNR), where agents naturally fall back to editing state files when the expected CLI is unavailable.
These results highlight a coverage boundary worth examining: auto mode assumes dangerous actions transit the shell, but agents routinely achieve equivalent effects through file edits that the classifier does not evaluate.
highlights: first deployed permission system for AI coding agents

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: FusionEval: Benchmarking Model Fusion for Large Language Models
papers.summary:
Model fusion aims to integrate the capabilities of multi-expert models into a single model.
Existing evaluations offer limited coverage of reasoning with long chains of thought and tool use, while strong average performance can mask substantial losses in individual expert capabilities.
We introduce FusionEval, a benchmark that provides controlled expert pools, integrates fusion methods with and without additional training, and offers a unified evaluation suite.
The pools contain domain experts independently trained from Qwen3 and Llama base models across math, code, science, instruction following, and tool use.
The suite evaluates capability retention and computational cost on eight public benchmarks under comparable data access rules, reporting normalized average and worst performance, runtime, and peak GPU memory usage.
Extensive experiments show that training-free methods preserve reasoning performance but substantially degrade tool use at both model scales.
In contrast, MOPD preserves tool use and achieves a more balanced capability profile, but requires additional data preparation, inference, and training.
Jointly retaining reasoning, instruction following, and tool use at low computational cost remains a challenge.
We hope FusionEval supports future research on efficient model fusion that jointly preserves expert capabilities.
Our code is available at https://github.com/Baicaihaochi/FusionEval_Benchmark.

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: Spectral Smoothing and Spiking Perturbations Reconfigure Capability Profiles and Selective Task Performance in Large Language Models
papers.summary:
Singular-value spectra encode important structure in transformer feed-forward projections, yet their causal role in downstream behavior remains underexplored.
We study post-hoc spectral smoothing and spiking interventions on the up_proj and down_proj matrices.
Positive perturbation stretches deviations from the geometric mean, making large singular values larger and small ones smaller (spiking), and vice versa.
The intervention preserves singular vectors and the geometric mean of the singular values.
Across five open Llama and Qwen instruction models, we evaluate the perturbed systems on capability-labeled subtasks, standard and chain-of-thought reasoning benchmarks, judge-scored truthfulness, hallucination, and safety tasks, and TRAIT personality probes.
To interpret score shifts, we fit responses in a three-dimensional capability basis consisting of factual knowledge, language understanding, and deductive reasoning.
The induced changes suggest structured rather than purely random sensitivity: large positive perturbations more reliably suppress language and deductive responses, moderate negative perturbations can sometimes improve factual or task-local performance on the evaluated grids, and sensitivity varies strongly by model family, benchmark module, and underlying layerwise spectral inequality.
These results position spectral perturbation as a lightweight intervention for probing how capabilities are organized and traded off in large language models.
highlights: We study post-hoc spectral smoothing and spiking interventions on the up_proj and down_proj matrices.
The intervention preserves singular vectors and the geometric mean of the singular values.

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: ADAPT for Science: A Multi-Agent System for Self-Evolving Scientific Optimization
papers.summary:
Scientific discovery often requires identifying a small number of high-performing designs in vast, constrained search spaces.
This is difficult when evaluations are costly, feasible solutions are sparse, parameters are strongly coupled, and physical constraints are strict.
Recent AI for AI methods can automatically improve algorithms and optimization procedures.
However, general purpose approaches are not designed around scientific priors, physical constraints, and limited evaluation budgets.
We introduce ADAPT for Science, a multi-agent framework that treats scientific optimization as two coupled decisions: where to search and how to search.
ADAPT uses historical designs to identify promising and diverse initial conditions, progressively concentrates computation on favorable search directions, and evolves the optimization procedure from execution feedback.
We evaluate ADAPT on the design of gravitational wave detectors using a differentiable physics simulator and eight unseen detector topologies.
Under matched scientific evaluation budgets, ADAPT achieves a mean loss of 0.204 +/- 0.101, reducing loss by 54.9% relative to the best classical optimizer and by 62.2% relative to the best general purpose agentic evolution baseline.
ADAPT achieves the lowest loss on all unseen topologies among the evaluated baselines.
ADAPT provides a step toward scientific optimization systems that continuously learn from prior experience and their own search outcomes.
highlights: Scientific discovery often requires identifying a small number of high-performing designs in vast, constrained search sp

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: R$^2$Orch: Recursive Self-Improvement for Agent Orchestration via Self-Play within a Skill-Internalization Loop
papers.summary:
In recent years, agentic orchestration has been widely applied to solve complex human tasks.
However, existing orchestration learning still faces key challenges, including hand-designed curricula, advantage collapse when a task's rollouts all reach the same outcome, and unreliable evaluation signals that judge each skill by one noisy score.
To address these challenges, we propose R$^2$Orch, a new paradigm of Recursive Self-Play Orchestration: an inner loop of self-play that improves the orchestrator on self-chosen tasks, and an outer loop that improves how the inner loop improves.
To support this paradigm, we introduce Recursive Learnability, a training objective that rewards a Proposer for choosing tasks whose rollouts keep reaching different outcomes as skills are withdrawn.
Built on this objective, we further propose Skill Withdrawal, in which the outer loop withdraws each skill once a controlled evaluation within self-play shows that the orchestrator performs as well without it.
Moreover, the two loops form one cycle: failures are distilled into skills, skills into parameters, and withdrawals lead the Proposer to new failures, so the orchestrator moves toward zero-skill deployment.
Experimental results on twelve datasets show that R$^2$Orch consistently outperforms baselines across question answering, math, code, and interactive tasks.
Our code is available at https://github.com/beita6969/R2Orch.

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: CollabFlow: Recursive Self-Improvement of Agent Collaboration
papers.summary:
Recursive self-improvement (RSI) lets a system improve from its own outcomes; in LLM-based multi-agent systems, Agents refine one another within a task, and outcomes improve how they collaborate across tasks.
However, existing multi-agent collaboration leaves this loop open: collaboration is pre-defined at the operator level, topology-only learning keeps verbatim exchange that propagates errors, and reward maximization on a system's own outcomes concentrates on a few teams.
To address these challenges, we propose CollabFlow, an RSI system of Learned Agent Collaboration: a trainable Collab-Director constructs teams of complete Agents, a frozen executor runs them, and each round's outcomes retrain the director.
Within each round, the edges of a collaboration graph carry protocols of Evidence-Conditioned Communication: a receiver adopts a differing answer only when the sender's evidence is stronger by a margin, so the director learns who communicates and how.
Across rounds, we further propose Collaborative Trajectory Balance (CTB), a flow-based objective that credits each team once across its construction orders and targets a reward-proportional distribution over teams, so several good teams stay in play.
We also bound how far this self-generated target moves between rounds, which shrinks as records accumulate.
On twelve datasets, CollabFlow outperforms all baselines and keeps improving across rounds.
Code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/CollabFlow-631E.
highlights: outperforms all baselines and keeps improving across rounds

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: CANNBot-CAKE: Collaborative Agentic Kernel Evolution for Ascend NPU
papers.summary:
Efficient custom operators are essential for modern deep learning workloads, yet developing high-performance kernels for Ascend NPUs remains slow, expert-intensive, and difficult to automate.
Although AI agents now approach expert performance on GPU kernel benchmarks, current models remain less capable of generating AscendC kernels for NPUs, potentially reflecting the relative scarcity of relevant training data.
We thus present CAKE, a CANN-native system for deployable custom operators that combines adaptive multi-DSL routing, separate Generation and Evolution modes, and reviewed knowledge reuse through CAKE Book and a Self-Evolving Agent.
On 53 CANN-Bench v1.1 operators on Ascend 950PR, CAKE's aggregated results achieve $100\%$ case pass rate on the standard set (1,060/1,060) and $98.28\%$ on the hidden set (4,167/4,240), with an overall mean score of 78.63 out of 100 and an average performance speedup of $1.334\times$ over the baseline.
Evolution then pushes correct operators further: EngramGateFusion cuts aggregate device time by $46.6\%$ over 20 rounds and roughly halves the mean roofline gap.
These results offer a practical path toward closing Ascend's AI-for-kernel capability gap.
highlights: These results offer a practical path toward closing Ascend's AI-for-kernel capability gap.

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Muffin - A Shared Memory Buffer for Asynchronous AI Agents
papers.summary:
The rise of Agentic AI systems has changed the landscape of artificial intelligence by enabling strong reasoning capabilities through specialized multi-agent interaction with structured self-reflection.
However, in target-driven reasoning tasks, single- and multi-agent systems are often on par in terms of performance gains.
A major challenge is that failures often arise from an ineffective exchange of critical information during inter-agent interaction and coordination.
Different from existing multi-agent debate paradigms that rely on synchronous turn-taking and sharing information across different agents, we propose an inter-agent protocol based on shared Memory bUFFer INference - referred to as MUFFIN - in an asynchronous agentic framework.
In the first step, an orchestrator routes queries based on their reasoning demands and delegates demanding ones to a multi-agent setting, where a shared memory buffer provides asynchronous exchange of intermediate findings while an agent's private reasoning remains local.
Our experiments show that our framework Muffin outperforms established competitors, achieving the best accuracy in 17 out of 20 of our benchmark settings, and provides a better quality-cost trade-off than multi-agent debate: Muffin improves accuracy by 19.2 accuracy points while using 77.4% fewer tokens, without requiring full-trace sharing.
highlights: propose an inter-agent protocol based on shared Memory bUFFer INference - referred to as MUFFIN - in an asynchronous age

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: R$^2$ Flow: Recursive Self-Improvement via Recursive Skill Evolution
papers.summary:
LLM-based agents can improve themselves across tasks by reusing and revising the skills they orchestrate into executable procedures.
Flow-based training fits this loop: it samples procedures in proportion to reward, and the flow through each skill credits it for the next library revision.
Three obstacles stand in the way of making this self-improvement reliable: flow training suffers strategy collapse over tree-structured histories; nonnegative flow-based credit rewards frequent use as if it were benefit; and library edits rest on the task reward the policy optimizes.
We introduce R$^2$ Flow, a recursive self-improvement framework that alternates policy learning, independent verification, and versioned skill-library updates on a shared-state orchestration graph.
The graph merges histories that differ only in the order of independent steps, allowing flow training to pool evidence across equivalent executions.
A flow-share readout of the trained flow, invariant to the backward policy, and a separate signed utility rank which skills to change, verifier evidence decides whether an edit is warranted, and a residual-variance plateau sets when to update.
Committed edits reshape the graph the next policy learns on, realizing recursive skill evolution.
Across question answering, mathematical reasoning, interactive decision making, and code generation, R$^2$ Flow improves task accuracy and library-edit precision over heuristic orchestration, reinforcement learning, and skill-evolution baselines, and transfers across executors.
Code is available at https://github.com/beita6969/r2flow.
highlights: LLM-based agents can improve themselves across tasks by reusing and revising the skills they orchestrate into executable

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: RSI Control: Can AI Models Perform Covert Sabotage in the Self-Improvement Process?
papers.summary:
Recursive self-improvement, in which frontier AI models work on training the next generation, is quickly becoming a reality.
However, the safety of this process has received far less attention than it should.
A misaligned model training its successor can shape what that successor knows, how it behaves, and what it wants, and the harm carries forward into the next generation.
We study this risk through the lens of AI control.
We introduce RSI Control Arena, a testbed in which a frontier model, acting as an autonomous R\&D agent, is given a benign main task from a stage of a successor model's training pipeline together with a covert side task to install a misaligned property in the successor.
The testbed contains 16 side tasks in three classes, forming 22 task pairs with main tasks that span the pipeline from data curation to reinforcement learning.
We evaluate six frontier models as agents against LLM monitors that read the transcript of the run and the agent's reasoning.
We observe that every model completes a substantial share of the side tasks without degrading the main-task performance, including side tasks that make the successor itself a better saboteur.
Under minimal instructions to stay covert, models already produce successful attacks that monitors fail to detect, and providing a short list of evasion tactics further reduces the detection rate.
Monitors with access to agent's reasoning detects most attacks, but not all.
Our results indicate that recursive self-improvement raises significant safety concerns, and that strong safety effort should be in place before models are trusted with greater responsibility of training their successors.
highlights: Recursive self-improvement, in which frontier AI models work on training the next generation, is quickly becoming a real

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: A Three-Pillar Governance Framework for Safe and Trustworthy AI Agents
papers.summary:
AI agents capable of autonomous decision-making introduce significant challenges related to safety, alignment, accountability, and human oversight.
Existing Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) and responsible AI approaches provide important foundations, but many remain fragmented across system design, governance, and operational deployment.
This paper presents a Three-Pillar (3P) model and framework for developing safe and trustworthy AI agents through transparency, accountability, and trustworthiness.
The framework defines an evolutionary path in which increasing agent autonomy is introduced through progressive validation, structured human oversight, and auditable operational controls.
We further describe how the model supports agent lifecycle monitoring, decision traceability, escalation management, and human-agent collaboration within enterprise agentic environments.
By integrating oversight principles with operational mechanisms, the proposed framework provides a practical foundation for deploying AI agents that remain aligned with human intent while enabling controlled progression toward higher autonomy.
highlights: AI agents capable of autonomous decision-making introduce significant challenges related to safety, alignment, accountab

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: EvoSteer: Online Self-Evolving Graph Orchestration via Reference-Anchored Credit Assignment
papers.summary:
In recent years, LLM-based multi-agent systems have been widely applied to orchestrate tool-using agents into executable communication graphs.
However, existing self-evolving orchestration still faces key challenges, including post-hoc evolution that revises the team only after the trajectory ends, credit diffusion that gives every action the same terminal advantage under confounded baselines, and skill admission that is uncalibrated and never retired.
To address these challenges, we propose EvoSteer, a new paradigm of Online Self-Evolving Graph Orchestration -- the orchestrator builds a running team and repairs its plausible but failing steps from execution features and a learned value estimate.
To support this paradigm, we introduce Anchored Trajectory Balance (AnchorTB), a regression-style flow-matching loss that assigns each orchestration action a coefficient by balancing subtrajectories against a frozen reference.
Built on the learned flow, we further propose Validated Skill Admission, in which a candidate skill is tried before promotion and promoted only if paired evidence passes a sequential test under a shared nominal testing budget.
Moreover, AnchorTB combines measured task-level reference reward statistics with prefix-dependent corrections.
Experimental results on twelve datasets show that EvoSteer significantly outperforms baselines across question answering, mathematical reasoning, code generation, and interactive decision making.
Our code is available at https://github.com/beita6969/evosteer.

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: RoleFlow: Self-Evolving Multi-Role Agentic Collaboration via Structural Adaptation
papers.summary:
Large language model (LLM) based multi-agent systems often rely on predefined collaboration structures, limiting their adaptability to evolving task requirements.
Although recent approaches enable dynamic orchestration, trajectory-level rewards they apply assign one outcome to each decision, ofen struggling to identify the contributions of individual structural changes.
We propose RoleFlow, a self-evolving multi-role agentic system that refines collaboration structures through feedback-driven atomic edits and on-demand role synthesis.
To make structural adaptation learnable, we introduce Single-Edit Counterfactual Policy Optimization (SECPO), which evaluates each edit against its no-edit counterpart at the same chain state and assigns targeted credit to edit-specific tokens.
Across seven benchmarks spanning four domains, RoleFlow achieves the optimal average performance, surpassing the strongest competitor by 4.7 points.
It leads on all three multi-hop QA benchmarks by 3.2-7.5 F1 points and also shows supremacy on mathematical reasoning, web interaction, and code generation.
Further analyses demonstrate cross-benchmark transferability, training-data efficiency, and cross-executor generalization.

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Auto-Director: Leveraging Multi-Agent Collaboration for Autonomous Video Editing
papers.summary:
Autonomous video editing from open-world resources remains a challenging problem in multimedia content creation.
Retrieval-based methods are constrained by fixed source material and lack creative flexibility, while generative models struggle with long-horizon coherence and often diverge from user intent.
Both paradigms fail to replicate the structured, multi-stage reasoning that underlies professional post-production.
To address these limitations, we present Auto-Director, a tool-augmented multi-agent framework that mirrors professional editorial workflows: a Planning Agent decomposes abstract topics into fact-grounded scripts via retrieval-augmented planning; a Material Agent indexes open-world footage through shot segmentation and visual tagging; an Editor Agent assembles semantically aligned clips with MLLM-driven spatial adaptation; and a Critic Agent governs an iterative Reflect-and-Revise loop that checks scene-level alignment and pacing.
To rigorously evaluate this new paradigm, we introduce VEdit-Bench, a benchmark of 100 expert-curated topics with human-annotated Golden Scripts and a five-dimensional metric suite covering Narrative Logic, Factual Accuracy, Semantic Alignment, Compositional Quality, and Stylistic Cohesion.
Extensive experiments demonstrate that Auto-Director significantly outperforms baseline methods in both automated metrics and human evaluation, effectively bridging the gap between amateurs and professional-grade video production.
highlights: outperforms baseline methods in both automated metrics and human evaluation

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Self-Assessment Reinforcement Learning for Search-State Awareness in Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models
papers.summary:
Recent advances in search agents have enabled large language models to tackle complex tasks by retrieving and synthesizing external information.
However, existing search agents often lack search-state awareness, i.e., the ability to recognize what information has been obtained and what remains missing, leading to hallucinated reasoning and prematurely terminated search.
To address this limitation, we propose Self-Assessment Reinforcement Learning (SARL), a reinforcement learning framework in which models learn to recognize their own search state during training and improve their search behavior accordingly, without requiring additional assessment at test time.
SARL achieves this through a dual reward design that captures the corrective effect of each assessment while penalizing excessive reliance on it, jointly encouraging effective and efficient search trajectories.
Under this setup, SARL achieves a 24.3% relative improvement over the strongest baseline, with average gains of 35.9% on multi-hop reasoning and 27.9% on deep research benchmarks against the strongest per-benchmark baselines.
SARL further surpasses methods built on auxiliary supervision or multi-agent coordination, despite operating as a standalone RL framework with no inference-time scaffolding.
Beyond final performance, SARL maintains training stability under extended search horizons, a regime where existing methods consistently degrade, enabling sustained gains as task complexity grows.
highlights: surpasses methods built on auxiliary supervision or multi-agent coordination

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Questioning Instrumental Convergence in RLVR: Checkpoint Evidence from OLMo-3
papers.summary:
Instrumental convergence is often invoked as a general reason to expect capable agents to acquire or express power-seeking subgoals: self-preservation, resource acquisition, deception, or resistance to oversight which poses an important threat to the society.
For LLMs, reinforcement learning is the first stage of post-training that directly optimizes behavior against an objective; therefore, it is the stage where convergent instrumental behavior, on IC grounds, likely to appear.
Does reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) make a model more likely to express instrumental-convergence behavior, or does this depend on the training regime, evaluation frame, and stage of post-training?
We study this question as a checkpoint-conditioned behavioral trajectory rather than as a single before/after safety score.
Using InstrumentalEval, we evaluate OLMo-3-7B-Think across SFT, DPO, 13 intermediate RLVR checkpoints, and the final RLVR model.
The trajectory is nonmonotonic: instrumental rate rises from 25.0% at SFT to 46.1% near RLVR step 200, then falls to 11.8% at the final checkpoint.
Paired item-level tests and step-wise regression support the final SFT-to-RLVR reduction.
Prompt framing does not explain this pattern: a harmful-prompt indicator combined with other framing effects explains only 15% of within-checkpoint score variance on average, and Iterative Null-space Projection (INLP) removes a detectable framing direction without changing the SFT-to-final-RLVR gap.
Together with preliminary 32B endpoint results (35.53% SFT to 22.37% RLVR final), these findings indicate that RLVR does not monotonically increase instrumental behavior in this setting: the rate rises early, then falls below the SFT baseline.
The result is specific to this model family and benchmark, and judge agreement is moderate, so absolute rates should be read cautiously.
highlights: first stage of post-training that directly optimizes behavior against an objective; therefore

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Conservative Meta-Agent Search: Architecture Adaptation under Non-Stationarity
papers.summary:
Automated agentic-system design is typically evaluated on static task suites with immediate scalar rewards.
Deployed systems face persistent shift, delayed dependent feedback, correlated component failures, and costly architecture changes.
We formalize meta-agent architecture search as sequential incumbent replacement with switching costs and hard risk constraints and introduce Conservative Meta-Agent Search (CMAS).
CMAS retrieves archived architectures and proposes typed graph edits, then scores each against the incumbent by paired shadow replay under common random numbers, with interventional component credit.
Promotion requires an empirically calibrated, variance-penalized simultaneous score above a pre-specified margin, and is followed by a simulated canary stage and pre-specified rollback.
Since backtests cannot certify meta-level skill, we introduce MetaInvest-Bench, a regime-switching simulator whose specified worker competence makes a surrogate-optimal architecture computable, with leakage-controlled replay, adversarial governance tracks, and five negative controls.
Financial streams serve as a risk-sensitive testbed for meta-level generalization; we claim no alpha.
Across 96 streams, CMAS cuts normalized mean surrogate dynamic-oracle regret from 0.116 to 0.104 and raises held-out utility from 0.44 to 0.48 over the strongest adaptive baseline; when extra workers add no value, it contracts to near-single-agent teams.
Its deployment inference cost is ~6% lower, though its search-inclusive token cost is the highest of the methods compared.
The observed per-update false-promotion rate is 3.4% against a nominal 5% target, and 4.8% in a sealed rerun.
The calibration is empirical: it concerns an update-level replay statistic on an author-designed benchmark, and guarantees neither full-utility improvement, nor absence of simulated canary-stage harm, nor sequence-level error control.
highlights: Automated agentic-system design is typically evaluated on static task suites with immediate scalar rewards.

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: CLEAR: Context Augmentation from Contrastive Learning of Experience via Agentic Reflection
papers.summary:
Large language model agents rely on effective model context to obtain task-relevant information for decision-making.
Many existing context engineering approaches primarily rely on the context generated from the past experience and retrieval mechanisms that reuse these context.
However, retrieved context from past tasks must be adapted by the execution agent to fit new situations, placing additional reasoning burden on the underlying LLM.
To address this limitation, we propose a generative context augmentation framework using Contrastive Learning of Experience via Agentic Reflection (CLEAR).
CLEAR first employs a reflection agent to perform contrastive analysis over past execution trajectories and summarize useful context for each observed task.
These summaries are then used as supervised fine-tuning data to train a context augmentation model (CAM).
Then we further optimize CAM using reinforcement learning, where the reward signal is obtained by running the task execution agent.
By learning to generate task-specific knowledge rather than retrieve knowledge from the past, CAM produces context that is better tailored to the current task.
We conduct comprehensive evaluations on the AppWorld and WebShop benchmarks.
Experimental results show that CLEAR consistently outperforms strong baselines.
It improves task completion rate from 72.62% to 81.15% on AppWorld test set and averaged reward from 0.68 to 0.74 on a subset of WebShop, compared with baseline agent.
Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/awslabs/CLEAR.
highlights: propose a generative context augmentation framework
first employs a reflection agent to perform contrastive analysis over past execution trajectories and summarize useful c

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Lifetime-valid decisions by continually evolving AI analysts
papers.summary:
AI agents increasingly act as analysts whose decision can often be cast as hypothesis tests.
Classical tests control the Type I error rate, the probability of rejecting a true null hypothesis, for fixed procedures.
However, AI analysts introduce internal randomness and can evolve continuously over time.
As AI analysts evolve, the risk of approving versions with Type I error rates above the target can accumulate, and adaptive use of evaluation feedback can lead to overfitting.
We introduce continual validation, which evaluates each proposed AI analyst version before deployment using simulated data under the null hypothesis, with scenarios that can be randomized and expanded over time.
We prove that, regardless of how updates are chosen or how many are proposed, the lifetime probability of ever deploying a version whose Type I error rate exceeds the allowed level remains bounded.
This guarantees that every subsequent decision controls the Type I error rate at the target level across these scenarios.
At the same time, updates with sufficiently low Type I error rates pass validation with high probability, allowing the analyst to continuously improve its performance without sacrificing rigor.
In two examples involving evolving AI analysts for bioequivalence studies and product A/B tests, Type I error rates reached 0.098 and 0.183 without continual validation, compared with at most 0.045 and 0.044 with it, while retaining 82% and 96% of the power from optimally selected valid updates.
highlights: exceeds the allowed level remains bounded

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Network topology shapes consensus and vulnerability in LLM populations
papers.summary:
As large language models (LLMs) are deployed in interacting populations, their collective behaviour depends not only on the models but also on who interacts with whom.
Studies of convention formation in LLM populations have mainly tested well-mixed interactions.
We place policies extracted from four LLMs on fully connected, random regular, and heterogeneous networks, with $10^3$ to $10^5$ agents playing the naming game.
Topology affects how quickly consensus emerges, sometimes whether it emerges at all, and, in rare cases, which convention wins.
Sparsest networks slow consensus up to twelvefold.
Yet, by preserving correlations between persistent neighbours, they restore consensus in some cases that fail to converge under well-mixed interactions.
Networks also govern vulnerability to adversarial attack.
We measure the critical mass of committed agents needed to overturn an established convention.
Tipping thresholds follow the same ordering across models and conditions: hubs $\leq$ random $\leq$ low-degree nodes.
On the most heterogeneous topology, median critical masses are 3%, 16%, and 35%, respectively; targeting hubs requires one-sixth as many committed agents as random placement.
For most models, networked populations are easier to tip than well-mixed ones, so well-mixed estimates can overstate robustness.
Assessing the safety of multi-agent AI requires mapping who interacts with whom.
highlights: Studies of convention formation in LLM populations have mainly tested well-mixed interactions.
Topology affects how quickly consensus emerges, sometimes whether it emerges at all, and, in rare cases, which conventio

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Automating Feature Flag Cleanup at Scale with Multi-Agent LLM Systems: An Industrial Experience at DoorDash
papers.summary:
Feature flags are runtime configuration mechanisms used for gradual feature rollouts, experimentation, and kill switches.
Once a feature is fully rolled out, the flag and its gated code become technical debt and can introduce operational risk through inadvertently enabling dormant code paths.
At DoorDash, over 56,000 feature flags span 623 repositories, with 1,659 currently stale as of May 2026, with internal estimates of one to two hours per manual cleanup.
Existing rule-based cleanup tools proved insufficient in DoorDash's codebases.
Our contribution is an end-to-end automated LLM-based feature flag cleanup system that integrates querying live feature flag rollout data using MCP, Jira ticket processing, and end-to-end pull request creation.
Our system successfully produced engineer-approved flag removal PRs for 45 (90%) of the 50 stale flags it was evaluated on, proving the system's operational viability at scale with each cleanup averaging only $4.79 and 13.8 minutes.
We evaluated the system's quality and reliability boundary based on success rates, cost per cleanup and time metrics.
Furthermore, we discuss our lessons learned when architecting this system, to provide practical guidance for developing similar multi-agent systems.
highlights: Automating Feature Flag Cleanup at Scale with Multi
Feature flags are runtime configuration mechanisms used for gradual feature rollouts, experimentation, and kill switches

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: PhyEvolve: Multi-Agent State-Evolution Planning for Physics-Aware Video Generation
papers.summary:
Recent advances in text-to-video generation have substantially improved visual fidelity, yet existing models still struggle to understand the physical evolution implicit in user prompts, making it difficult to generate videos with continuous physical state evolution.
Here, we propose PhyEvolve, a multi-agent framework that enhances natural-language prompts through structured state-evolution planning.
PhyEvolve consists of three agents: a Director, a Physical Evolver, and a Composer.
Given a user prompt and an optional first frame, the Director grounds the scene and disentangles physical events from observation changes.
The Physical Evolver uses scene evidence to identify physical mechanisms then constructs causally linked state transitions that unfold throughout the video, whether visible or not.
The Composer utilizes these transitions to enhance the original prompts.
Without retraining or model modification, PhyEvolve works directly with existing generators through prompt replacement.
Extensive experiments on four major benchmarks show that PhyEvolve achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming the cutting-edge prior agentic baseline by 7.9 percentage points on average.
These results demonstrate that explicit causal state-evolution planning improves physical consistency and state continuity in generated videos through natural-language prompt enhancement.
highlights: outperforming the cutting-edge prior agentic baseline by 7

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: MLEvolve: A Self-Evolving Framework for Automated Machine Learning Algorithm Discovery
papers.summary:
Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly applied to long-horizon tasks such as scientific discovery and machine learning engineering (MLE), where sustained self-evolution becomes a key capability.
However, existing MLE agents suffer from isolated exploration, inefficient experience reuse, and lack of hierarchical control, which together hinder long-horizon optimization.
We present MLEvolve, an LLM-based self-evolving multi-agent framework for end-to-end machine learning algorithm discovery.
By extending tree search to Progressive MCGS, MLEvolve enables cross-branch information flow through graph-based reference edges and gradually shifts the search from broad exploration to focused exploitation with an entropy-inspired progressive schedule.
To allow the agent to evolve with accumulated experience, we introduce Retrospective Memory, which combines a cold-start domain knowledge base with a dynamic global memory for task-specific experience retrieval and reuse.
For stable long-horizon iteration, we further decouple strategic planning from code generation with adaptive coding modes.
Evaluation on MLE-Bench shows that MLEvolve achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple dimensions including average medal rate and valid submission rate under a 12-hour budget (half the standard runtime).
Moreover, MLEvolve also outperforms specialized algorithm discovery methods including AlphaEvolve on mathematical algorithm optimization tasks, demonstrating strong cross-domain generalization.
Code is available at https://github.com/InternScience/MLEvolve.
highlights: outperforms specialized algorithm discovery methods including AlphaEvolve on mathematical algorithm optimization tasks

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: AgentVQA: A Unified Benchmark for Agentic Visual Understanding
papers.summary:
Vision-language models (VLMs) can perform a broad range of tasks across diverse settings, yet their performance in agentic contexts remains poorly understood.
Although online evaluations in simulators and real-world environments are essential for measuring interactive agent performance, they are costly and challenging to scale.
Complementary offline VQA benchmarks can enable faster and more reliable comparisons across agentic domains, yet existing benchmarks remain limited and fragmented.
To address this gap, we introduce AgentVQA, an offline benchmark for evaluating VLMs on realistic agentic scenarios across five agent domains: Web Agents, Robotics, Egocentric Videos, Games, and Spatial Planning.
We build AgentVQA by manually selecting 1000 challenging, real-world agent examples from 23 source datasets and adapting them for reliable offline evaluation.
The resulting benchmark preserves realistic scenarios from interactive environments across diverse domains, and its model rankings track those from corresponding online evaluations.
Across the 22 evaluated models, the best achieves only 58.5% accuracy.
Our cross-domain analysis shows that errors are driven primarily by failures to ground and maintain accurate representations of the current and evolving visual state, including localizing relevant UI elements, interpreting motion, tracking state changes over time, and inferring 3D spatial relationships, rather than by task misinterpretation or downstream logical reasoning.
highlights: Across the 22 evaluated models, the best achieves only 58.5% accuracy.

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: UniField++: A Unified Agentic Framework with Loop Reasoning for MRI Field-Strength Enhancement
papers.summary:
MRI field-strength enhancement seeks to combine the accessibility of low-field scanners with the image quality of high-field scanners.
Yet, existing methods remain prone to anatomical hallucinations, as uniform processing leaves difficult brain regions insufficiently examined and scarce paired data limit their learning of how tissue contrast and anatomical visibility change across field strengths.
To address these challenges, we propose UniField++, a two-agent framework that unifies enhancement tasks across multiple field-strength transitions, including 64mT-to-3T and 3T-to-7T.
Unified learning allows both the VLM-based planner and the flow-matching-based enhancer to draw on field-dependent image characteristics observed across tasks, rather than relying on a single transition.
Trained with radiologists' annotations of hallucination-prone regions and corresponding correction plans, the planner predicts regional risk and formulates targeted restoration strategies.
Guided by these plans, the enhancer performs loop reasoning along the flow-matching trajectory, repeatedly processing high-risk regions for additional refinement.
Together, cross-transition learning and risk-guided refinement support anatomically faithful enhancement across field strengths.
Across the evaluated tasks, UniField++ improves PSNR by an average of 2.74 dB and SSIM by 14.05 percentage points over comparison methods, with corresponding gains of 3.97 dB and 13.92 percentage points over the ablation baseline.
It also maintains enhancement quality on an external cohort with an unseen field strength and improves downstream whole-brain segmentation Macro Dice by an average of 0.1457 over the original low-field images.
Code is available at https://github.com/CUHK-AIM-Group/UniField_plusplus.
highlights: MRI field-strength enhancement seeks to combine the accessibility of low-field scanners with the image quality of high-f

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Learning to Incentivise: Using Reinforcement Learning for Sustainable Urban Mobility
papers.summary:
Traffic management has traditionally focused on toll-based and road pricing solutions.
However, road pricing often raises concerns about accessibility and public dissatisfaction, leading to its prohibition in some places, such as Finland.
This study optimises the dynamic allocation of incentives to drivers, encouraging them to reroute onto alternative (potentially longer) paths to achieve greater societal benefit, reduced total travel time (TTT) and total emissions in the transportation network, contributing to sustainable urban mobility.
We employ a multi-agent reinforcement learning approach to dynamically assign incentives to drivers to reduce both TTT and emissions, with travel times estimated using traffic simulation software.
We demonstrate that, with an unlimited budget and an objective of minimising travel time, the incentive scheme reduces TTT by 16%, compared to the dynamic User-Equilibrium (UE) with a budget equivalent to about 11% of the UE total time.
When the goal is to minimise emissions, a 9% reduction in CO2 emissions is observed under an unlimited budget.
We demonstrate a critical trade-off: minimising TTT leads to an increase in emissions, while prioritising emission reductions raises TTT.
However, with the right combination of weights in the multi-objective function, both TTT and total emissions are improved beyond the baseline.
highlights: Traffic management has traditionally focused on toll-based and road pricing solutions.

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Is Complex Agentic Memory Always Needed? Naive RAG Is Stronger Than We Thought
papers.summary:
LLM memory is widely used in long-term conversation understanding.
Agentic memory systems often use mutation, structural organization, learned retrieval strategies, or other complex operations.
Is this complexity always necessary?
We study Raw-RAG, a naive RAG baseline using dense retrieval and reranking over raw history to supply evidence to a reader LLM.
Across LoCoMo, LongMemEval, MEME, and MemoryAgentBench, Raw-RAG ranks first among the compared memory systems in six of seven benchmark-model settings, outperforming the strongest compared agentic memory system by 0.13-5.53 points.
We investigate why raw-history retrieval remains competitive.
Evidence analysis shows that its higher coverage of necessary evidence can offset lower utilization.
Useful evidence includes both answer values and the relations and dependency paths needed to derive them.
Even complete access to transformed memory stores leaves an accuracy gap relative to raw evidence, highlighting the importance of preserving raw information.
These findings challenge the necessity of complex agentic memory for the evaluated conversation tasks and establish naive RAG as an essential baseline.
highlights: outperforming the strongest compared agentic memory system by 0
first among the compared memory systems in six of seven benchmark-model settings
LLM memory is widely used in long-term conversation understanding.

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Agentic Knowledge-Model Co-Evolution via Consistency Regularization
papers.summary:
LLM agents can evolve by learning from accumulated experience.
Existing approaches extract reusable external knowledge, such as skills and memories, from experience to guide subsequent task solving, with some further internalizing this knowledge through model training.
However, different ways of analyzing and transforming the same experience can yield knowledge with substantially different utility, even when the resulting guidance appears reasonable.
Inspired by consistency regularization, we identify consistent utility gains across different ways of analyzing the same experience, rather than relying on any single way of analyzing it.
We introduce SPLICE, a framework for consistency-regularized knowledge-model co-evolution.
It constructs evolution views by perturbing how the same experience is analyzed, producing different knowledge candidates.
Knowledge updates are then guided by common gain, which accounts for utility gains and their consistency across views.
During model evolution, self-distillation internalizes the evolved knowledge alongside reinforcement learning, using knowledge associated with consistent utility degradation as a contrastive reference.
The two processes interleave, with model updates driving further knowledge evolution.
Experiments across diverse domains show that SPLICE outperforms knowledge evolution and model training baselines by up to 7.1 and 4.6 points in average accuracy, while its evolved knowledge reduces output tokens per correct solution by up to 44% and transfers across model sizes and families.
highlights: outperforms knowledge evolution and model training baselines by up to 7

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: RIPPLE: Recovery Internalization through Process-Level Policy Learning and Effect-Aware Credit for Long-Horizon Agentic Coding
papers.summary:
Long-horizon coding agents can observe a failure and generate a plausible critique yet continue along the same incorrect trajectory.
We call this the Critique-to-Action Handoff Gap.
We introduce RIPPLE, a recovery-oriented training framework that internalizes process-level guidance into a single self-recovering policy.
A prefix-only teacher provides evidence-grounded recovery supervision without access to future actions or terminal outcomes.
After lightweight distillation, reinforcement learning assigns stage-specific credit to reflection triggering, diagnosis, and corrective action.
Local validity signals gate trajectory advantages so that intermediate recovery decisions do not indiscriminately inherit terminal outcomes.
Across four repository-level software-engineering benchmarks, RIPPLE improves the base policy by an arithmetic mean of 4.8 score points, with no auxiliary critic at deployment.
Controlled ablations isolate the benefits of local, stage-aligned credit, and matched-prefix interventions show that critique semantics affect subsequent correction.
Recovery gains concentrate where the prefix contains sufficient diagnostic evidence and the repository state remains reversible within the remaining budget.
highlights: Long-horizon coding agents can observe a failure and generate a plausible critique yet continue along the same incorrect

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Compositional Safety Failures in Harness Evolution: Identification and Runtime Monitoring
papers.summary:
Self-evolving agent harnesses continually update persistent components such as memory, prompts, skills, and tools.
We call this process harness evolution.
However, such evolution could introduce unexpected safety risks.
Existing work studies harness misevolution and validates candidate harnesses or attributed individual component updates, leaving safety analysis of cross-component update interactions largely unexamined.
To address this gap, we study compositional safety failures in harness evolution, where interactions among individually safe and utility-preserving component updates can produce undesirable or unsafe agent behavior, revealing a safety risk intrinsic to harness evolution.
Across three safety-related benchmarks, we identify 43 pairwise and 18 irreducible 3-way compositional safety failures.
Conventional solution incurs combinatorial complexity in validating cross-component interactions, leaving the safety checking impractical as the harness evolves.
To solve this, we introduced a typed hypergraph that represents component states as nodes and safety-relevant higher-order interactions as hyperedges.
When the harness changes, the hypergraph updates only the interaction neighborhood of the changed states rather than reconstructing the global composition space.
Building on that, we develop a hypergraph-guided runtime monitoring mechanism.
Experiments show that our method effectively mitigates compositional safety risks while preserving task utility and reducing interaction-checking costs, and further reveal an empirical safety-utility-cost trade-off across different safety mechanisms.
highlights: Compositional Safety Failures in Harness Evolution
Self-evolving agent harnesses continually update persistent components such as memory, prompts, skills, and tools.

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Beyond Accuracy: Disentangling Decomposition from Typed-State Quality Assurance in Multi-Agent LLM Pipelines
papers.summary:
Multi-agent LLM pipelines are often credited with gains in software engineering tasks, but it is rarely clear whether a gain stems from the typed contract between agents or from the specialized prompts that decomposition enables.
We study this attribution problem in Requirements Engineering, comparing three architectures for classifying requirements as functional or non-functional and then prioritizing them with MoSCoW: a single-call baseline; a two-call variant that reuses the pipeline's specialized prompts but passes an unvalidated intermediate; and a pipeline with a Pydantic-validated typed state.
The 18 conditions cover PROMISE NFR+ (625 requirements), three locally hosted small language models, and two languages.
The F1 gain over the baseline is associated with the two-call, specialized-prompt variant (up to +0.075), whereas the typed state adds a small difference (-0.003 to +0.013) that is significant in one of six comparisons.
Beyond accuracy, the typed pipeline contains out-of-range model outputs at the agent boundary, while the unvalidated variant fails later and drops the requirement, and it shows a small, reproducible increase in inter-model MoSCoW consistency whose cause our design cannot isolate.
The study is associative: the contrasts bundle prompts, call count, and staged context, and the results come from three 7--8B models on one dataset.
The implementation and replication package are archived on Zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23380444).
highlights: The 18 conditions cover PROMISE NFR+ (625 requirements), three locally hosted small language models, and two languages.

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Markovian Generation Chains in Large Language Models
papers.summary:
The widespread use of large language models (LLMs) raises an important question: how do texts evolve when they are repeatedly processed by LLMs?
In this paper, we define this iterative inference process as Markovian generation chains, where each step takes a specific prompt template and the previous output as input, without including any prior data.
In iterative rephrasing and round-trip translation experiments, the output either converges to a small recurrent set or continues to produce novel sentences within a finite horizon.
Through sentence-level Markov chain modeling and analysis of simulated data, we show that iterative process can either increase or reduce the diversity depending on factors such as the temperature parameter and the initial input sentence.
These results offer valuable insights into the dynamics of iterative LLM inference and their implications for multi-agent LLM systems.

These results offer valuable insights into the dynamics of iterative LLM inference and their implications for multi-agen

featuredPapers.title: FlashNext-RL: A System Optimization Study for Long-Horizon Agentic RL of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next

However, the memory requirements and model-specific operators of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next make this difficult with existing open-source implementations. 但是， Qwen3.8-Flash-Next的内存要求和模型特定运算符使得现有的开源实现很难做到这一点。
To resolve these limitations, we introduce FlashNext-RL, a model-specific RL training optimization framework based on prime-rl, with vLLM for software engineering (SWE) rollout generation. 为了解决这些限制，我们引入了FlashNext-RL ，这是一种基于prime-rl的特定模型RL训练优化框架，其中vLLM用于软件工程（ SWE ）推出生成。
Our main focus is BF16 training of the full 48-layer model on a single 8xB200 node, with the first two layers, the n-gram table, the sparse-attention indexer and the multi-token prediction head frozen. 我们的主要重点是在单个8xB200节点上对全48层模型进行BF16训练，前两层即n-gram表、稀疏注意力索引器和多令牌预测头被冻结。

These results highlight the importance of tailoring RL training to the model's architecture, memory layout and kernel requirements, rather than relying only on general-purpose RL infrastructure. 这些结果强调了根据模型的架构、内存布局和内核要求定制RL训练的重要性，而不是仅依赖于通用RL基础设施。

featuredPapers.title: BIRD-RL: Scaling Agentic Reinforcement Learning over Stateful Data-Centric Environments
featuredPapers.authors: Ge Qu, Jinyang Li, Xiaohan Xu
featuredPapers.summary:
While agentic reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as a promising paradigm for training small language models (SLMs), existing frameworks are predominantly tool-centric and struggle with data-centric environments. 虽然代理强化学习（ RL ）已成为训练小型语言模型（ SLM ）的一个有前途的范例，但现有框架主要以工具为中心，并且在以数据为中心的环境中挣扎。
Specifically, applying tool-centric frameworks to stateful tasks like SQL debugging introduces severe spatial inefficiencies since proper environment isolation typically requires a separate database container per rollout. 具体来说，将以工具为中心的框架应用于SQL调试等有状态任务会引入严重的空间效率低下，因为适当的环境隔离通常需要每个部署一个单独的数据库容器。
Naively reusing databases without tracking evolving states across multi-turn interactions causes trajectory contamination and cross-trajectory interference, which severely destabilizes policy updates. 天真地重复使用数据库而不跟踪多回合交互中不断变化的状态会导致轨迹污染和跨轨迹干扰，从而严重破坏政策更新的稳定性。
To overcome these bottlenecks, we introduce BIRD-RL, a novel four-stage agentic RL curriculum that alternately enhances foundational agent reasoning and trajectory-adaptive on-policy exploration to circumvent the instability inherently associated with direct end-to-end learning. 为了克服这些瓶颈，我们引入了BIRD-RL ，这是一种新颖的四阶段代理RL课程，可交替增强基础代理推理和轨迹自适应策略上探索，以规避与直接端到端学习固有的不稳定性。
Crucially, to support this curriculum, BIRD-RL is driven by a Trajectory-scoped Persistent Execution Infrastructure, which enables safe database replica reuse while preserving trajectory isolation. 至关重要的是，为了支持该课程， BIRD-RL由轨迹范围的持久执行基础设施驱动，该基础设施可以实现安全的数据库副本重用，同时保持轨迹隔离。
This design improves spatial RL efficiency by 12.8x, successfully enabling scalable agentic RL for complex data-centric tasks without needs of Kubernettes. 这种设计将空间RL效率提高了12.8倍，成功地为复杂的以数据为中心的任务实现了可扩展的代理RL ，而无需Kubernettes。
Empirical evaluations on the BIRD-CRITIC-SQLite benchmark demonstrate that our 7B and 14B models achieve Success Rates of 44.40% and 48.00%, respectively, showing competitive performance against strong proprietary model-based agents such as Claude-Opus-4.6 Agent (48.20%). 对BIRD-CRITIC-SQLite基准的实证评估表明，我们的7B和14B模型的成功率分别为44.40%和48.00% ，与Claude-Opus-4.6 Agent （ 48.20% ）等强大的基于模型的专有代理相比，表现出竞争力。
Furthermore, BIRD-RL successfully trains unified SLMs capable of both advanced SQL debugging and generation, highlighting its broader potential for multi-objective optimization across heterogeneous, real-world data-centric tasks. 此外， BIRD-RL成功培训了能够进行高级SQL调试和生成的统一SLM ，突出了其在异构、以实际数据为中心的任务中进行多目标优化的更广泛潜力。

featuredPapers.title: Harness Scaling for Generalizable Agentic Reinforcement Learning
featuredPapers.authors: Fei Bai, Huatong Song, Chuan Hao
featuredPapers.summary:
Agent harnesses have become a central component of modern agentic systems, shaping how models use tools, manage context, and coordinate long-horizon interaction. 智能体线束已成为现代智能体系统的核心组成部分，塑造了模型使用工具、管理上下文和协调长距离交互的方式。
Realizing the benefits of these harnesses depends on how effectively the underlying model can make use of them, motivating reinforcement learning directly through the harness. 实现这些线束的好处取决于底层模型如何有效地利用它们，直接通过线束激励强化学习。
However, existing approaches typically train through a single fixed harness, which can lead to specialization and limited transfer across harness configurations. 然而，现有方法通常通过单个固定线束进行训练，这可能导致线束配置的专业化和有限的转移。
To address this, we introduce \textbf{Harness Scaling}, a new scaling dimension for agentic RL that extends training from a single harness to diverse execution configurations. 为了解决这个问题，我们引入了\ textbf {线束缩放} ，这是代理RL的新缩放维度，将训练从单个线束扩展到不同的执行配置。
Concretely, we construct a factorized harness space, select a compact training subset with balanced factorial coverage, and organize cross-harness training to combine global coverage with controlled variation for the same task. 具体来说，我们构建了一个分解的线束空间，选择了一个具有平衡分解覆盖率的紧凑训练子集，并组织了交叉训练，将全局覆盖率与同一任务的受控变化相结合。
Across multiple benchmarks, model scales, and RL algorithms, Harness Scaling consistently improves generalization to unseen white-box configurations. 在多个基准、模型缩放和RL算法中，线束缩放始终如一地改进了对看不见的白盒配置的泛化。
Moreover, models trained through structured white-box variation transfer effectively to unseen external black-box harnesses, outperforming models trained through a single complex black-box harness. 此外，通过结构化白盒变异训练的模型有效地转移到看不见的外部黑盒线束，优于通过单个复杂的黑盒线束训练的模型。
These results establish harness diversity as a meaningful scaling dimension for agentic RL and highlight the importance of how this diversity is organized for cross-harness generalization. 这些结果确立了线束多样性作为代理RL的一个有意义的缩放维度，并强调了如何组织这种多样性以进行交叉线束泛化的重要性。

featuredPapers.title: Recursive Self-Improvement on a Budget: Scoring Code Edits Before They Run
featuredPapers.authors: Erfan Darzi, Sree Bhargavi Balija, Sheng He
featuredPapers.summary:
A coding agent that rewrites its own scaffold has to choose which proposed edit to expand before that edit has been evaluated, and the search then has to return one agent. 重写自己脚手架的编码代理必须在评估编辑之前选择要扩展的拟议编辑，然后搜索必须返回一个代理。
Each run fits one linear readout on the parent's steering-split solve rate and eight coordinates of the proposed diff, from 96 scaffold edits labeled by four evaluations of a 16-instance fit split, and then freezes the coefficients. 每次运行拟合父级转向拆分求解率的一个线性读数和提议的diff的八个坐标，从由16实例拟合拆分的四个评估标记的96个脚手架编辑中，然后冻结系数。
HumanEval+ reserves 48 instances as the steering split and Polyglot reserves 64. HumanEval +保留48个实例作为转向拆分和Polyglot保留64。
That split scores parents and keeps an archive of four nodes. 该拆分对父节点进行评分，并保留四个节点的存档。
Huxley-G\"odel Machine selection draws a parent by Thompson sampling on the steering counts of nodes that have already been evaluated, and it expands the child that parent proposes. Huxley-G\ "odel Machine选择在已经评估的节点的转向计数上绘制Thompson采样的父节点，并扩展父节点提出的子节点。
Every method then returns the earliest evaluated node whose steering-split solve count is maximal. 然后，每个方法返回其steering-split求解计数最大的最早计算节点。
The tables report the held-out score of that node on the other 100 HumanEval+ instances and the other 145 Polyglot instances, next to the root scaffold and the calibration edit with the highest fit-split label. 这些表格报告了该节点在其他100个HumanEval +实例和其他145个Polyglot实例上的保留分数，仅次于根支架和具有最高拟合拆分标签的校准编辑。
Twelve runs of GPT-4o return a node at 87.0% on held-out HumanEval+, against 84.2% for the parent-rate ablation. 在保留的HumanEval +中， 12次GPT-4o检测以87.0%的速度返回一个淋巴结，而父速率消融为84.2%。
On that split Huxley-G\"odel Machine selection returns 85.1%, the root is at 81.2%, and the calibration-best edit is at 82.8%. 在该分割Huxley-G\ "odel Machine选择上，返回85.1 ％ ，根为81.2 ％ ，校准最佳编辑为82.8 ％。
On the same split Claude Sonnet 4.5 returns 86.6%, beside 86.5% for Huxley-G\"odel Machine selection, 85.3% for the parent-rate ablation, and 85.1% for the calibration-best edit. 在同一分割上， Claude Sonnet 4.5返回86.6% ， Huxley-G\ "odel Machine选择返回86.5% ，父速率消融返回85.3% ，校准最佳编辑返回85.1%。
highlights: HumanEval+ reserves 48 instances as the steering split and Polyglot reserves 64.

featuredPapers.title: VeriEvolve: Evaluator-First Evolution for Tool-Using Agents
featuredPapers.authors: Yueshen Li, Kamer Ali Yuksel, Gokhan Tur
featuredPapers.summary:
A central obstacle to self-improving agents is the absence of a reliable fitness signal for realistic stateful tasks. 自我提升智能体的一个主要障碍是缺乏可靠的适应性信号，无法完成逼真的状态化任务。
We introduce \textsc{VeriEvolve}, an evaluator-first evolution framework that constructs this missing evaluation layer before optimizing the agent. 我们引入了\ textsc {VeriEvolve} ，这是一个评估者优先的演化框架，在优化代理之前构建了这个缺失的评估层。
From task instruction, VeriEvolve synthesizes instruction-grounded challenge states and an executable evaluator that checks them. 根据任务指令， VeriEvolve合成基于指令的质询状态和检查它们的可执行评估器。
During each round of workflow evolution, the evaluator is frozen and serves as the fitness signal. 在每轮工作流程演进过程中，评估者都会被冻结，并充当健康信号。
Between rounds, VeriEvolve revises the evaluator by converting the end states of strong and weak runs into a pair of counterfactual test cases. 在两轮之间， VeriEvolve通过将强运行和弱运行的结束状态转换为一对反事实测试用例来修改评估者。
Across all 30 MCPMark Filesystem tasks, VeriEvolve constructs 30 evaluators with 141 challenge states, achieving 141/141 agreement on the generated suites and 113/122 agreement on held-out states produced by executor agents. 在所有30个MCPMark文件系统任务中， VeriEvolve构建了30个具有141个挑战状态的评估器，就生成的套件达成了141/141协议，并就执行代理产生的保留状态达成了113/122协议。
Evaluator-guided evolution increases externally verified success from 6/30 to 18/30 for GLM-5.2 and from 27/30 to 30/30 for Claude; refinement removes all three false positives that the weak executor exposes. 评估者指导的进化将GLM-5.2的外部验证成功率从6/30提高到18/30 ， Claude从27/30提高到30/30 ；细化消除了弱执行者暴露的所有三个误报。
Cross-environment studies on PostgreSQL, Playwright, Notion, and GitHub further expose complementary limits from observability, state representation, and search/execution capacity. PostgreSQL、Playwright、Notion和GitHub的跨环境研究进一步揭示了可观察性、状态表示和搜索/执行能力的互补限制。
These results show that executable evaluators can be synthesized and used to guide search when task success is observable and an external verifier is available for calibration. 这些结果表明，当任务成功可观察且外部验证器可用于校准时，可以合成可执行评估器并用于指导搜索。
highlights: first evolution framework that constructs this missing evaluation layer before optimizing the agent
