papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Trackable Skill Library Lifecycle Management for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary:
Skill-augmented agentic RL has emerged as an effective approach to improving LLM agents on long-horizon tasks. 技能增强型代理强化学习已成为改进长期任务LLM代理的有效方法。
Despite this progress, individual skills may follow distinct trajectories as the policy evolves, with some becoming redundant after the model internalizes their capabilities, others remaining valuable as external scaffolding, and still others turning harmful. 尽管取得了这一进展，但随着政策的演变，个人技能可能会遵循不同的轨迹，其中一些技能在模型内化其能力后变得多余，另一些技能作为外部支架仍然具有价值，还有一些技能变得有害。
However, existing skill library systems fail to identify each skill's true contribution due to free-riding among co-retrieved skills, difficulty confounding across tasks, and the absence of skill-specific counterfactual evidence, which prevents reliable skill lifecycle management. 然而，现有的技能库系统由于在共同检索的技能之间搭便车、难以混淆任务以及缺乏特定技能的反事实证据而无法识别每项技能的真正贡献，这阻碍了可靠的技能生命周期管理。
We propose TrackRL, an agentic RL framework where skill tracking drives skill library full lifecycle management. 我们提出了TrackRL ，这是一个代理式RL框架，其中技能跟踪驱动技能库的整个生命周期管理。
Specifically, within each GRPO group, we turn grouped sampling into online randomized controlled experiments. 具体而言，在每个GRPO组中，我们将分组抽样转化为在线随机对照实验。
Independent random injection and within-group contrasts on the same task isolate each skill's true contribution, and reliability-weighted aggregation accumulates evidence across groups. 同一任务的独立随机注射和组内对比隔离了每项技能的真正贡献，可靠性加权聚合积累了跨组证据。
As evidence accumulates, we continuously track skill utility, which measures the skill's causal contribution as external scaffolding, and model mastery, which reflects how far the corresponding capability has been internalized. 随着证据的积累，我们不断跟踪技能效用，将技能的因果关系作为外部支架来衡量，以及模型掌握，这反映了相应能力的内化程度。
Along this line, we formulate skill lifecycle management as an evidence-gated state-transition process that governs each skill from generation and admission through protected incubation to retention, retirement, or removal, while a soft capacity bound controls library growth. 沿着这一思路，我们将技能生命周期管理制定为一个循证门控的状态转换过程，从生成和录取到受保护的孵化到保留、退休或移除，管理每个技能，而软容量绑定控制库增长。
Experiments show that TrackRL outperforms recent skill-augmented RL baselines in both library-assisted and skill-free evaluation, with further analyses revealing how skill value shifts during policy learning and how evidence-driven state transitions shape skill library evolution. 实验表明， TrackRL在图书馆辅助和无技能评估方面都优于最近的技能增强RL基线，进一步分析揭示了政策学习过程中技能价值的转变以及循证驱动的状态转变如何影响技能库的演变。
Our code is available at https://github.com/xizhu1022/TrackRL. 我们的代码可在https://github.com/xizhu1022/TrackRL上找到。
highlights: outperforms recent skill-augmented RL baselines in both library-assisted and skill-free evaluation
Skill-augmented agentic RL has emerged as an effective approach to improving LLM agents on long-horizon tasks.

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: IDEAgent: Agentic Quality-Diversity Search for Research Idea Generation
papers.summary:
Large Language Models (LLMs) have significantly advanced the automation of scientific discovery. 大型语言模型（ LLM ）大大推进了科学发现的自动化。
However, existing systems share a core limitation: they optimize ideas independently for either Quality or Diversity. 然而，现有的系统有一个核心限制：它们独立地优化创意，以实现质量或多样性。
This often results in closely related ideas or large sets of trivial, unsound, or unclear concepts. 这通常会导致密切相关的想法或大量琐碎、不健全或不清楚的概念。
We instead argue that research ideation should be framed as a conjunction of Quality and Diversity objectives, i.e., a Quality-Diversity (QD) search. 相反，我们认为研究理念应被视为质量和多样性目标的结合，即质量-多样性（ QD ）搜索。
Accordingly, we introduce IDEAgent, a multi-agent framework that tracks idea evolution through lineages. 因此，我们引入了IDEAgent ，这是一个通过谱系跟踪创意演变的多智能体框架。
We jointly drive Quality using multi-objective feedback for repair and refinement, while Diversity is achieved through lightweight sequential memory and explicit comparison against completed ideas, historical variants, and rejected proposals. 我们使用多目标反馈进行维修和改进，共同推动质量，而多元化则通过轻量级顺序记忆以及与已完成的想法、历史变体和被拒绝的提案的明确比较来实现。
To evaluate this joint objective, we develop Yield, a metric that computes the largest mutually diverse set of ideas satisfying predefined quality thresholds. 为了评估这一共同目标，我们开发了收益率指标，该指标计算了满足预定义质量阈值的最大的相互多样化的想法集。
Across 32 topics spanning 8 CS domains, IDEAgent outperforms the best baseline by 3.89x on Yield, while achieving Yield of at least 2 on 8x as many topics. 在横跨8个CS域的32个主题中， IDEAgent在Yield上的表现优于最佳基线3.89倍，而在8倍的主题上实现了至少2倍的Yield。
We further analyze quality improvements, showing that repair and refinement improve logical rigor and clarity while preserving non-obviousness. 我们进一步分析质量改进，表明维修和改进可以提高逻辑严谨性和清晰度，同时保持非显而易见性。
Lastly, we extend IDEAgent to two algorithm discovery tasks for verifiable quality judgment and find that it still consistently outperforms all baselines, and yields the largest set of high-quality and diverse programs that beat a trivial/standard baseline. 最后，我们将IDEAgent扩展到两个算法发现任务，以实现可验证的质量判断，并发现它仍然始终如一地优于所有基线，并产生了超过琐碎/标准基线的最大一组高质量和多样化的程序。
To encourage future research on QD-search-based ideation, we open-source IDEAgent at https://github.com/declare-lab/IDEAgent. 为了鼓励未来对基于QD搜索的构思的研究，我们在https://github.com/declare-lab/IDEAgent上开源了IDEAgent。

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: RaspAssistant as an Agentic Framework for Automating Adsorption Simulation Research in Porous Materials
papers.summary:
Porous-material adsorption studies require coordinated structure preparation, force-field selection, simulation, validation, and interpretation, making end-to-end automation difficult. 多孔材料吸附研究需要协调的结构制备、力场选择、模拟、验证和解释，这使得端到端的自动化变得困难。
We test whether RaspAssistant, a hierarchical multi-agent framework, can carry an adsorption study from force-field preparation through validation and downstream separation analysis. 我们测试分层多药剂框架RaspAssistant是否可以通过验证和下游分离分析从力场准备进行吸附研究。
Across twelve multi-agent workflow-reproduction runs spanning four adsorption and separation benchmarks, overall scores ranged from 8.50 to 10.00 on a rubric evaluating workflow correctness, simulation validity, and analysis consistency. 在跨越四个吸附和分离基准的十二个多药剂工作流程再生产运行中，在评估工作流正确性、模拟有效性和分析一致性的标题上，总分从8.50到10.00不等。
In a separate eight-case force-field extraction benchmark, the mean weighted score was 0.967, combining parameter agreement and RASPA readiness. 在单独的八例力场提取基准中，平均加权分数为0.967 ，结合了参数一致性和RASPA就绪性。
In open-ended studies, the system diagnosed and refined an acetylene force field and, after validating a CO$_2$ force field against MFI experiments, screened 197 pure-silica zeolites that passed automated input checks. 在开放式研究中，该系统诊断并改进了乙炔力场，并在对照MFI实验验证了CO $_2 $力场后，筛选了197个通过自动输入检查的纯二氧化硅沸石。
These results demonstrate autonomous workflow execution after task specification and input provision: RaspAssistant coordinates, validates, adapts, and documents extended adsorption-simulation workflows while exposing model sensitivity and methodological limitations for expert review. 这些结果展示了任务规范和输入供应后的自主工作流程执行： RaspAssistant坐标、验证、调整和记录扩展的吸附模拟工作流程，同时暴露了模型灵敏度和方法限制，供专家审查。

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: RSI Control: Can AI Models Perform Covert Sabotage in the Self-Improvement Process?
papers.summary:
Recursive self-improvement, in which frontier AI models work on training the next generation, is quickly becoming a reality. 递归自我提升正在迅速成为现实，在这种自我提升中，前沿人工智能模型致力于培训下一代。
However, the safety of this process has received far less attention than it should. 然而，这一过程的安全性却远没有得到应有的重视。
A misaligned model training its successor can shape what that successor knows, how it behaves, and what it wants, and the harm carries forward into the next generation. 一个不对齐的模型训练其继任者可以塑造继任者所知道的，它的行为方式，以及它想要的，并且危害会延续到下一代。
We study this risk through the lens of AI control. 我们通过人工智能控制的镜头来研究这种风险。
We introduce RSI Control Arena, a testbed in which a frontier model, acting as an autonomous R\&D agent, is given a benign main task from a stage of a successor model's training pipeline together with a covert side task to install a misaligned property in the successor. 我们引入了RSI Control Arena ，这是一个测试平台，其中作为自主研发代理的前沿模型从后续模型的训练管道阶段被赋予良性主要任务，以及在后续模型中安装未对齐属性的隐蔽侧任务。
The testbed contains 16 side tasks in three classes, forming 22 task pairs with main tasks that span the pipeline from data curation to reinforcement learning. 测试平台包含三个类别的16个副任务，形成22个任务对，主要任务跨越从数据管理到强化学习的管道。
We evaluate six frontier models as agents against LLM monitors that read the transcript of the run and the agent's reasoning. 我们评估了六个前沿模型，作为LLM监查员的代理，这些监查员阅读了运行的成绩单和代理的推理。
We observe that every model completes a substantial share of the side tasks without degrading the main-task performance, including side tasks that make the successor itself a better saboteur. 我们观察到，每个模型都完成了大部分的辅助任务，而不会降低主任务性能，包括使继任者本身成为更好的破坏者的辅助任务。
Under minimal instructions to stay covert, models already produce successful attacks that monitors fail to detect, and providing a short list of evasion tactics further reduces the detection rate. 在最低限度的隐蔽指令下，模型已经产生了监测器无法检测到的成功攻击，并且提供简短的逃避策略列表进一步降低了检测率。
Monitors with access to agent's reasoning detects most attacks, but not all. 具有代理推理访问权限的监视器检测到大多数攻击，但不是全部。
Our results indicate that recursive self-improvement raises significant safety concerns, and that strong safety effort should be in place before models are trusted with greater responsibility of training their successors. 我们的研究结果表明，递归自我改进引发了重大的安全问题，在模型被信任承担更大责任培训其继任者之前，应该采取强有力的安全措施。
highlights: Recursive self-improvement, in which frontier AI models work on training the next generation, is quickly becoming a real

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: MaD-RSI: Model-as-Data for Recursive Self-Improvement of Agent Harnesses
papers.summary:
Recursive self-improvement (RSI) of agent harnesses has emerged as an effective approach to enhancing the capabilities of large language model (LLM) agents. 代理利用的递归自我改进（ RSI ）已成为增强大型语言模型（ LLM ）代理能力的有效方法。
By searching the harness space for a specific LLM on a given dataset, RSI can discover a harness tailored to the capabilities and behavioral characteristics of that model. 通过在给定数据集上搜索特定LLM的线束空间， RSI可以发现根据该模型的能力和行为特征量身定制的线束。
However, such optimization often creates a strong coupling between the learned harness and its target LLM, limiting generalization across models and requiring substantial computational resources to adapt to new LLMs. 然而，这种优化通常会在学习的线束及其目标LLM之间产生强大的耦合，限制了模型之间的泛化，并需要大量的计算资源来适应新的LLM。
Moreover, existing RSI methods typically optimize a harness using feedback from a single model and evaluate its generalization to other models only after training. 此外，现有的RSI方法通常使用来自单个模型的反馈来优化线束，并且仅在训练后才评估其对其他模型的泛化。
This paradigm treats model differences primarily as a criterion for evaluating generalization rather than as valuable evidence for optimization. 这种范式将模型差异主要视为评估概括的标准，而不是优化的有价值证据。
In this paper, we introduce a new perspective that treats models as data and places the harness at the center of optimization. 在本文中，我们引入了一个新的视角，将模型视为数据，并将线束置于优化的中心。
Building on this perspective, we propose \textsc{MaD-RSI}, a framework that directly optimizes a shared harness across multiple heterogeneous LLMs by incorporating their diverse failure trajectories into the training process. 基于这一观点，我们提出了\ textsc {MaD-RSI} ，这是一个框架，通过将不同的失败轨迹纳入培训过程，直接优化多个异构LLM的共享线束。
Rather than assessing model differences only after optimization, \textsc{MaD-RSI} leverages these differences as training evidence to guide the self-improvement of a shared harness. 与其仅在优化后评估模型差异，\ textsc {MaD-RSI}利用这些差异作为训练证据来指导共享线束的自我改进。
Furthermore, we introduce a new evaluation framework with two complementary metrics designed to assess the effectiveness of harness optimization across models. 此外，我们引入了一个新的评估框架，其中包含两个互补的指标，旨在评估跨模型的线束优化的有效性。
Experiments across multiple datasets and LLMs demonstrate that \textsc{MaD-RSI} improves generalization over existing approaches while reducing training costs. 跨多个数据集和LLM的实验表明，\ textsc {MaD-RSI}改进了现有方法的泛化，同时降低了培训成本。

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: KernelClaw: A Multi-Agent Framework for GPU Kernel Optimization with Dual-Memory Mechanisms
papers.summary:
Improving GPU kernel efficiency is crucial for efficient AI systems. 提高GPU内核效率对于高效的人工智能系统至关重要。
Recent work has explored leveraging large language models (LLMs) for GPU kernel generation and optimization. 最近的工作探索了利用大型语言模型（ LLM ）进行GPU内核生成和优化的方法。
However, existing LLM-based kernel optimization pipelines typically rely on opaque, implicitly learned heuristics within the LLMs to determine optimization strategies. 然而，现有的基于LLM的内核优化流水线通常依赖于LLM中的不透明、隐式学习的启发式算法来确定优化策略。
This leads to inefficient trial-and-error and weakly interpretable optimizations. 这导致低效的试错和弱可解释的优化。
Our key insight is to replace implicit heuristics with expert optimization knowledge that is aware of task trajectories. 我们的关键见解是用了解任务轨迹的专家优化知识取代隐式启发式方法。
Specifically, we present KernelClaw, a multi-agent framework with a dual-level memory architecture. 具体来说，我们提出了KernelClaw ，这是一个具有双层内存架构的多代理框架。
KernelClaw operates by coordinating agents with long-term memory of reusable expert knowledge and short-term memory to prevent repetitive backtracking. KernelClaw通过协调具有可重复使用的专业知识和短期记忆的长期记忆的代理来防止重复回溯。
On KernelBench Levels 1-3, KernelClaw achieves a 100% success rate and average speedups of 6.98x, 7.89x, and 1.94x over Torch Eager on Levels 1, 2, and 3, respectively, outperforming prior baselines. 在KernelBench级别1-3上， KernelClaw在级别1、2和3上分别比Torch Eager取得了100%的成功率和6.98倍、7.89倍和1.94倍的平均加速，优于先前的基线。
Code is available at https://github.com/0satan0/KernelMem/. 优惠码可在https://github.com/0satan0/KernelMem/上获得。

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Beyond Trajectory Statistics: Community-Consistent Human Mobility Generation via Evolving User-Location Graphs
papers.summary:
Human mobility data are fundamental to Web-based location services and broader urban applications, and mobility generation provides synthetic trajectories when real data are costly or inaccessible. 人类移动数据是基于网络的位置服务和更广泛的城市应用的基础，当真实数据昂贵或无法访问时，移动性生成提供了合成轨迹。
Although recent mobility generators have incorporated collective mobility patterns, they primarily focus on individual trajectories and aggregate population dynamics, leaving evolving community structures formed by user-location interactions insufficiently modeled. 尽管最近的流动性生成器已纳入集体流动性模式，但它们主要关注个人轨迹和总人口动态，使得由用户位置交互形成的不断演变的社区结构未得到充分建模。
In this paper, we study community-consistent human mobility generation. 在本文中，我们研究了社区一致的人类流动生成。
To this end, we formulate mobility generation as the generation of dynamic user-location graphs to model community structures and propose MOTION, a Multi-agent framework for cOmmuniTy-consIstent human mObility geNeration. 为此，我们将移动性生成公式化为动态用户位置图的生成，以建模社区结构并提出运动，这是cOmmuniTy-consIstent人类移动性geNeration的多智能体框架。
MOTION consists of user agents, location agents, and a global manager agent. MOTION由用户代理、位置代理和全球经理代理组成。
MOTION first detects coherent communities from historical mobility using the Leiden algorithm and extracts community-conditioned interaction priors to guide the generation process. MOTION首先使用Leiden算法从历史流动性中检测相干社区，并提取社区条件交互先验以指导生成过程。
Guided by these priors, the user agents plan mobility, search destination candidates, and infer user movements from the individual view. 在这些先验的指导下，用户代理规划移动性，搜索目标候选者，并从个人视图推断用户移动。
In parallel, selectively activated location agents infer likely user arrivals from the community view. 同时，选择性激活的位置代理从社区视图推断可能的用户到达。
The manager coordinates both views, diagnoses interactions causing deviations, and attributes targeted reflection signals to revise user decisions, location attraction, and source-user selection. 经理协调两种视图，诊断导致偏差的交互，并归因于有针对性的反射信号，以修改用户决策、位置吸引力和源用户选择。
Experiments on two real-world datasets show that MOTION outperforms baselines by at least 4.05% across reported metrics of individual trajectories, population and flow distributions, and community and graph structures. 在两个真实世界数据集上的实验表明，在单个轨迹、人口和流量分布以及社区和图形结构的报告指标中，运动的表现至少比基线高4.05%。
Further analyses confirm its robustness, privacy preservation, and downstream utility. 进一步的分析证实了其稳健性、隐私保护和下游实用性。
The code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/MOTION-04C4. 该代码可在https://anonymous.4open.science/r/MOTION-04C4上获得。

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Memory as Belief: Bayesian Evolution of Memory for Self-Evolving LLM Agents
papers.summary:
Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly rely on external memory to accumulate past experiences for continual adaptation. 大型语言模型（ LLM ）代理越来越依赖外部记忆来积累过去的经验，以进行持续的适应。
However, effectively reusing memory requires accurately assessing its value, as retrieved experiences may become unreliable when transferred across task contexts. 然而，有效重用内存需要准确评估其价值，因为当跨任务上下文传输时，检索到的体验可能变得不可靠。
Despite its importance, memory valuation remains largely underexplored, with existing methods relying on historical retrieval success rates that overlook the context dependency of memory usefulness and the varying reliability of estimates under different amounts of evidence.
Inspired by the Bayesian brain hypothesis, we propose BEAM (Bayesian-style Evolutionary Agentic Memory), a framework that reformulates memory value evaluation as a parameterized cognitive inference process, where memory value is represented as a context-conditioned dynamic belief rather than a passive historical statistic.
Specifically, BEAM infers memory value beliefs from current task contexts and continuously calibrates them using execution feedback as empirical evidence, transforming memory from passive storage into an adaptive cognitive mechanism for continual self-evolution.
Extensive experiments across reasoning and code generation benchmarks demonstrate that BEAM consistently improves memory utilization and enables continual self-evolution of LLM agents.
highlights: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly rely on external memory to accumulate past experiences for continual adap

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: How Data Scales in Agentic Reinforcement Learning: Laws and Synthesis Strategies
papers.summary:
Pretraining scaling laws treat training data as a one-dimensional quantity: a token count.
Agentic reinforcement learning (RL) inherits this scalar abstraction, but modern synthesis pipelines now generate \textit{tasks}, \textit{environments}, and \textit{trajectories} independently and at very different costs, turning data into a structured design space.
This raises a question pretraining never had to answer: given a synthesis budget, \textit{which axis} should be scaled?
We address this question end-to-end with three tightly coupled contributions.
First, we decompose agentic data into three cardinality axes (task, environment, trajectory), plus a reward-density control variable, and fit per-axis scaling relations on different large language models (LLMs) across math+code, SWE, web, and UI/tool application domains.
Across all model sizes, model families, domains, and RL algorithms (PPO and GRPO) we measured, the scaling exponents order as environment $>$ task $>$ trajectory.
When environment diversity is decomposed into world and environment-structure diversity, its advantage is mainly driven by the former, while the latter is just comparable to the task diversity.
Second, we use the fitted laws as a common ruler to price synthesis methods, capturing each method's efficiency as a per-axis discount factor and identifying critical synthetic-to-real ratios at which collapse begins; these ratios differ by an order of magnitude across axes.
Third, we cast budget allocation as a constrained optimization under our laws and discounts, deriving a Chinchilla-style compute-optimal recipe and validating it at held-out scale.
The empirical results demonstrate that following the recipe yields up to $1.7\times$ compute efficiency over the dominant ``scale-the-trajectories'' practice.
highlights: How Data Scales in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
Pretraining scaling laws treat training data as a one-dimensional quantity: a token count.

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Auto-Director: Leveraging Multi-Agent Collaboration for Autonomous Video Editing
papers.summary:
Autonomous video editing from open-world resources remains a challenging problem in multimedia content creation.
Retrieval-based methods are constrained by fixed source material and lack creative flexibility, while generative models struggle with long-horizon coherence and often diverge from user intent.
Both paradigms fail to replicate the structured, multi-stage reasoning that underlies professional post-production.
To address these limitations, we present Auto-Director, a tool-augmented multi-agent framework that mirrors professional editorial workflows: a Planning Agent decomposes abstract topics into fact-grounded scripts via retrieval-augmented planning; a Material Agent indexes open-world footage through shot segmentation and visual tagging; an Editor Agent assembles semantically aligned clips with MLLM-driven spatial adaptation; and a Critic Agent governs an iterative Reflect-and-Revise loop that checks scene-level alignment and pacing.
To rigorously evaluate this new paradigm, we introduce VEdit-Bench, a benchmark of 100 expert-curated topics with human-annotated Golden Scripts and a five-dimensional metric suite covering Narrative Logic, Factual Accuracy, Semantic Alignment, Compositional Quality, and Stylistic Cohesion.
Extensive experiments demonstrate that Auto-Director significantly outperforms baseline methods in both automated metrics and human evaluation, effectively bridging the gap between amateurs and professional-grade video production.
highlights: outperforms baseline methods in both automated metrics and human evaluation

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Conjugate Compilation: Self-Improving Agentic Co-Compilation for Speculative Decoding
papers.summary:
As LLM adoption surges, scaling model serving requires unlocking stranded GPU capacity alongside deploying more GPUs.
Speculative decoding brings two models into the serving process: a small draft model proposes tokens that a larger target model verifies.
Yet compiling these models individually leaves their shared execution outside the compiler's optimization boundary.
We introduce CONJUGATE COMPILATION, which reframes speculative decoding as a cross-model compilation problem and jointly optimizes the draft and target models within their shared execution rather than treating each in isolation.
Our key insight is that cross-model compilation should be informed by the measured performance of the co-located shared execution it produces: an optimization that improves a kernel in isolation need not improve the models when they execute together.
To expand cross-model opportunities, we devise operand layouts that interleave blocks from both models within common tiles, co-locating GEMM and non-GEMM work while preserving their mathematics.
We realize CONJUGATE COMPILATION through a self-improving agentic search system in which an LLM edits cross-model optimization plans using the compiler and GPU execution as its environment.
Each proposed plan is compiled and evaluated through its co-located shared execution, whose measured score, together with kernel-level verdicts and compiler feedback, informs subsequent proposals, while Monte Carlo tree search accumulates rewards to guide exploration.
Across six single-GPU speculative-decoding configurations on NVIDIA B300 and RTX 5090 GPUs, CONJUGATE COMPILATION achieves a geometric-mean per-round speedup of 1.37x over conventional execution.
Interleaved kernels raise this speedup to 1.45x, reaching 1.59x in the best case.
CONJUGATE COMPILATION also improves GPU utilization on average by 1.46x on RTX 5090 and 1.50x on B300.
highlights: As LLM adoption surges, scaling model serving requires unlocking stranded GPU capacity alongside deploying more GPUs.

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: COMPASS: Routing via Capability-Oriented Model Profiling with Adaptive Search, Selection, and Tool Use
papers.summary:
LLM routing aims to select a capable model at low cost, but specialized routers can require updates as models and tasks change.
We propose COMPASS, an agentic router in which an LLM follows a routing recipe, gathers performance and cost evidence through tools, and optionally inspects candidate answers before selecting a model.
Our evaluations on LLMRouterBench and DeepSWE show that agentic routing can improve accuracy and lower model-call cost relative to specialized and trained routing baselines, without routing-specific training.
On LLMRouterBench, COMPASS reaches 69.85% accuracy at \$139.57, compared with RLCascadeRouter's 69.14% at \$180.22.
On DeepSWE under fixed five-fold cross-validation, it reaches 78.1% at \$215, compared with 74.1% at \$500 for the best single model.
COMPASS also supports routing across benchmarks and adapts to an expanded model pool by reading new evaluation records, without changing the router's weights or prompt.

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: OptScientist: Automated Discovery of Optimization Laws
papers.summary:
Many scientific phenomena are best understood as outcomes of underlying optimization problems, yet automated scientific discovery has largely focused on recovering equations that describe observed input-output patterns.
We introduce OptScientist, a novel automated framework for discovering compact symbolic optimization laws directly from data.
OptScientist comprises (i) a model that infers symbolic optimization problems by first learning to represent data as an optimization problem and then extracting its symbolic form, and (ii) an LLM agentic system embedding the model in a discovery process that integrates theoretical priors from scientific literature, discovers candidate laws, abstracts their underlying mechanisms, and suggests new data to collect.
We first evaluate OptScientist on OptFeynman, a novel benchmark of 99 physics-derived optimization problems, where OptScientist recovers ground-truth laws for over 80% of the problems and remains robust to noisy contextual information, while substantially outperforming machine-learning, symbolic, and LLM-based model-discovery baselines.
On human risky choice and central-bank monetary policy, OptScientist discovers compact symbolic optimization laws that achieve held-out predictive performance competitive with leading baselines, while using few parameters and substantially fewer tokens than LLM baselines.
Overall, OptScientist extends automated scientific discovery to uncovering optimization laws that generate observed phenomena, enabling automated theory building across the physical, biological, behavioral, and social sciences.
highlights: first learning to represent data as an optimization problem and then extracting its symbolic form

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: RELAY: Scaling Historical Build Restoration through Rule Reuse and Agentic Repair
papers.summary:
Vulnerability benchmarks and software engineering research depend on rebuilding historical software.
Yet builds rely on external resources, such as base images and packages, that change independently of the source code.
In this study, we examine this environment decay on 14,159 OSS-Fuzz cases.
We find that 69.7% no longer complete reconstruction and verification, and that most failures share a small number of recurring failure symptoms.
A recurring failure can therefore be diagnosed once and its repair reused.
We present Relay, a hybrid framework that uses an LLM to derive and validate deterministic repair rules from representative failures, reuses them without model calls, and escalates cases unresolved by rules to a per-case agent.
We evaluate Relay in human-guided and fully automated rule-derivation campaigns and compare it with a per-case agent approach.
We find that rule derivation can be fully automated, and that reusable rules restore as many builds as per-case agents with fewer build executions.
However, agents restore cases that the rules cannot.
Our results show that a hybrid approach that applies rules first and escalates the remaining cases to an agent restores more builds than either approach alone and at a lower cost than using agents alone.
highlights: first and escalates the remaining cases to an agent restores more builds than either approach alone and at a lower cost

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: VibeTraining-Bench: Data-Trainer-Harness Co-Design for Iterative System Improvement
papers.summary:
Recursive self-improvement (RSI) requires agents to diagnose system bottlenecks and coordinate improvements across training and inference.
We refer to the agents' capability to jointly optimize training data, the trainer, and the inference harness as cross-component co-design.
We introduce VibeTraining-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating this capability across tasks spanning terminal operation, software engineering, multi-turn tool use, and mathematical reasoning.
Within each task, research agents start from an identical initial agent system under a fixed resource budget.
Guided by validation feedback, they iteratively refine data, trainers, and inference harnesses, then select and submit a final agent system for evaluation on the test set.
To prevent reward hacking, we enforce three safeguards: test data isolation, separate research and grading containers, and network restrictions for research agents.
Our evaluation results show that frontier research agents substantially improve target agent systems.
For example, on SWE-bench Verified, GPT-6-Astra raises the target agent system's performance from 32.9% to 53.7%, comparable to the human-developed instruct model's 55.4%.
However, there is still room to improve their ability to co-design and iteratively refine data, trainer, and harness to achieve cumulative performance gains.
We hope that VibeTraining-Bench will serve as a unified platform for advancing RSI, deepening our understanding of cross-component optimization for agent systems.
Code and data are available at https://github.com/D2I-ai/VibeTraining-Bench.
highlights: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) requires agents to diagnose system bottlenecks and coordinate improvements across train

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Differentiable Mixture-of-Agents Incentivizes Swarm Intelligence of Large Language Models
papers.summary:
Recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) have catalyzed the development of multi-agent systems (MAS) for complex reasoning tasks.
However, existing MAS typically rely on pre-defined or pre-compiled communication topologies, which limits their flexibility and adaptability to dynamic task requirements.
In this work, we propose Differentiable Mixture-of-Agents (DMoA), a self-evolving multi-agent framework that enables elastic and adaptive agent collaboration during inference.
Instead of statically constructing workflows, DMoA dynamically routes and activates agents at each reasoning step, allowing the system to implicitly simulate diverse communication topologies and adapt to evolving demands.
To achieve this, we design a differentiable, context-aware routing mechanism that leverages recurrent structures to incorporate historical and contextual information, producing sparse agent activations in a step-wise manner.
Furthermore, we introduce predictive entropy as self-supervised signals to optimize the routing process, enabling efficient test-time adaptation without external annotations.
Extensive experiments across 9 benchmarks demonstrate that DMoA achieves state-of-the-art performance while exhibiting strong efficiency, robustness, and ensembling capabilities.

featuredPapers.title: BlenderWorld: Benchmarking Visual Agents for 3D Creation from Real-World References
featuredPapers.authors: Xinyu Fang, Yuchi Wang, Weihao Yu
featuredPapers.summary:
Recent advances in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have enabled them to act as autonomous agents, creating and editing 3D models via code or direct software manipulation. 多模态大型语言模型（ MLLM ）的最新进展使它们能够充当自主代理，通过代码或直接软件操作创建和编辑3D模型。
In practical workflows, these models must infer object shapes, materials, spatial layouts, and lighting from diverse references while strictly following instructions to reconstruct, modify, or design 3D content. 在实际工作流程中，这些模型必须从不同的参考中推断出对象形状、材质、空间布局和光照，同时严格按照说明重建、修改或设计3D内容。
However, existing benchmarks provide limited coverage of such open-ended requests across real-world scenarios. 但是，现有基准在现实场景中对此类开放式请求的覆盖范围有限。
To bridge this gap, we introduce BlenderWorld, the first comprehensive benchmark dedicated to evaluating frontier models on realistic 3D creation tasks. 为了弥合这一差距，我们引入了BlenderWorld ，这是第一个致力于评估逼真3D创建任务的前沿模型的综合基准。
BlenderWorld comprises 223 tasks spanning architecture, products, natural environments, and scientific visualization, driven by text, image, video, and structured specification inputs. BlenderWorld由223项任务组成，涵盖架构、产品、自然环境和科学可视化，由文本、图像、视频和结构化规范输入驱动。
To rigorously assess these complex deliverables, we establish a unified evaluation protocol: we render the submitted Blender projects from multiple viewpoints and evaluate them against 2,651 task-specific binary rubrics alongside holistic visual quality scores. 为了严格评估这些复杂的可交付成果，我们建立了一个统一的评估协议：我们从多个角度渲染提交的Blender项目，并根据2,651个特定任务的二元评分细则表和全面的视觉质量评分进行评估。
Benchmarking thirteen frontier models reveals that GPT-6-Astra achieves the highest overall fused score of 79.9, followed by Opus-5 (73.0) and GPT-5.6-Sol (67.7). 对13个前沿模型进行基准测试显示， GPT-6-Astra的总体融合得分最高，为79.9 ，其次是Opus-5 （ 73.0 ）和GPT-5.6-Sol （ 67.7 ）。
Ultimately, our findings reveal a critical bottleneck: while current models can parse broad instructions, they still profoundly struggle with fine-grained 3D spatial coherence and accurate structural reproduction in Blender, leaving substantial headroom for future 3D-native agentics. 最终，我们的研究结果揭示了一个关键的瓶颈：虽然当前的模型可以解析广泛的指令，但它们仍然在Blender中与精细的3D空间连贯性和准确的结构复制进行着深刻的斗争，为未来的3D原生代理留下了巨大的空间。
highlights: first comprehensive benchmark dedicated to evaluating frontier models on realistic 3D creation tasks

featuredPapers.title: IndusAgent: Agentic Reinforcement Learning for Cross-Category Industrial Anomaly Detection
featuredPapers.authors: Rongbin Tan*, Fangfang Lin*, Jinguo Luo*
featuredPapers.summary:
Small defects in unfamiliar product categories can be difficult to distinguish from benign appearance variations in a global view. 在全球范围内，很难将不熟悉的产品类别中的小缺陷与良性外观变化区分开来。
Additional reasoning over the same view may leave this ambiguity unresolved. 对同一视图的其他推理可能会使这种模棱两可的问题得不到解决。
We introduce IndusAgent, a Qwen3-VL-8B inspection policy trained through supervised fine-tuning and tool-augmented reinforcement learning for cross-category industrial anomaly detection. 我们引入了IndusAgent ，这是一种Qwen3-VL-8B检测策略，通过监督微调和工具增强强化学习进行培训，用于跨类别工业异常检测。
The policy selects among six tools for cropping, enhancement, measurement, within-image comparison, texture analysis, and external visual opinions from Qwen3-VL-Max, then integrates returned observations into a structured diagnosis. 该策略从Qwen3-VL-Max的裁剪、增强、测量、图像内比较、纹理分析和外部视觉意见的六个工具中进行选择，然后将返回的观察结果集成到结构化诊断中。
Indus-CoT provides 3,000 trajectories from 26 Real-IAD categories, generated with actual tool feedback and screened against annotations after teacher generation. Indus-CoT提供来自26个Real-IAD类别的3,000条轨迹，这些轨迹通过实际工具反馈生成，并在教师生成后对照注释进行筛选。
GRPO optimizes an accuracy-gated objective that conditions localization, type, and tool rewards, including call costs, on final diagnostic correctness while retaining an independent format reward. GRPO优化了一个精度门控目标，该目标在最终诊断正确性方面为本地化、类型和工具奖励（包括呼叫成本）提供条件，同时保留独立的格式奖励。
Across five benchmarks, IndusAgent achieves 83.5% mean balanced accuracy, compared with 79.4% for direct Max inference under the common protocol. 在五个基准中， IndusAgent实现了83.5%的平均平衡精度，而在通用协议下，直接最大推断的准确率为79.4%。
Across three training seeds, the five-benchmark mean balanced accuracy is 80.5\% for a weight-matched ungated control and 83.5% for the gated policy. 在三个训练种子中，对于重量匹配的无门控控制，五基准平均平衡准确率为80.5\ % ，对于门控策略，平均平衡准确率为83.5%。
Evaluation uses disjoint product categories and a fixed defect vocabulary. 评估使用不相交的产品类别和固定的缺陷词汇。

featuredPapers.title: Web Agent Agentic Reinforcement Learning Decision Model Under Multi-Cost and Failure Risk
featuredPapers.authors: Qianli Ma, Limengxi Yue, Shuyang Xu
featuredPapers.summary:
Intelligent agent interactions in real-world web environments are commonly constrained by request budgets, time delays, anti-crawling restrictions, and operational failure risks. 现实Web环境中的智能代理交互通常受到请求预算、时间延迟、反爬网限制和操作故障风险的限制。
Strategies solely optimizing task success rates often exhibit unusable phenomena such as "high success but high cost" or "low risk but conservative failure." This paper proposes a constrained agentic reinforcement learning model for web agents, unifying page access, search requests, and external API calls into a unified long-term decision-making framework with associated costs. 仅优化任务成功率的策略通常表现出不可用的现象，例如“高成功但高成本”或“低风险但保守的失败”。“本文提出了一种用于Web代理的约束代理强化学习模型，将页面访问、搜索请求和外部API调用统一到具有相关成本的统一长期决策框架中。
It simultaneously incorporates cost budget constraints and tail risk control into the optimization objective: constructing a multidimensional cost vector comprising cumulative request count, total latency, and failure penalties to achieve budget compliance via Lagrange dual updates, while employing a CVaR risk term to suppress excessive exploration of high-failure-probability paths, thereby achieving an adaptive balance among "completion rate, cost, and risk."
  Experiments were conducted across 30-70 site/page templates and 800-1,500 end-to-end web tasks, including information extraction, price comparison, form submission, and cross-page navigation.
Interaction sequences spanned 20-120 steps with tool scales of 30-200. 交互序列跨越20-120个步骤，工具尺度为30-200。
Performance was benchmarked against unconstrained RL, budget-constrained RL, and rule-based/scripted web agents, quantifying task completion rates, cost-per-success, failure rates, and policy stability. 根据不受约束的RL、预算受限的RL和基于规则/脚本的Web代理对性能进行基准测试，量化任务完成率、每次成功成本、失败率和策略稳定性。
Results demonstrate that at equivalent completion rates, our method reduces C-PS by 22%-31% and lowers failure rates by 18%-26% under high failure penalties. 结果表明，在相同的完成率下，我们的方法在高故障罚款下可将C-PS降低22% -31% ，并将故障率降低18% -26%。
Under fixed budgets, task completion rates increase by 10%-16%, highlighting the necessity and effectiveness of constraint modeling for practical web agent deployment. 在固定预算下，任务完成率提高10% -16% ，凸显了约束建模在实际Web代理部署中的必要性和有效性。

featuredPapers.title: CoEvo-RSI: When Harnesses Evolve, Which Models Should Follow?
featuredPapers.authors: Jiaqi Su, Guibin Zhang, Jie-Jing Shao
featuredPapers.summary:
Model--harness co-evolution has emerged as a prominent paradigm for recursive self-improving (RSI) agents, jointly evolving their execution scaffolds and intrinsic capabilities. 模型- Harness协同进化已成为递归自我改善（ RSI ）代理的突出范例，共同发展其执行支架和内在能力。
We study the persistent yet often overlooked brain--body mismatch problem in this paradigm, where an evolving harness (body) demands behaviors its model (brain) has not learned or restricts capabilities it already possesses. 我们研究了这种范式中持续存在但经常被忽视的大脑-身体错配问题，在这种范式中，不断发展的线束（身体）要求其模型（大脑）尚未学习的行为或限制其已经拥有的能力。
We introduce CoEvo-RSI, a RSI framework that advances model--harness co-evolution through agent-driven, bidirectional historical inheritance. 我们引入了CoEvo-RSI ，这是一个RSI框架，它通过代理驱动的双向历史继承来推进模型- Harness协同进化。
Drawing on a shared evolutionary archive and execution feedback, a meta-agent coordinates harness development from historical designs with model checkpoint selection or merging and subsequent adaptation under the selected harness, aligning inherited capabilities with evolving execution requirements to reduce brain--body mismatch. 借助共享的进化存档和执行反馈，元代理通过模型检查点选择或合并以及所选线束下的后续适应来协调历史设计中的线束开发，使继承的能力与不断变化的执行要求保持一致，以减少脑-身体不匹配。
Using only supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on its own rejection-sampled trajectories, CoEvo-RSI makes Qwen3.5-9B competitive with larger models across diverse vertical applications, including multi-agent failure attribution, role-aware text-to-SQL, and smart-home instruction following. CoEvo-RSI仅在其自身的剔除采样轨迹上使用监督微调（ SFT ） ，使Qwen3.5-9B在不同的垂直应用中与更大的模型竞争，包括多代理失败归因、角色感知文本到SQL和智能家居指令跟踪。
It surpasses DeepSeek-V4-Pro on TraceElephant (+14.16 agent accuracy) and GLM-5.3 on HomeBench VM (+4.90 success rate), underscoring the need for brain--body alignment and the potential of bidirectional historical inheritance to advance agent co-evolution. 它超过了TraceElephant上的DeepSeek-V4-Pro （ +14.16药剂准确度）和HomeBench VM上的GLM-5.3 （ +4.90成功率） ，强调了大脑-身体对齐的必要性以及双向历史遗传的潜力，以促进药剂的共同进化。

featuredPapers.title: Trackable Skill Library Lifecycle Management for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
featuredPapers.authors: Xi Zhu, Yuanlin Duan, Changyi Yang
featuredPapers.summary:
Skill-augmented agentic RL has emerged as an effective approach to improving LLM agents on long-horizon tasks. 技能增强型代理强化学习已成为改进长期任务LLM代理的有效方法。
Despite this progress, individual skills may follow distinct trajectories as the policy evolves, with some becoming redundant after the model internalizes their capabilities, others remaining valuable as external scaffolding, and still others turning harmful. 尽管取得了这一进展，但随着政策的演变，个人技能可能会遵循不同的轨迹，其中一些技能在模型内化其能力后变得多余，另一些技能作为外部支架仍然具有价值，还有一些技能变得有害。
However, existing skill library systems fail to identify each skill's true contribution due to free-riding among co-retrieved skills, difficulty confounding across tasks, and the absence of skill-specific counterfactual evidence, which prevents reliable skill lifecycle management. 然而，现有的技能库系统由于在共同检索的技能之间搭便车、难以混淆任务以及缺乏特定技能的反事实证据而无法识别每项技能的真正贡献，这阻碍了可靠的技能生命周期管理。
We propose TrackRL, an agentic RL framework where skill tracking drives skill library full lifecycle management. 我们提出了TrackRL ，这是一个代理式RL框架，其中技能跟踪驱动技能库的整个生命周期管理。
Specifically, within each GRPO group, we turn grouped sampling into online randomized controlled experiments. 具体而言，在每个GRPO组中，我们将分组抽样转化为在线随机对照实验。
Independent random injection and within-group contrasts on the same task isolate each skill's true contribution, and reliability-weighted aggregation accumulates evidence across groups. 同一任务的独立随机注射和组内对比隔离了每项技能的真正贡献，可靠性加权聚合积累了跨组证据。

Experiments show that TrackRL outperforms recent skill-augmented RL baselines in both library-assisted and skill-free evaluation, with further analyses revealing how skill value shifts during policy learning and how evidence-driven state transitions shape skill library evolution. 实验表明， TrackRL在图书馆辅助和无技能评估方面都优于最近的技能增强RL基线，进一步分析揭示了政策学习过程中技能价值的转变以及循证驱动的状态转变如何影响技能库的演变。

featuredPapers.title: HarnessPro: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement with Pareto Optimization for Performance-Cost Trade-offs
featuredPapers.authors: Zhuoshi Pan, ZhiYuan Feng, Yukuo Cen
featuredPapers.summary:

Recent approaches improve harnesses through recursive self-improvement (RSI), but their performance gains often come with higher execution costs. 最近的方法通过递归自我改进（ RSI ）来改进线束，但其性能提升通常伴随着更高的执行成本。

In this setting, candidate harnesses are evaluated using LLM-generated tests without access to ground-truth solutions or official tests. 在此设置中，候选线束使用LLM生成的测试进行评估，而无需访问地面真相解决方案或官方测试。

Rather than returning a single harness, HarnessPro uses normalized weighted squared-distance selection to provide cost-focused (lite), balanced (medium), and performance-focused (heavy) harnesses for different deployment budgets.

featuredPapers.title: Compile Once, Run Cheap: Frozen, Portable Skills for Embodied Agents, and What Recursive Self-Improvement Adds
featuredPapers.authors: Jingwen Bai, Guochao Bai, Canbo Zhang
featuredPapers.summary:
Embodied AI lacks the data-rich pretraining that gave language models their agents and skills, so new manipulation capability costs demonstrations per task or a frontier model in every episode.
We study a third route: a strong general model acts only as an offline author that writes, runs, diagnoses and repairs a manipulation skill in simulation until it passes an exam on layouts drawn after freezing; the frozen skill then runs as code alone or under a cheap caller that reads only its description.
We call this skill-level recursive self-improvement Skill-RSI and specify a compile protocol (isolated, audited author; hidden validation layouts; no-feedback and inherit-only controls; tamper-evident ledger) and a reuse protocol that runs the identical files with executors from another model family.
On 7 RoboTwin 2.0 tasks with cluttered tables, Claude Code compiled 4 tasks into 7 frozen skills, 5 from a first draft needing only qualification, at USD 4.29-8.22 of author cost each (USD 55 per skill counting the 13 failed campaigns).
The other three tasks did not compile in 18 campaigns, including five with GPT-6 and a pre-registered 150-layout run: on the hardest task every campaign scored 78-95 of 100 but had 3-16 safety aborts, failing the gate of 95% success with zero aborts; a 100-episode exam bounds an abort rate only to 3.6%.
On hidden layouts, repair that inherits the previous version beat from-scratch rewriting in 8 of 8 controlled campaigns (sign test p = 0.004); an inherit-only lineage attributes most of the gap to inheritance, with development feedback adding a little (3 of 3, p = 0.125).
Write-once campaigns found no detectable first-draft effect of practice (minimum detectable effect 14 points).
The frozen skills kept 148/150 successes on new layouts with no model and 147/150 with a DeepSeek-flash caller at USD 0.00028-0.00054 per episode; no direct-control baseline was run.

featuredPapers.title: MOSAIC: More LLMs, Less Cost through Collaborative Reasoning for Compiler Optimizations
featuredPapers.authors: Annabelle Sujun Tang, Christopher Priebe, Lianhui Qin
featuredPapers.summary:
LLM-guided compiler optimization has recently shown promise.
However, current LLM-guided optimizers query a single LLM at every search step, so their cost grows with both that model's price and the search budget.
A smaller model is cheaper but degrades the search: in our experiments, a recent single-LLM optimizer reaches 10.2% (6.0%) lower speedup on GPU (CPU) with gpt-5-mini than with GPT-5.2.
Agentic multi-LLM frameworks add controllers, concurrent calls, and shared memory, whose overhead can offset the savings of cheaper models.
This paper shows that the optimization search tree itself can coordinate heterogeneous LLMs: the tree already records which proposals improved the program, and we can augment the tree to record which model made them.
That evidence can then be used to decide which model should propose next.
To this end, we introduce MOSAIC, in which each Monte Carlo tree search (MCTS) node records a program and the LLM that expands it, and the active LLM proposes both a compiler transformation and the LLM for the next step.
We also contribute an LLM-aware UCT that favors smaller models and a course-alteration rule that invokes the largest model only after repeated small-model regressions.
Against that single-LLM optimizer run with GPT-5.2 alone and the same number of search iterations and tree parameters, on an NVIDIA GPU (Intel CPU), MOSAIC with eight LLMs improves the geometric-mean speedup on five kernels by 7.2% (14.4%) and the end-to-end Llama-3-8B speedup by 1.61x (1.41x), while reducing kernel compilation time by 1.95x (1.74x) and API cost by 4.47x (4.32x), with GPT-5.2 making only 23.1% (23.9%) of LLM calls.
With the same eight models, random or round-robin model choice improves over the single-LLM baseline by only 2.5% on CPU, showing that the gains come from letting the LLMs choose the next model rather than from mixing the pool at random.

featuredPapers.title: RLTLDR: Self-improvement by Internalizing Self-generated Feedback
featuredPapers.authors: Michael Kirchhof, Eleonora Gualdoni, Andrew Szot
featuredPapers.summary:
The common paradigm of reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) is to let agents make multiple attempts at a task, and optimize towards the successful ones.
This becomes problematic in the realms of self-improvement, where tasks are so difficult that the agent has a low or even no chance of success, and where there are no teacher models or example solutions to distill from.
In this paper, we introduce RLTLDR.
After each failed attempt, we show the policy the verifier outputs and let it write its own feedback, in the form of a single TL;DR insight.
The next rollout is conditioned on all previous insights, and we sequentially sample rollouts until a solution is found.
Moreover, we enable backpropagation on the in-context insights to internalize a direct task to insight mapping.
On challenging tool-calling and coding datasets (filtered to Pass@128=0), standard GRPO training of a Qwen 3.5 9B Thinking policy stays flat at a Pass@1 of 0% to 1%.
RLTLDR breaks through this learning barrier, achieving a Pass@1 of 14-31% with insights in context during training and, crucially, 12-13% when no insight is in context at eval time.
We identify that the key is the task to insight internalization.
To study this further, we reduce our approach to SFTLDR, training only on (task, insight) tuples, without showing or backpropagating on any rollouts.
Training on only 4k of these tuples recovers almost the full performance of RLTLDR and classical SFT on full rollouts.
This demonstrates a promising compacted training paradigm of the form "on this sort of task, keep this sort of thing in mind", which we hope to inspire future research on.
highlights: In this paper, we introduce RLTLDR.

featuredPapers.title: OpenCollab: A Multi-Agent Coding Framework with Programmable Collaboration and Controllable Runtime
featuredPapers.authors: Chun-Wah Hsu, Kai Gong, Yu Wu
featuredPapers.summary:
Multi-agent coding systems are designed to tackle complex software engineering tasks through collaboration.
However, existing evaluations typically assume configured organizations are followed faithfully, whereas reality differs.
This behavioral gap, combined with differences in underlying system components, prevents clear attribution of observed gains.
To this end, we introduce OpenCollab, a multi-agent coding framework that provides a unified infrastructure for programmable collaboration and controllable runtime.
Specifically, OpenCollab unifies organization design, enforces experimental control on a shared runtime, and tracks execution through fine-grained event streams.
On this basis, we define Adherence to quantify whether the declared organization is actually realized.
Our experiments reveal that agents collaborate very differently across configurations: changing any single dimension shifts Adherence, from 47.2% to as high as 97.2%.
Furthermore, extensive agentic coding benchmarks show that OpenCollab (Duo) establishes new SOTA performance compared to the mainstream harnesses such as Mini-SWE-agent, OpenHands, Codex CLI, and Claude Code, showing that a well-designed organization can outperform strong existing harnesses, while OpenCollab's single-agent configuration uses the fewest tokens across all evaluated suites.
OpenCollab establishes a unified multi-agent infrastructure for easy programmable collaboration and controlled causal evaluation.

featuredPapers.title: AM-Bench: A Unified Taxonomy and Evaluation Suite for Agentic Misalignment
featuredPapers.authors: Eric Zhang, Terry Jingchen Zhang, Chijioke Ugwuanyi
featuredPapers.summary:
As LLM-based agents are deployed with increasing autonomy in real-world environments, a critical failure mode emerges: agentic misalignment, where agents choose harmful actions over failure.
However, existing safety benchmarks primarily evaluate whether agents comply with explicitly harmful instructions, leaving the conditions that cause agents to choose harmful actions poorly understood.
To address this limitation, we propose AM-Bench, a unified taxonomy and 35 scenario evaluation benchmark spanning seven industries for agentic misalignment grounded in the fraud triangle, a well-established criminological framework explaining goal-directed misconduct.
We adapt this framework to agentic environments and construct our evaluation suite and detection systems along three dimensions: perceived threat, perceived opportunity, and reasoning.
We operationalize each dimension into structured subcategories rooted in prior theory: five threat categories derived from the instrumental convergence thesis, seven opportunity categories drawn from the Emergent Strategic Reasoning Risks (ESRR) taxonomy, and a novel four-question binary reasoning framework synthesized from prior literature.
Our evaluation of 10 frontier models reveals a 62-percentage-point gap in misalignment across scenarios, with Gemini 3 Flash and Gemini 3.1 Pro exhibiting the highest levels of agentic misalignment while Claude Sonnet 4.6 displays near-zero rates across all conditions.
Our reasoning framework further reveals that models may exhibit harmful behaviours without explicit situational awareness or explanation, complicating both mitigation and detection.

featuredPapers.title: IF-MAP: Influence-Function-Inspired Agent Prioritization in Multi-Agent Systems
featuredPapers.authors: Jie Mao, Pingchen Lu, Zikun Qu
featuredPapers.summary:
Improving every agent in an LLM-based multi-agent system can be prohibitively costly, making it important to identify which agent should be prioritized to achieve the greatest system-level gain with limited resources.
Failure attribution can inform this decision, but an agent's responsibility for failures does not directly reveal the system-level gains achievable by improving it.
We therefore introduce IF-MAP, an influence-function-inspired method for identifying agents with high potential for system-level improvement.
For each agent, IF-MAP measures end-to-end loss changes under controlled semantic prompt perturbations, fits a regularized local response model in a low-dimensional prompt-embedding subspace, and uses the estimated response norm as a priority score.
This black-box procedure requires no access to model parameters or gradients and produces agent priorities that can guide subsequent improvement effort.
We evaluate IF-MAP across six multi-agent workflows spanning code generation, question answering, and mathematical reasoning, using the same priorities for prompt optimization and model upgrades.
Optimizing the selected agents' prompts achieves a macro-average gain of 3.81 percentage points, compared with 1.85 for uniform agent selection.
Across five target models, upgrading the selected agents yields macro-average gains of 7.62-16.42 percentage points, compared with 3.81-8.62 for uniform agent selection.
Despite its probing overhead, IF-MAP reduces Qwen3-8B and DeepSeek-V3.2 token use by 74.2% and 35.2%, respectively, relative to optimizing every agent, and reduces target-model tokens by 63.6-64.9% relative to upgrading every agent.
These results support the use of IF-MAP to identify promising agents and direct improvement effort toward greater end-to-end performance gains.

featuredPapers.title: MELD: Recursive Self-Improvement via Hierarchical Coordination for Multi-Agent Scientific Discovery
featuredPapers.authors: Sizhe Tang, Zuyuan Zhang, Zeyu Fang

Multi-agent scientific discovery with large language models raises a coupled learning problem: research assignments determine both which experiments are pursued and the experiences from which agents adapt.
We introduce MELD, a unified hierarchical test-time training framework that jointly adapts a team-level Coordinator policy and agent-level individual Scientist policies within a single discovery process.
The Coordinator generates a joint portfolio of search branches and research directives over a shared derivation tree, while Scientists develop hypotheses and execution plans implemented by a shared frozen Executor.
Both levels receive alternating GRPO-style parameter updates under a shared smooth best-of-budget objective, allowing team organization and individual research behavior to co-evolve in a recursive self-improvement loop.
Our analysis establishes objective alignment for the hierarchy, characterizes conditions for coordination gains over independent parallel discovery and the first-order benefit of private adaptation, and derives a finite-budget regret bound for adapted models.
On 22 MLGym and MLE-bench tasks, MELD is best on 20 of them and achieves the highest aggregate normalized scores on MLGym, using a 4B backbone for coordination and research.
Most baselines use proprietary Scientists, and all systems share one frozen Executor.

featuredPapers.title: One Skill Takes Over: Clashing Agent Skills and a One-File Fix
featuredPapers.authors: Parsa Razmara, Seyedarmin Azizi, Ardalan Aryashad
featuredPapers.summary:
Agent Skills are instruction files that tell a coding agent how to do one job.
Users install skills from many authors, so two skills for the same job can be active at the same time.
We ask what a model does when both skill files are in its context: does it combine their compatible rules, or follow one skill and drop the other?
We build SkillClash, 16 pairs of same-job skills in which code checks every rule and a reference output shows the best result that can be reached.
On seven models from five families, from 4B open models to Qwen3-235B and GPT-4.1, a skill's rules are followed 93 to 99% of the time when it is loaded alone and 61 to 62% when a same-job skill is loaded next to it.
Most outputs show takeover: every rule that only one skill asks for is followed, and every rule that only the other skill asks for is dropped.
The worked examples inside the skills drive this.
When each skill file instead ends with one example that follows both skills, takeover falls to 1 to 15% on the six models we tested.
Telling the model which skill has priority does not bring the dropped skill back, and telling it to apply both skills brings the dropped skill back only on the two strong models and leaves the interacting rules broken.
One merged skill file written by the strongest model we used, Claude Opus 5.5, lets all seven models follow 96 to 99% of the achievable rules.
Most of its gain over a plain list of both skills' rules comes from its one worked example, and such an example helps only when it is correct.
Code and data: https://github.com/prazmara/skillclash

featuredPapers.title: EvalRx: Agentic Diagnosis and Verified Repair of Foundation Models
featuredPapers.authors: Jiaqi Liu, Ruinan Jin, Yitong Tang
featuredPapers.summary:
Model evaluation reveals where models fail, but rarely why or whether a proposed fix genuinely works.
We introduce EvalRx, an open-source agentic framework for statistically grounded model diagnosis and repair.
EvalRx discovers systematic failure modes, explores candidate mechanisms, formulates falsifiable hypotheses, and verifies them by executing frozen, pre-specified tests before using supported diagnoses to guide tiered repair.
Candidate repairs are validated against the unchanged model and promoted only when they improve the target behavior without unacceptable regression.
Across language, vision-language, and audio-language settings spanning Gemini, Qwen, Gemma, and Nemotron, EvalRx improves performance in all 12 evaluated model family-modality combinations, with gains ranging from +1.4 to +10.9 percentage points (+5.8 points on average).
These results show that model evaluation can serve not only to measure failures, but to support an auditable process for diagnosing and repairing them.

featuredPapers.title: BetaMem: Learning to Remember a Changing World for Embodied Agents
featuredPapers.authors: Mai Liu, He Sun, Siru Zhong
featuredPapers.summary:
Long-horizon embodied agents face temporal confusion and incomplete or distorted records, recurring errors from fixed memory rules, and growing storage and retrieval costs.
We present BetaMem, a framework for building and evolving traceable long-term memory through six linked layers: working, spatial, entity, episodic, experiential, and procedural memory.
A dual-level write contract constrains operation executability and source support for content: supervised fine-tuning learns compliant memory operations, while reinforcement learning combines repeated sampling with teacher verification of the original observations to reward complete, accurate records and penalize omissions, distortion, and unsupported content.
We formulate failure-driven policy recursive self-improvement through diagnosis along the causal sequence of memory operations and local rule repairs gated by independent replay.
Atomic tools frame storage, updates, retrieval, and forgetting as cost-utility allocation under storage and read budgets.
Using the open-source Qwen3.5-9B model for memory generation, BetaMem achieves overall scores of 48.08% on M3-Bench-robot, 92.08% on LoCoMo, 72.6% on OpenEQA EM-EQA, and 62.4% on EgoLifeQA, the highest among the listed memory methods under their respective evaluation protocols.
Training the model for memory generation raises the contract pass rate from 50.9% to 86.2% while reducing output tokens per stored action by 47.3%.
A separate Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct evaluation on EMem-Bench achieves an average success rate of 38.4% and an average error recurrence rate of 24.9%.
We perform best among evaluated methods using comparably sized open-source models.
Category results show that we have advantages in integrating information across observations, recalling events over long histories, and inferring personal habits.

featuredPapers.title: OR-License: Evaluating LLM Agents as Real-World Operations Research Practitioners
featuredPapers.authors: Peisong Wang, Feixue Liu, Yize Meng

Can large language model (LLM) agents deliver expert-level operations research (OR) solutions directly from original client materials, without prior expert reformulation?
Existing OR benchmarks typically begin with self-contained descriptions or predefined optimization tasks, underrepresenting the translation of original business materials into professionally validated solutions.
We introduce OR-License, an end-to-end benchmark of 31 instances across 10 industrial scenarios from paid OR engagements totaling USD 3.68 million.
It preserves original requirements, input data, deliverable formats, and information boundaries after de-identification.
To study information acquisition, we introduce ORSim, a controlled client simulator that discloses business facts without supplying OR expertise.
Hidden evaluation checks feasibility and compares objective quality against original expert solutions accepted by clients before benchmark construction.
Deployment-Adjusted Quality (DAQ) averages expert-relative quality across instances, assigning zero to infeasible deliveries.
Across 11 frontier LLMs using coding-agent harnesses, several exceed the expert reference in conditional objective quality, but none matches its DAQ; the strongest primary Claude Code configuration achieves 88.39% strict feasibility and a DAQ of 0.87 against the expert reference of 1.
Client information acquisition extends beyond clarification into solution development and validation, with some later stages showing higher confirmed issue-resolution proportions.
Trajectory analysis identifies formulation and implementation failures, while task-equalized research-chain completion rates range from 24% to 45% across models on evaluable tasks.
These findings motivate sustained information-gap resolution, faithful problem formulation, and evidence-linked self-improvement for reliable long-horizon agents.
highlights: exceed the expert reference in conditional objective quality

featuredPapers.title: Hyper Algorithm Design Agent: Evolving Learnable Optimizer from Zero
featuredPapers.authors: Zipei Yu, Yue-Jiao Gong, Zeyuan Ma
featuredPapers.summary:
Meta-Black-Box Optimization (MetaBBO) is one of the highlights in the recent AI for Optimization trend.
This paradigm's bi-level workflow leverages the learnable algorithm design policy at meta level to ensure the performance and generalization improvement on the low-level optimization task.
While MetaBBO helps advance the performance lower bound of the resulted optimization system, it is currently handcrafted and customized case by case to adapt different optimization problems, which inevitably introduces inherent subjectivity and hence restricts the performance upper bound and usability in practice.
In this paper, we address this issue by regarding MetaBBO's design loop as coding task, where we could introduce openendedness into MetaBBO with recursive self-improvement capability of advanced coding agents.
Specifically, we propose a dual-agent framework: i) a task agent continuously refines the codebase of a target MetaBBO approach through code evolution; ii) a hyper agent progressively modifies the task agent and itself to provide open-ended design behavior; iii) the evolved MetaBBO codebase is evaluated and all in-execution information is fed back to the agents for recursive self-referential improvement.
As a result, given a naive MetaBBO template, our framework automates a design evolution and finds novel variants superior to up-to-date human-made MetaBBO baselines.
Surprisingly, the experimental results also demonstrate that our framework supports fast adaption across different optimization domains.
Solid interpretation analysis further reveals interesting design principles emerge in such open-ended process.
This work serves as the first exploration on automating design of complex learning-assisted optimization algorithms.
highlights: first exploration on automating design of complex learning-assisted optimization algorithms

featuredPapers.title: HTN-Orchestrate: A Hierarchical Task Network Framework for Multi-Agent Orchestration
featuredPapers.authors: Yanchen Deng, Jianguo Huang, Yao Long Teng
featuredPapers.summary:
Orchestrating multiple agents on a complex task requires reconciling local subtask execution with global task planning.
Dynamic dispatch approaches provide execution flexibility but do not explicitly model subtask hierarchies or dependencies, while predefined workflows impose this structure but fix the decomposition before execution begins.
Therefore, we introduce HTN-Orchestrate, a two-layer framework that separates these responsibilities through a hierarchical task network (HTN).
The Planner maintains subtask hierarchies and dependencies, deferring decomposition until prerequisite results become available, while local Orchestrators schedule workers to execute each leaf subtask.
Results propagate upward under \textbf{AND} semantics, and accumulated findings inform a rebuilt task network when the current decomposition cannot resolve the task.
On five benchmarks spanning web research, scientific reasoning, and research workflows, HTN-Orchestrate outperforms ReAct, Agent Team, and DeepSeek Harness using the same base model, achieving 89.73% accuracy on BrowseComp and 73.44% on SUPERChem, exceeding Agent Team by 2.45 and 4.69 percentage points, respectively.

papers.title: BlenderWorld: Benchmarking Visual Agents for 3D Creation from Real-World References
papers.summary:
Recent advances in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have enabled them to act as autonomous agents, creating and editing 3D models via code or direct software manipulation. 多模态大型语言模型（ MLLM ）的最新进展使它们能够充当自主代理，通过代码或直接软件操作创建和编辑3D模型。
In practical workflows, these models must infer object shapes, materials, spatial layouts, and lighting from diverse references while strictly following instructions to reconstruct, modify, or design 3D content. 在实际工作流程中，这些模型必须从不同的参考中推断出对象形状、材质、空间布局和光照，同时严格按照说明重建、修改或设计3D内容。
However, existing benchmarks provide limited coverage of such open-ended requests across real-world scenarios. 但是，现有基准在现实场景中对此类开放式请求的覆盖范围有限。
To bridge this gap, we introduce BlenderWorld, the first comprehensive benchmark dedicated to evaluating frontier models on realistic 3D creation tasks. 为了弥合这一差距，我们引入了BlenderWorld ，这是第一个致力于评估逼真3D创建任务的前沿模型的综合基准。
BlenderWorld comprises 223 tasks spanning architecture, products, natural environments, and scientific visualization, driven by text, image, video, and structured specification inputs. BlenderWorld由223项任务组成，涵盖架构、产品、自然环境和科学可视化，由文本、图像、视频和结构化规范输入驱动。
To rigorously assess these complex deliverables, we establish a unified evaluation protocol: we render the submitted Blender projects from multiple viewpoints and evaluate them against 2,651 task-specific binary rubrics alongside holistic visual quality scores. 为了严格评估这些复杂的可交付成果，我们建立了一个统一的评估协议：我们从多个角度渲染提交的Blender项目，并根据2,651个特定任务的二元评分细则表和全面的视觉质量评分进行评估。
Benchmarking thirteen frontier models reveals that GPT-6-Astra achieves the highest overall fused score of 79.9, followed by Opus-5 (73.0) and GPT-5.6-Sol (67.7). 对13个前沿模型进行基准测试显示， GPT-6-Astra的总体融合得分最高，为79.9 ，其次是Opus-5 （ 73.0 ）和GPT-5.6-Sol （ 67.7 ）。
Ultimately, our findings reveal a critical bottleneck: while current models can parse broad instructions, they still profoundly struggle with fine-grained 3D spatial coherence and accurate structural reproduction in Blender, leaving substantial headroom for future 3D-native agentics. 最终，我们的研究结果揭示了一个关键的瓶颈：虽然当前的模型可以解析广泛的指令，但它们仍然在Blender中与精细的3D空间连贯性和准确的结构复制进行着深刻的斗争，为未来的3D原生代理留下了巨大的空间。
highlights: first comprehensive benchmark dedicated to evaluating frontier models on realistic 3D creation tasks

papers.title: IndusAgent: Agentic Reinforcement Learning for Cross-Category Industrial Anomaly Detection
papers.summary:
Small defects in unfamiliar product categories can be difficult to distinguish from benign appearance variations in a global view. 在全球范围内，很难将不熟悉的产品类别中的小缺陷与良性外观变化区分开来。
Additional reasoning over the same view may leave this ambiguity unresolved. 对同一视图的其他推理可能会使这种模棱两可的问题得不到解决。
We introduce IndusAgent, a Qwen3-VL-8B inspection policy trained through supervised fine-tuning and tool-augmented reinforcement learning for cross-category industrial anomaly detection. 我们引入了IndusAgent ，这是一种Qwen3-VL-8B检测策略，通过监督微调和工具增强强化学习进行培训，用于跨类别工业异常检测。
The policy selects among six tools for cropping, enhancement, measurement, within-image comparison, texture analysis, and external visual opinions from Qwen3-VL-Max, then integrates returned observations into a structured diagnosis. 该策略从Qwen3-VL-Max的裁剪、增强、测量、图像内比较、纹理分析和外部视觉意见的六个工具中进行选择，然后将返回的观察结果集成到结构化诊断中。
Indus-CoT provides 3,000 trajectories from 26 Real-IAD categories, generated with actual tool feedback and screened against annotations after teacher generation. Indus-CoT提供来自26个Real-IAD类别的3,000条轨迹，这些轨迹通过实际工具反馈生成，并在教师生成后对照注释进行筛选。
GRPO optimizes an accuracy-gated objective that conditions localization, type, and tool rewards, including call costs, on final diagnostic correctness while retaining an independent format reward. GRPO优化了一个精度门控目标，该目标在最终诊断正确性方面为本地化、类型和工具奖励（包括呼叫成本）提供条件，同时保留独立的格式奖励。
Across five benchmarks, IndusAgent achieves 83.5% mean balanced accuracy, compared with 79.4% for direct Max inference under the common protocol. 在五个基准中， IndusAgent实现了83.5%的平均平衡精度，而在通用协议下，直接最大推断的准确率为79.4%。
Across three training seeds, the five-benchmark mean balanced accuracy is 80.5\% for a weight-matched ungated control and 83.5% for the gated policy. 在三个训练种子中，对于重量匹配的无门控控制，五基准平均平衡准确率为80.5\ % ，对于门控策略，平均平衡准确率为83.5%。
Evaluation uses disjoint product categories and a fixed defect vocabulary. 评估使用不相交的产品类别和固定的缺陷词汇。

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: CoEvo-RSI: When Harnesses Evolve, Which Models Should Follow?
papers.summary:
Model--harness co-evolution has emerged as a prominent paradigm for recursive self-improving (RSI) agents, jointly evolving their execution scaffolds and intrinsic capabilities. 模型- Harness协同进化已成为递归自我改善（ RSI ）代理的突出范例，共同发展其执行支架和内在能力。
We study the persistent yet often overlooked brain--body mismatch problem in this paradigm, where an evolving harness (body) demands behaviors its model (brain) has not learned or restricts capabilities it already possesses. 我们研究了这种范式中持续存在但经常被忽视的大脑-身体错配问题，在这种范式中，不断发展的线束（身体）要求其模型（大脑）尚未学习的行为或限制其已经拥有的能力。
We introduce CoEvo-RSI, a RSI framework that advances model--harness co-evolution through agent-driven, bidirectional historical inheritance. 我们引入了CoEvo-RSI ，这是一个RSI框架，它通过代理驱动的双向历史继承来推进模型- Harness协同进化。
Drawing on a shared evolutionary archive and execution feedback, a meta-agent coordinates harness development from historical designs with model checkpoint selection or merging and subsequent adaptation under the selected harness, aligning inherited capabilities with evolving execution requirements to reduce brain--body mismatch. 借助共享的进化存档和执行反馈，元代理通过模型检查点选择或合并以及所选线束下的后续适应来协调历史设计中的线束开发，使继承的能力与不断变化的执行要求保持一致，以减少脑-身体不匹配。
Using only supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on its own rejection-sampled trajectories, CoEvo-RSI makes Qwen3.5-9B competitive with larger models across diverse vertical applications, including multi-agent failure attribution, role-aware text-to-SQL, and smart-home instruction following. CoEvo-RSI仅在其自身的剔除采样轨迹上使用监督微调（ SFT ） ，使Qwen3.5-9B在不同的垂直应用中与更大的模型竞争，包括多代理失败归因、角色感知文本到SQL和智能家居指令跟踪。
It surpasses DeepSeek-V4-Pro on TraceElephant (+14.16 agent accuracy) and GLM-5.3 on HomeBench VM (+4.90 success rate), underscoring the need for brain--body alignment and the potential of bidirectional historical inheritance to advance agent co-evolution. 它超过了TraceElephant上的DeepSeek-V4-Pro （ +14.16药剂准确度）和HomeBench VM上的GLM-5.3 （ +4.90成功率） ，强调了大脑-身体对齐的必要性以及双向历史遗传的潜力，以促进药剂的共同进化。

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: Zephyrus-R1: Agentic Reinforcement Learning for Weather Reporting
papers.summary:
Reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as a key method for training AI models in scientific applications, but RL remains difficult when outputs cannot easily be verified against a known ground-truth answer. 强化学习（ RL ）已成为在科学应用中训练人工智能模型的关键方法，但当无法根据已知的地面真实答案轻松验证输出时， RL仍然很困难。
Natural-language weather forecast reports are one such domain: they translate atmospheric data into assessments of weather evolution, hazards, and uncertainty for both the general public and key decision-makers. 自然语言天气预报报告就是这样一个领域：它们将大气数据转化为公众和关键决策者对天气演变、灾害和不确定性的评估。
Unlike numerical weather-analysis questions, they admit many valid outputs, which limits deterministic verification. 与数值天气分析问题不同，它们承认许多有效的输出，这限制了确定性验证。
To address this, we develop Zephyrus-R1, a practical framework for RL on scientific weather forecast reporting. 为了解决这个问题，我们开发了Zephyrus-R1 ，这是科学天气预报报告的实用框架。
We focus on three key components of the agentic RL pipeline: reward design, curriculum learning, and an analysis of human-expert alignment. 我们专注于代理RL管道的三个关键组成部分：奖励设计、课程学习和人与专家对齐分析。
To encourage both report legibility and factual accuracy, we design a reward function that combines a meteorological rubric with bidirectional claim entailment, both evaluated against National Weather Service reference reports. 为了鼓励报告清晰度和事实准确性，我们设计了一个奖励函数，将气象分类和双向索赔相结合，两者都根据国家气象局参考报告进行了评估。
Our framework optimizes this reward in a simulated tool-calling environment, enabling vision-language agents to gather and analyze forecast evidence across regions and lead times before producing a report. 我们的框架在模拟工具调用环境中优化此奖励，使视觉语言代理能够在生成报告之前收集和分析跨地区和交付周期的预测证据。
We use annotations from three meteorologists to audit the claim labels produced by our LLM judges. 我们使用三位气象学家的注释来审核法学硕士评委制作的索赔标签。
Finally, a curriculum helps small models first develop tool use and scientific reasoning through RL on verifiable weather-analysis questions, then optimize the open-ended report reward. 最后，课程帮助小模型首先通过RL在可验证的天气分析问题上开发工具使用和科学推理，然后优化开放式报告奖励。
After training Qwen3.5-4B with Zephyrus-R1, we improve the mean across six judge-metric scores by 26% over the base model and achieve results competitive with frontier open-weight models. 在使用Zephyrus-R1训练Qwen3.5-4B之后，我们将六个判断指标的平均分比基本模型提高了26% ，并实现了与前沿开放权重模型竞争的结果。
For Qwen3.8-27B, we improve the same mean by 13% over the base model, by 6.7% over Kimi-K3, and by 2.7% over GPT-5.6-Luna. 对于Qwen3.8-27B ，我们将相同的平均值比基本模型提高了13% ，比Kimi-K3提高了6.7% ，比GPT-5.6-Luna提高了2.7%。
highlights: first develop tool use and scientific reasoning through RL on verifiable weather-analysis questions

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: HarnessPro: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement with Pareto Optimization for Performance-Cost Trade-offs
papers.summary:
Harness development plays a crucial role in building capable AI agents. 线束开发在构建有能力的人工智能代理中起着至关重要的作用。
Recent approaches improve harnesses through recursive self-improvement (RSI), but their performance gains often come with higher execution costs. 最近的方法通过递归自我改进（ RSI ）来改进线束，但其性能提升通常伴随着更高的执行成本。
We introduce HarnessPro, a label-free method for evolving harnesses to improve task performance while reducing execution cost. 我们引入了HarnessPro ，这是一种无标签的方法，用于改进线束，以提高任务性能，同时降低执行成本。
In this setting, candidate harnesses are evaluated using LLM-generated tests without access to ground-truth solutions or official tests. 在此设置中，候选线束使用LLM生成的测试进行评估，而无需访问地面真相解决方案或官方测试。
Specialized agents diagnose execution trajectories, plan updates with different performance-cost priorities, and implement them as candidate harnesses. 专业代理诊断执行轨迹，使用不同的绩效成本优先级计划更新，并将其作为候选工具来实施。
Rather than returning a single harness, HarnessPro uses normalized weighted squared-distance selection to provide cost-focused (lite), balanced (medium), and performance-focused (heavy) harnesses for different deployment budgets.
Selected harnesses enter the next iteration, where execution feedback guides further updates.
Our experiments cover Terminal-Bench 2, SWE-Bench Pro, and ProgramBench, using GPT-5.5 with Codex and GLM-5.2 with Claude Code.
Across these benchmarks using GPT-5.5 with Codex, the heavy mode of HarnessPro achieves an average pass-rate gain of 2.0 percentage points and an average per-task cost reduction of 26.1% relative to RHO.
This advantage also holds when using GLM-5.2 with Claude Code.
Code is available at https://github.com/pzs19/HarnessPro
highlights: Harness development plays a crucial role in building capable AI agents.

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: Compile Once, Run Cheap: Frozen, Portable Skills for Embodied Agents, and What Recursive Self-Improvement Adds
papers.summary:
Embodied AI lacks the data-rich pretraining that gave language models their agents and skills, so new manipulation capability costs demonstrations per task or a frontier model in every episode.
We study a third route: a strong general model acts only as an offline author that writes, runs, diagnoses and repairs a manipulation skill in simulation until it passes an exam on layouts drawn after freezing; the frozen skill then runs as code alone or under a cheap caller that reads only its description.
We call this skill-level recursive self-improvement Skill-RSI and specify a compile protocol (isolated, audited author; hidden validation layouts; no-feedback and inherit-only controls; tamper-evident ledger) and a reuse protocol that runs the identical files with executors from another model family.
On 7 RoboTwin 2.0 tasks with cluttered tables, Claude Code compiled 4 tasks into 7 frozen skills, 5 from a first draft needing only qualification, at USD 4.29-8.22 of author cost each (USD 55 per skill counting the 13 failed campaigns).
The other three tasks did not compile in 18 campaigns, including five with GPT-6 and a pre-registered 150-layout run: on the hardest task every campaign scored 78-95 of 100 but had 3-16 safety aborts, failing the gate of 95% success with zero aborts; a 100-episode exam bounds an abort rate only to 3.6%.
On hidden layouts, repair that inherits the previous version beat from-scratch rewriting in 8 of 8 controlled campaigns (sign test p = 0.004); an inherit-only lineage attributes most of the gap to inheritance, with development feedback adding a little (3 of 3, p = 0.125).
Write-once campaigns found no detectable first-draft effect of practice (minimum detectable effect 14 points).
