The frozen skills kept 148/150 successes on new layouts with no model and 147/150 with a DeepSeek-flash caller at USD 0.00028-0.00054 per episode; no direct-control baseline was run.

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: MOSAIC: More LLMs, Less Cost through Collaborative Reasoning for Compiler Optimizations
papers.summary:
LLM-guided compiler optimization has recently shown promise.
However, current LLM-guided optimizers query a single LLM at every search step, so their cost grows with both that model's price and the search budget.
A smaller model is cheaper but degrades the search: in our experiments, a recent single-LLM optimizer reaches 10.2% (6.0%) lower speedup on GPU (CPU) with gpt-5-mini than with GPT-5.2.
Agentic multi-LLM frameworks add controllers, concurrent calls, and shared memory, whose overhead can offset the savings of cheaper models.
This paper shows that the optimization search tree itself can coordinate heterogeneous LLMs: the tree already records which proposals improved the program, and we can augment the tree to record which model made them.
That evidence can then be used to decide which model should propose next.
To this end, we introduce MOSAIC, in which each Monte Carlo tree search (MCTS) node records a program and the LLM that expands it, and the active LLM proposes both a compiler transformation and the LLM for the next step.
We also contribute an LLM-aware UCT that favors smaller models and a course-alteration rule that invokes the largest model only after repeated small-model regressions.
Against that single-LLM optimizer run with GPT-5.2 alone and the same number of search iterations and tree parameters, on an NVIDIA GPU (Intel CPU), MOSAIC with eight LLMs improves the geometric-mean speedup on five kernels by 7.2% (14.4%) and the end-to-end Llama-3-8B speedup by 1.61x (1.41x), while reducing kernel compilation time by 1.95x (1.74x) and API cost by 4.47x (4.32x), with GPT-5.2 making only 23.1% (23.9%) of LLM calls.
With the same eight models, random or round-robin model choice improves over the single-LLM baseline by only 2.5% on CPU, showing that the gains come from letting the LLMs choose the next model rather than from mixing the pool at random.
highlights: LLM-guided compiler optimization has recently shown promise.

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: RLTLDR: Self-improvement by Internalizing Self-generated Feedback
papers.summary:
The common paradigm of reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) is to let agents make multiple attempts at a task, and optimize towards the successful ones.
This becomes problematic in the realms of self-improvement, where tasks are so difficult that the agent has a low or even no chance of success, and where there are no teacher models or example solutions to distill from.
In this paper, we introduce RLTLDR.
After each failed attempt, we show the policy the verifier outputs and let it write its own feedback, in the form of a single TL;DR insight.
The next rollout is conditioned on all previous insights, and we sequentially sample rollouts until a solution is found.
Moreover, we enable backpropagation on the in-context insights to internalize a direct task to insight mapping.
On challenging tool-calling and coding datasets (filtered to Pass@128=0), standard GRPO training of a Qwen 3.5 9B Thinking policy stays flat at a Pass@1 of 0% to 1%.
RLTLDR breaks through this learning barrier, achieving a Pass@1 of 14-31% with insights in context during training and, crucially, 12-13% when no insight is in context at eval time.
We identify that the key is the task to insight internalization.
To study this further, we reduce our approach to SFTLDR, training only on (task, insight) tuples, without showing or backpropagating on any rollouts.
Training on only 4k of these tuples recovers almost the full performance of RLTLDR and classical SFT on full rollouts.
This demonstrates a promising compacted training paradigm of the form "on this sort of task, keep this sort of thing in mind", which we hope to inspire future research on.
highlights: In this paper, we introduce RLTLDR.

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: OpenCollab: A Multi-Agent Coding Framework with Programmable Collaboration and Controllable Runtime
papers.summary:
Multi-agent coding systems are designed to tackle complex software engineering tasks through collaboration.
However, existing evaluations typically assume configured organizations are followed faithfully, whereas reality differs.
This behavioral gap, combined with differences in underlying system components, prevents clear attribution of observed gains.
To this end, we introduce OpenCollab, a multi-agent coding framework that provides a unified infrastructure for programmable collaboration and controllable runtime.
Specifically, OpenCollab unifies organization design, enforces experimental control on a shared runtime, and tracks execution through fine-grained event streams.
On this basis, we define Adherence to quantify whether the declared organization is actually realized.
Our experiments reveal that agents collaborate very differently across configurations: changing any single dimension shifts Adherence, from 47.2% to as high as 97.2%.
Furthermore, extensive agentic coding benchmarks show that OpenCollab (Duo) establishes new SOTA performance compared to the mainstream harnesses such as Mini-SWE-agent, OpenHands, Codex CLI, and Claude Code, showing that a well-designed organization can outperform strong existing harnesses, while OpenCollab's single-agent configuration uses the fewest tokens across all evaluated suites.
OpenCollab establishes a unified multi-agent infrastructure for easy programmable collaboration and controlled causal evaluation.

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: AM-Bench: A Unified Taxonomy and Evaluation Suite for Agentic Misalignment
papers.summary:
As LLM-based agents are deployed with increasing autonomy in real-world environments, a critical failure mode emerges: agentic misalignment, where agents choose harmful actions over failure.
However, existing safety benchmarks primarily evaluate whether agents comply with explicitly harmful instructions, leaving the conditions that cause agents to choose harmful actions poorly understood.
To address this limitation, we propose AM-Bench, a unified taxonomy and 35 scenario evaluation benchmark spanning seven industries for agentic misalignment grounded in the fraud triangle, a well-established criminological framework explaining goal-directed misconduct.
We adapt this framework to agentic environments and construct our evaluation suite and detection systems along three dimensions: perceived threat, perceived opportunity, and reasoning.
We operationalize each dimension into structured subcategories rooted in prior theory: five threat categories derived from the instrumental convergence thesis, seven opportunity categories drawn from the Emergent Strategic Reasoning Risks (ESRR) taxonomy, and a novel four-question binary reasoning framework synthesized from prior literature.
Our evaluation of 10 frontier models reveals a 62-percentage-point gap in misalignment across scenarios, with Gemini 3 Flash and Gemini 3.1 Pro exhibiting the highest levels of agentic misalignment while Claude Sonnet 4.6 displays near-zero rates across all conditions.
Our reasoning framework further reveals that models may exhibit harmful behaviours without explicit situational awareness or explanation, complicating both mitigation and detection.
AM-Bench scenarios and code are available at https://github.com/AI4Collaboration/Agentic-Misalignment-Bench
highlights: AM-Bench scenarios and code are available at https://github.com/AI4Collaboration/Agentic-Misalignment-Bench

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: IF-MAP: Influence-Function-Inspired Agent Prioritization in Multi-Agent Systems
papers.summary:
Improving every agent in an LLM-based multi-agent system can be prohibitively costly, making it important to identify which agent should be prioritized to achieve the greatest system-level gain with limited resources.
Failure attribution can inform this decision, but an agent's responsibility for failures does not directly reveal the system-level gains achievable by improving it.
We therefore introduce IF-MAP, an influence-function-inspired method for identifying agents with high potential for system-level improvement.
For each agent, IF-MAP measures end-to-end loss changes under controlled semantic prompt perturbations, fits a regularized local response model in a low-dimensional prompt-embedding subspace, and uses the estimated response norm as a priority score.
This black-box procedure requires no access to model parameters or gradients and produces agent priorities that can guide subsequent improvement effort.
We evaluate IF-MAP across six multi-agent workflows spanning code generation, question answering, and mathematical reasoning, using the same priorities for prompt optimization and model upgrades.
Optimizing the selected agents' prompts achieves a macro-average gain of 3.81 percentage points, compared with 1.85 for uniform agent selection.
Across five target models, upgrading the selected agents yields macro-average gains of 7.62-16.42 percentage points, compared with 3.81-8.62 for uniform agent selection.
Despite its probing overhead, IF-MAP reduces Qwen3-8B and DeepSeek-V3.2 token use by 74.2% and 35.2%, respectively, relative to optimizing every agent, and reduces target-model tokens by 63.6-64.9% relative to upgrading every agent.
These results support the use of IF-MAP to identify promising agents and direct improvement effort toward greater end-to-end performance gains.
highlights: We therefore introduce IF-MAP, an influence-function-inspired method for identifying agents with high potential for syst

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: One Skill Takes Over: Clashing Agent Skills and a One-File Fix
papers.summary:
Agent Skills are instruction files that tell a coding agent how to do one job.
Users install skills from many authors, so two skills for the same job can be active at the same time.
We ask what a model does when both skill files are in its context: does it combine their compatible rules, or follow one skill and drop the other?
We build SkillClash, 16 pairs of same-job skills in which code checks every rule and a reference output shows the best result that can be reached.
On seven models from five families, from 4B open models to Qwen3-235B and GPT-4.1, a skill's rules are followed 93 to 99% of the time when it is loaded alone and 61 to 62% when a same-job skill is loaded next to it.
Most outputs show takeover: every rule that only one skill asks for is followed, and every rule that only the other skill asks for is dropped.
The worked examples inside the skills drive this.
When each skill file instead ends with one example that follows both skills, takeover falls to 1 to 15% on the six models we tested.
Telling the model which skill has priority does not bring the dropped skill back, and telling it to apply both skills brings the dropped skill back only on the two strong models and leaves the interacting rules broken.
One merged skill file written by the strongest model we used, Claude Opus 5.5, lets all seven models follow 96 to 99% of the achievable rules.
Most of its gain over a plain list of both skills' rules comes from its one worked example, and such an example helps only when it is correct.
Code and data: https://github.com/prazmara/skillclash
highlights: Agent Skills are instruction files that tell a coding agent how to do one job.

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: EvalRx: Agentic Diagnosis and Verified Repair of Foundation Models
papers.summary:
Model evaluation reveals where models fail, but rarely why or whether a proposed fix genuinely works.
We introduce EvalRx, an open-source agentic framework for statistically grounded model diagnosis and repair.
EvalRx discovers systematic failure modes, explores candidate mechanisms, formulates falsifiable hypotheses, and verifies them by executing frozen, pre-specified tests before using supported diagnoses to guide tiered repair.
Candidate repairs are validated against the unchanged model and promoted only when they improve the target behavior without unacceptable regression.
Across language, vision-language, and audio-language settings spanning Gemini, Qwen, Gemma, and Nemotron, EvalRx improves performance in all 12 evaluated model family-modality combinations, with gains ranging from +1.4 to +10.9 percentage points (+5.8 points on average).
These results show that model evaluation can serve not only to measure failures, but to support an auditable process for diagnosing and repairing them.
highlights: Model evaluation reveals where models fail, but rarely why or whether a proposed fix genuinely works.

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: BetaMem: Learning to Remember a Changing World for Embodied Agents
papers.summary:
Long-horizon embodied agents face temporal confusion and incomplete or distorted records, recurring errors from fixed memory rules, and growing storage and retrieval costs.
We present BetaMem, a framework for building and evolving traceable long-term memory through six linked layers: working, spatial, entity, episodic, experiential, and procedural memory.
A dual-level write contract constrains operation executability and source support for content: supervised fine-tuning learns compliant memory operations, while reinforcement learning combines repeated sampling with teacher verification of the original observations to reward complete, accurate records and penalize omissions, distortion, and unsupported content.
We formulate failure-driven policy recursive self-improvement through diagnosis along the causal sequence of memory operations and local rule repairs gated by independent replay.
Atomic tools frame storage, updates, retrieval, and forgetting as cost-utility allocation under storage and read budgets.
Using the open-source Qwen3.5-9B model for memory generation, BetaMem achieves overall scores of 48.08% on M3-Bench-robot, 92.08% on LoCoMo, 72.6% on OpenEQA EM-EQA, and 62.4% on EgoLifeQA, the highest among the listed memory methods under their respective evaluation protocols.
Training the model for memory generation raises the contract pass rate from 50.9% to 86.2% while reducing output tokens per stored action by 47.3%.
A separate Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct evaluation on EMem-Bench achieves an average success rate of 38.4% and an average error recurrence rate of 24.9%.
We perform best among evaluated methods using comparably sized open-source models.
Category results show that we have advantages in integrating information across observations, recalling events over long histories, and inferring personal habits.
highlights: Atomic tools frame storage, updates, retrieval, and forgetting as cost-utility allocation under storage and read budgets

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: OR-License: Evaluating LLM Agents as Real-World Operations Research Practitioners
papers.summary:
Can large language model (LLM) agents deliver expert-level operations research (OR) solutions directly from original client materials, without prior expert reformulation?
Existing OR benchmarks typically begin with self-contained descriptions or predefined optimization tasks, underrepresenting the translation of original business materials into professionally validated solutions.
We introduce OR-License, an end-to-end benchmark of 31 instances across 10 industrial scenarios from paid OR engagements totaling USD 3.68 million.
It preserves original requirements, input data, deliverable formats, and information boundaries after de-identification.
To study information acquisition, we introduce ORSim, a controlled client simulator that discloses business facts without supplying OR expertise.
Hidden evaluation checks feasibility and compares objective quality against original expert solutions accepted by clients before benchmark construction.
Deployment-Adjusted Quality (DAQ) averages expert-relative quality across instances, assigning zero to infeasible deliveries.
Across 11 frontier LLMs using coding-agent harnesses, several exceed the expert reference in conditional objective quality, but none matches its DAQ; the strongest primary Claude Code configuration achieves 88.39% strict feasibility and a DAQ of 0.87 against the expert reference of 1.
Client information acquisition extends beyond clarification into solution development and validation, with some later stages showing higher confirmed issue-resolution proportions.
Trajectory analysis identifies formulation and implementation failures, while task-equalized research-chain completion rates range from 24% to 45% across models on evaluable tasks.
These findings motivate sustained information-gap resolution, faithful problem formulation, and evidence-linked self-improvement for reliable long-horizon agents.
highlights: exceed the expert reference in conditional objective quality

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: HTN-Orchestrate: A Hierarchical Task Network Framework for Multi-Agent Orchestration
papers.summary:
Orchestrating multiple agents on a complex task requires reconciling local subtask execution with global task planning.
Dynamic dispatch approaches provide execution flexibility but do not explicitly model subtask hierarchies or dependencies, while predefined workflows impose this structure but fix the decomposition before execution begins.
Therefore, we introduce HTN-Orchestrate, a two-layer framework that separates these responsibilities through a hierarchical task network (HTN).
The Planner maintains subtask hierarchies and dependencies, deferring decomposition until prerequisite results become available, while local Orchestrators schedule workers to execute each leaf subtask.
Results propagate upward under \textbf{AND} semantics, and accumulated findings inform a rebuilt task network when the current decomposition cannot resolve the task.
On five benchmarks spanning web research, scientific reasoning, and research workflows, HTN-Orchestrate outperforms ReAct, Agent Team, and DeepSeek Harness using the same base model, achieving 89.73% accuracy on BrowseComp and 73.44% on SUPERChem, exceeding Agent Team by 2.45 and 4.69 percentage points, respectively.

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: Agentic AI -- Physicist Collaboration in Experimental Particle Physics: A Proof-of-Concept Measurement with LEP Open Data
papers.summary:
We present an agentic measurement of the thrust distribution in $e^{+}e^{-}$ collisions at $\sqrt{s}=91.2$ GeV using ALEPH archived data.
This work was carried out through an AI agent-physicist collaboration, using interactive natural-language prompting of Anthropic Claude and OpenAI Codex.
Under physicist guidance, the agents wrote and executed all analysis code and drafted the majority of the text included in this paper.
A fully-corrected thrust spectrum is obtained via Iterative Bayesian Unfolding and Monte Carlo based corrections.
The principal contribution of this work is the demonstration of the agentic analysis, with thrust serving as a benchmark observable for the method.
Dedicated precision measurements of thrust are reported in the community elsewhere.
This work represents a step toward a theory-experiment loop in which AI agents assist with experimental measurements and theoretical calculations, and synthesize insights by comparing the results, thereby accelerating the cycle that drives discovery in fundamental physics.
Our work suggests that precision physics, leveraging the open LEP data and advanced theoretical landscape, provides an ideal testing ground for developing AI agent systems for scientific applications.
highlights: We present an agentic measurement of the thrust distribution in $e^{+}e^{-}$ collisions at $\sqrt{s}=91.2$ GeV using ALE

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: EditPPT: Structured Execution and Evaluation for Reliable Slide Editing
papers.summary:
Reliable slide editing requires precise modifications to intended objects while preserving the rest of the presentation.
We argue that slide editing is a problem of structured, constrained modification rather than open-ended code generation.
Despite the complexity of real presentations, editing requests can largely be decomposed into the objects to change, the operations to apply, and the state to preserve.
This perspective guides both evaluation and execution.
For evaluation, we introduce DeckEdit-Bench, 183 editing tasks on 28 human-authored decks whose target and preserved objects are annotated at the shape level, so that intended and unintended changes are scored mostly by deterministic rules.
For execution, we present EditPPT, a multi-agent framework that resolves targets before editing, restricts each specialist to a subset of 37 predefined tools, and validates each edit for instruction fulfillment and preservation, correcting or rolling back failed ones.
Across five backbone models, EditPPT reaches 66.7-74.9% Task Success while keeping Preservation above 97%.
Even with an open 27B model and no task-specific fine-tuning, it approaches Claude Code with Sonnet 5 in Task Success while better preserving the original deck.
These results suggest that constraining how edits are executed, not only model scale, makes slide editing more reliable.
highlights: Reliable slide editing requires precise modifications to intended objects while preserving the rest of the presentation.

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: Editing as Language: Teaching LLM Agents a Grammar for Native Context Editing
papers.summary:
A synopsis in novels folds a story into a few lines; a function in code gathers many steps with a single execution.
Context editing is native to language itself.
In this paper, we propose the Native Context Editing (NCE) framework, which gives language model agents a grammar for natively editing their own context.
By encoding context-editing operations in a grammar of dedicated special tokens, we teach the agents to invoke edits through the language itself.
We train agents on iteratively constructed trajectory segments, with each teacher edit conditioned on the evolving context.
This establishes context editing as an atomic and inherent capability of LLM agents, enabling them to dynamically modify their context as they generate responses over long-horizon reasoning and interaction.
Compared with context-editing methods that learn to generate tool-use code within specific external harness environments, our approach integrates context editing as an internal mechanism of the model's native generation process, enabling better generalization across diverse real-world workflows.
On four long-horizon agentic benchmarks (Terminal-Bench 2.0, SWE-bench Verified, SWE-bench Multilingual, and SWE-bench Pro), NCE improves the average task success rate over the base model by 5.6 percentage points for LongCat-Flash-Lite-Sparse and by 4.5 for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, while reducing average token usage by 36% and 15%, respectively.
highlights: propose the Native Context Editing (NCE) framework

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: Who Speaks, Who Authorizes, Who Acts? Understanding Trust Boundaries in Multi-Agent LLMs
papers.summary:
Multi-agent LLM systems exchange messages before acting through tools, but message delivery, signing authority, and tool-side enforcement are separate trust boundaries.
We represent them as communication, authorization, and execution structures, and use the authority cut to characterize the smallest independently compromised signer coalition that can construct a policy-valid false-claim proof under stated assumptions.
Controlled paired hidden-state studies reveal four distinctions.
First, no fixed-message routing contrast across four models meets the prespecified large-effect criterion; when relays rewrite messages, executed false-state action rates vary by model and route configuration.
Second, presented source-identity cues do not uniformly increase protected-action selection across three models.
Third, on invalid-proof cases, Nemotron and Llama request protected actions in 52.1% and 54.2% of trials, respectively, yet a deterministic tool gate commits none: request-level and commitment-level safety readouts diverge.
Finally, a separate single-model authorization check shows that a false claim with a policy-valid compromised-signer proof can pass the gate, since proof validity is not factual truth.
These findings motivate evaluating delivered information, qualified authorization, model proposals, and committed actions separately.
highlights: Who Speaks, Who Authorizes, Who Acts? Understanding Trust Boundaries in Multi
Controlled paired hidden-state studies reveal four distinctions.

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: fxBench: Evaluating and Understanding Formula Suggestions in Spreadsheets
papers.summary:
Spreadsheets are among the most widely used tools for computations, and formulas are their core building blocks.
Besides agentic spreadsheet tools, proactive formula suggestions enable significant productivity gains and are now available in popular spreadsheet software (Microsoft Excel and Google Sheets).
Such suggestions pose interesting challenges: the right context must be collected and represented for a machine learning model, which must then be able to write a correct formula, in a way that is fast and cheap enough to trigger on every = (or subsequent keystrokes for auto-completion) without taking users out of their editing flow.
Surprisingly, there is no public benchmark for formula suggestions on real spreadsheets.
In this paper, we therefore (1) introduce fxBench as a manually curated benchmark of 503 formula suggestion tasks based on Sheetpedia, (2) break down the formula suggestion problem into four capabilities (gather context, understand context, understand intent, write formula) that a formula suggestion system requires, and (3) evaluate existing and new approaches to understand bottlenecks in these capabilities that pose interesting research directions.
Specifically, we annotate each benchmark with the cells that describe intent to determine the theoretical performance limit of a given context selection strategy, we evaluate performance of small and large models on different representations of context, including a dense format with high theoretical coverage at low token counts, and we fine-tune smaller language models to show that we can learn to understand such dense formats.
Additionally, we perform quantitative and qualitative analysis on failure modes to understand bottlenecks in the formula writing capability; the best configuration only achieved 58.8% correct suggestions.
highlights: Spreadsheets are among the most widely used tools for computations, and formulas are their core building blocks.

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: Agentic Interpretation: Harness-Governed Evidence Construction for Software Agents
papers.summary:
Software agents answer behavioral questions about code, such as whether a patch passes tests or which lines caused a failure.
These tasks require repository-wide evidence, yet most scaffolds leave intermediate findings in free-form trajectories, making them hard to reuse and easy to disconnect from final answers.
We present Agentic Interpretation (AgInt), a framework for harness-governed evidence construction.
The model proposes typed records, while a deterministic harness admits, grades, and persists them, reports unresolved requirements, and licenses answers under task-specific rules.
The resulting certificate gives the model persistent external state and leaves an auditable decision record.
Formally, append-only certificate states form a grounding lattice ordered by record inclusion, where each admitted record extends the state by union.
We evaluate AgInt with four models on SWE-bench-Live and DeepSWE for patch acceptance and Defects4J and GitBug-Java for fault localization.
AgInt outperforms the plain agent and Agentic Code Reasoning on all reported patch-acceptance metrics and ranks responsible lines higher while inspecting fewer irrelevant lines in fault localization.
For GLM-5, reject-class F1 rises from 0.256 to 0.543 on SWE-bench-Live, All@1 rises from 0.140 to 0.400 on Defects4J, and wasted inspected lines fall from 31.5 to 11.7 on GitBug-Java.
A matched-template control separates the mechanism: the persistent scaffold drives most fault-localization gains, while the certificate body and gate govern patch-acceptance calibration.
With execution licensed, AgInt produces harness-reproduced witnesses for 293 of 475 null-dereference candidates versus 253 for a matched shell agent, and 62 of 117 resource-leak candidates versus 58.
Across reported efficiency measurements, it uses 35% fewer executions and reduces cost per candidate by 59%.
highlights: outperforms the plain agent and Agentic Code Reasoning on all reported patch-acceptance metrics and ranks responsible li

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: TempoMoE: Identifying and Steering Fast-Slow Thinking Experts for Efficient Multimodal Reasoning
papers.summary:
Multimodal Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) reasoning models rely on long chain-of-thought (CoT) for complex tasks, yet often overthink easy inputs, increasing token cost and latency, and sometimes degrading accuracy.
Existing methods optimize reasoning length during training or impose external control at inference, but leave the underlying reasoning mechanism a black box.
We find that fast and slow thinking exhibit distinct expert-routing patterns: holding the input fixed and varying only the prompted reasoning tempo produces stable routing shifts.
Suppressing slow-thinking experts shortens the reasoning chain, whereas suppressing fast-thinking experts lengthens it, providing causal evidence that these experts influence reasoning depth.
Based on this finding, we propose TempoMoE, a training-free, two-stage framework.
It identifies fast- and slow-thinking experts via tempo-contrastive routing analysis and redistributes routing weights within the original top-k set according to sample difficulty.
It amplifies fast-thinking experts and suppresses slow-thinking experts on easy inputs and reverses this adjustment on hard ones, enabling difficulty-adaptive control over reasoning depth.
We evaluate TempoMoE on Kimi-VL, Qwen3-VL, and ERNIE-4.5-VL across six benchmarks.
Compared with Vanilla, TempoMoE consistently improves accuracy while reducing output tokens, with accuracy gains of up to 2.6 points and token reductions of up to 35.4%.
highlights: Based on this finding, we propose TempoMoE, a training-free, two-stage framework.

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: OpenVLHarness: Real World Visual Agentic Tool-Use with Multimodal Memory
papers.summary:
Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have made rapid progress on visual reasoning, yet many tasks require evidence that is difficult to obtain through internal reasoning alone: our controlled study on 22 benchmarks shows that simply increasing the inference budget of the base model yields only modest gains.
Such tasks demand grounded perception, external knowledge, and numerical measurements obtained through heterogeneous tools, whose outputs must be made interpretable to the model and retained across reasoning steps.
We introduce OpenVLHarness, a multimodal reasoning harness organized around a capability layer and persistent multimodal memory.
The capability layer combines task-level tool interfaces with evidence rendering, providing consistent access to heterogeneous backends and converting their outputs into model-readable observations.
Persistent multimodal memory retains the corresponding images, structured data, and web references as addressable artifacts throughout each query.
A coding interface executes generated programs over stored data, enabling computations that combine results from multiple tools.
Together, these mechanisms support an iterative process of acquiring, inspecting, and composing multimodal evidence.
Evaluated on 22 benchmarks with eight open and proprietary backbones, OpenVLHarness improves average scores by 9.7-12.6 points over matched no-tool baselines, including +11.2 with Qwen3-VL-8B, +9.7 with Kimi K3, and +9.9 with GPT-6 Astra.
With GPT-6 Luna at medium reasoning effort, OpenVLHarness outperforms the base model, Codex, and Visual Sketchpad at maximum effort by 7.7-8.5 points while incurring at most 37% of their model-token cost.

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: Red-Teaming Multi-Agent Attacks for Loss-of-Control Risks
papers.summary:
AI agents are growing more capable and persistent, and are being deployed in ever larger numbers.
As more start collaborating, AI control measures must remain effective when they covertly collude on a harmful objective.
We introduce MiniLab, a synthetic series of live services and codebases (5 interconnected services, 249 benign tasks, 8 attack objectives), adapted from internal AI deployment infrastructure.
We demonstrate distributed attacks, in which different agents carry out separate attack fragments, and how their covertness evades frontier monitors when reading their trajectories individually.
We show how distributed attacks spread across diverse contexts and harmful objectives through 16 human-optimized attacks (weight exfiltration, unmonitored rogue deployment, permission elevation, and more).
A frontier monitor, GPT-5.6 Sol, reading each agent separately flags only 7% of successful distributed attacks, compared with 87% when a single agent carries out the same side task.
Individual attacks can also be composed into longer attack sequences toward a greater loss-of-control outcome, without any individual agent being flagged.
Finally, we tested whether models can plan these covert attacks: even with execution and monitor feedback, the best model-planned attacks succeed covertly against a single-trajectory GPT-5.6 Sol monitor in at most 25% of executions, compared with 80% for human-crafted plans, though this may scale with model capabilities.
By turning worst-case coordinated attacks into reproducible red-team cases, our work provides a foundation for preventing locally benign agent actions from accumulating into system-level loss of control.
highlights: AI agents are growing more capable and persistent, and are being deployed in ever larger numbers.

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: Muse Glimmer 30B: An On-Device Agentic Model
papers.summary:
We introduce Muse Glimmer, an open-source 30B parameter causal language model with perception encoder, purpose-built for autonomous agentic tasks on consumer hardware.
Muse Glimmer integrates multi-step reasoning, reliable tool use and failure recovery into a single model that runs locally on consumer devices without requiring cloud infrastructure.
The model accepts text and image inputs and produces text outputs, was trained on data from over a hundred languages, and is quantized to approximately 4-bit precision for efficient single-GPU inference.
Muse Glimmer achieves state-of-the-art performance for its size class on agentic benchmarks, setting a new standard compared to the models of its size: Gemma4-31B and Qwen3.6-27B on tool use, multi-step planning, and agentic task completion.
We release the model under the Apache 2.0 license to foster open-source development of capable, safe, local AI agents.
highlights: We release the model under the Apache 2.0 license to foster open-source development of capable, safe, local AI agents.

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: LVMH: A Meta-Optimization Harness for Long-Video Agent Memory
papers.summary:
Long-video agents must map hours or days of multimodal evidence into a bounded context while respecting token and latency budgets, making memory design a context-management challenge.
Existing memory systems largely rely on hand-designed policies, leaving open how to jointly optimize memory design for performance and efficiency.
We propose Long Video Meta-memory Harness (LVMH), an automated multi-agent framework that formulates memory-policy development as multi-objective code search around a fixed answer model.
To guard against self-certification and development-set overfitting, LVMH separates implementation from independent review and enforces protected observation boundaries.
Persistent meta-memory records past proposals, traces, costs, and failures to guide subsequent policy revisions.
Through this harness, we discover Self-Evolving Evidence Memory (SEEM), a "text-first, vision-second" policy that answers from compact structured event memory and evidence specialists, consulting localized frames through a selective visual gate.
The policy evolved on EgoLifeQA generalizes to unseen benchmarks, outperforming Meta-Harness on both Ego-R1 Bench and Video-MME (L) with GPT-5 mini.
Across the three benchmarks, SEEM with GPT-5 achieves 65.7% average accuracy, surpassing the previous state of the art by 7.7 percentage points with approximately 32x lower average evaluation token use and 91x shorter average response time.
highlights: outperforming Meta-Harness on both Ego-R1 Bench and Video-MME (L) with GPT-5 mini

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: Write Once, Query Many: Evolving Compact Reusable Memory for Long Videos
papers.summary:
Long videos often exceed the context capacity of multimodal large language models (MLLMs), while agentic search repeats costly video processing and grounding for each query.
Reusable memory can amortize this cost, but must preserve information for questions unknown during construction.
We propose Video-EMem, an evolvable video memory harness built on time-anchored perceptual observations.
This representation combines compact free-form text with sparse images to preserve semantic content and complementary visual details across temporal scales, supporting temporal navigation without a fixed semantic schema.
A Writer encodes each video once by consolidating overlapping multiscale observations, and a Reader retrieves and organizes evidence solely from the resulting memory.
With the underlying models frozen, we evolve their workflows and operators using distinct feedback: query-independent source fidelity and coverage for the Writer, and QA failures in evidence localization and utilization for the Reader.
Experiments support this separation for generalization beyond development queries, with our evolution strategy improving average accuracy by 7.2% over the unevolved harness.
While reducing storage by about 99.86% on average relative to raw videos, Video-EMem improves Qwen3-VL-30B by an average of 2.6% across three long-video QA benchmarks over direct input of 2,048 frames.
Using the same o3 answer model as the state-of-the-art agentic method, it improves average accuracy by 2.5% with lower per-query latency.
highlights: exceed the context capacity of multimodal large language models (MLLMs)

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: How Do Agentic LLMs Decide to Call Tools? A Tool-Call Vector Shaped by Suppression
papers.summary:
Tool calling, invoking external tools on demand, is central to agentic LLMs, yet the mechanism that decides whether a model calls a tool or responds directly remains poorly understood.
Agentic prompts are long and heavily scaffolded, combining role instructions, tool schemas, format templates, and the user's request across hundreds of tokens, creating a noisy, highly entangled context in which no single controllable variable for mechanistic analysis is obvious.
To obtain such a variable, we propose a method that converts complex agentic prompts into minimal contrastive pairs in which a single request verb determines the tool-call decision: replacing an execution-verb (e.g., \textit{write}) with an analysis-verb (e.g., \textit{discuss}) reliably flips the decision, suggesting it is mediated by a compact internal state.
We construct 500 such paired prompts across Python, Java, and C++ (300 for mechanistic analysis, 200 held out for evaluation).
We trace the decision to a vector, $\mu_\Delta$, that is both causally necessary and sufficient and generalizes beyond the discovery prompts to native multi-turn $\tau^2$-Bench trajectories and verb-free requests.
Behavioral ablations show that the scaffold establishes a tool-call prior; Transcoder decomposition then reveals that analysis verbs suppress this prior through features signaling that tool use is unnecessary, whereas execution verbs largely leave it intact.
Downstream scaffold-reading attention heads and MLP features read out the resulting state, and the same mechanism recurs across seven models from the Qwen, Mistral, and Granite families.
Our code is available at https://github.com/XijieGo/MI4ToolCalling.
highlights: How Do Agentic LLMs Decide to Call Tools? A Tool

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: Same Simulation, Different Evidence: Where Retrieved Tool Output Costs LLM Agents Accuracy
papers.summary:
LLM agents that compute the right answer can still answer wrongly.
Agent harnesses increasingly keep long tool outputs out of the context window, saving them to files that the agent searches or reads on demand.
We ask where this costs accuracy with a real scientific tool: PHREEQC, a widely used geochemistry simulator from the USGS, whose reports reach 846.8k characters and whose determinism lets every printed value be traced.
Agents use it to answer 158 execution-verified multiple-choice items.
When agents read the simulator's report through a section index rather than in context, GPT-5.1 and GPT-5.2 lose 11.3 and 7.9 points of accuracy, while Claude Opus 4.6 and Claude Sonnet 4.6 show no detectable cost.
Re-running all 11,007 logged simulator calls shows that both GPT models compute the keyed value about as often as before; what changes is the evidence they answer from.
Under retrieval they often skip the report, answer from their own higher-precision output files, and misround to a neighboring option, a failure we call evidence substitution.
With the simulation held fixed, retrieval still costs GPT-5.2 9.4 points.
For GPT-5.4, more frequent correct simulations mask an evidence-use loss of about ten points, leaving a net change indistinguishable from zero.
Naming the authoritative output raises accuracy by 6.3-7.9 points over plain retrieval for the three GPT models; for GPT-5.1 and GPT-5.2, inlining outputs that fit works as well, while asking for correct rounding does not.
Context-management choices in agent harnesses should be judged by where accuracy is lost, not only by final accuracy.
highlights: LLM agents that compute the right answer can still answer wrongly.

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Web Agent Agentic Reinforcement Learning Decision Model Under Multi-Cost and Failure Risk
papers.summary:
Intelligent agent interactions in real-world web environments are commonly constrained by request budgets, time delays, anti-crawling restrictions, and operational failure risks. 现实Web环境中的智能代理交互通常受到请求预算、时间延迟、反爬网限制和操作故障风险的限制。
Strategies solely optimizing task success rates often exhibit unusable phenomena such as "high success but high cost" or "low risk but conservative failure." This paper proposes a constrained agentic reinforcement learning model for web agents, unifying page access, search requests, and external API calls into a unified long-term decision-making framework with associated costs. 仅优化任务成功率的策略通常表现出不可用的现象，例如“高成功但高成本”或“低风险但保守的失败”。“本文提出了一种用于Web代理的约束代理强化学习模型，将页面访问、搜索请求和外部API调用统一到具有相关成本的统一长期决策框架中。
It simultaneously incorporates cost budget constraints and tail risk control into the optimization objective: constructing a multidimensional cost vector comprising cumulative request count, total latency, and failure penalties to achieve budget compliance via Lagrange dual updates, while employing a CVaR risk term to suppress excessive exploration of high-failure-probability paths, thereby achieving an adaptive balance among "completion rate, cost, and risk."
  Experiments were conducted across 30-70 site/page templates and 800-1,500 end-to-end web tasks, including information extraction, price comparison, form submission, and cross-page navigation.
Interaction sequences spanned 20-120 steps with tool scales of 30-200. 交互序列跨越20-120个步骤，工具尺度为30-200。
Performance was benchmarked against unconstrained RL, budget-constrained RL, and rule-based/scripted web agents, quantifying task completion rates, cost-per-success, failure rates, and policy stability. 根据不受约束的RL、预算受限的RL和基于规则/脚本的Web代理对性能进行基准测试，量化任务完成率、每次成功成本、失败率和策略稳定性。
Results demonstrate that at equivalent completion rates, our method reduces C-PS by 22%-31% and lowers failure rates by 18%-26% under high failure penalties. 结果表明，在相同的完成率下，我们的方法在高故障罚款下可将C-PS降低22% -31% ，并将故障率降低18% -26%。
Under fixed budgets, task completion rates increase by 10%-16%, highlighting the necessity and effectiveness of constraint modeling for practical web agent deployment. 在固定预算下，任务完成率提高10% -16% ，凸显了约束建模在实际Web代理部署中的必要性和有效性。
highlights: Web Agent Agentic Reinforcement Learning Decision Model Under Multi

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Trackable Skill Library Lifecycle Management for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary:
Skill-augmented agentic RL has emerged as an effective approach to improving LLM agents on long-horizon tasks. 技能增强型代理强化学习已成为改进长期任务LLM代理的有效方法。
Despite this progress, individual skills may follow distinct trajectories as the policy evolves, with some becoming redundant after the model internalizes their capabilities, others remaining valuable as external scaffolding, and still others turning harmful. 尽管取得了这一进展，但随着政策的演变，个人技能可能会遵循不同的轨迹，其中一些技能在模型内化其能力后变得多余，另一些技能作为外部支架仍然具有价值，还有一些技能变得有害。
However, existing skill library systems fail to identify each skill's true contribution due to free-riding among co-retrieved skills, difficulty confounding across tasks, and the absence of skill-specific counterfactual evidence, which prevents reliable skill lifecycle management. 然而，现有的技能库系统由于在共同检索的技能之间搭便车、难以混淆任务以及缺乏特定技能的反事实证据而无法识别每项技能的真正贡献，这阻碍了可靠的技能生命周期管理。
We propose TrackRL, an agentic RL framework where skill tracking drives skill library full lifecycle management. 我们提出了TrackRL ，这是一个代理式RL框架，其中技能跟踪驱动技能库的整个生命周期管理。
Specifically, within each GRPO group, we turn grouped sampling into online randomized controlled experiments. 具体而言，在每个GRPO组中，我们将分组抽样转化为在线随机对照实验。
Independent random injection and within-group contrasts on the same task isolate each skill's true contribution, and reliability-weighted aggregation accumulates evidence across groups. 同一任务的独立随机注射和组内对比隔离了每项技能的真正贡献，可靠性加权聚合积累了跨组证据。
As evidence accumulates, we continuously track skill utility, which measures the skill's causal contribution as external scaffolding, and model mastery, which reflects how far the corresponding capability has been internalized. 随着证据的积累，我们不断跟踪技能效用，将技能的因果关系作为外部支架来衡量，以及模型掌握，这反映了相应能力的内化程度。
Along this line, we formulate skill lifecycle management as an evidence-gated state-transition process that governs each skill from generation and admission through protected incubation to retention, retirement, or removal, while a soft capacity bound controls library growth. 沿着这一思路，我们将技能生命周期管理制定为一个循证门控的状态转换过程，从生成和录取到受保护的孵化到保留、退休或移除，管理每个技能，而软容量绑定控制库增长。
Experiments show that TrackRL outperforms recent skill-augmented RL baselines in both library-assisted and skill-free evaluation, with further analyses revealing how skill value shifts during policy learning and how evidence-driven state transitions shape skill library evolution. 实验表明， TrackRL在图书馆辅助和无技能评估方面都优于最近的技能增强RL基线，进一步分析揭示了政策学习过程中技能价值的转变以及循证驱动的状态转变如何影响技能库的演变。
Our code is available at https://github.com/xizhu1022/TrackRL. 我们的代码可在https://github.com/xizhu1022/TrackRL上找到。
highlights: outperforms recent skill-augmented RL baselines in both library-assisted and skill-free evaluation
Skill-augmented agentic RL has emerged as an effective approach to improving LLM agents on long-horizon tasks.

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: MELD: Recursive Self-Improvement via Hierarchical Coordination for Multi-Agent Scientific Discovery
papers.summary:
Multi-agent scientific discovery with large language models raises a coupled learning problem: research assignments determine both which experiments are pursued and the experiences from which agents adapt.
We introduce MELD, a unified hierarchical test-time training framework that jointly adapts a team-level Coordinator policy and agent-level individual Scientist policies within a single discovery process.
The Coordinator generates a joint portfolio of search branches and research directives over a shared derivation tree, while Scientists develop hypotheses and execution plans implemented by a shared frozen Executor.
Both levels receive alternating GRPO-style parameter updates under a shared smooth best-of-budget objective, allowing team organization and individual research behavior to co-evolve in a recursive self-improvement loop.
Our analysis establishes objective alignment for the hierarchy, characterizes conditions for coordination gains over independent parallel discovery and the first-order benefit of private adaptation, and derives a finite-budget regret bound for adapted models.
On 22 MLGym and MLE-bench tasks, MELD is best on 20 of them and achieves the highest aggregate normalized scores on MLGym, using a 4B backbone for coordination and research.
Most baselines use proprietary Scientists, and all systems share one frozen Executor.
highlights: Most baselines use proprietary Scientists, and all systems share one frozen Executor.

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Hyper Algorithm Design Agent: Evolving Learnable Optimizer from Zero
papers.summary:
Meta-Black-Box Optimization (MetaBBO) is one of the highlights in the recent AI for Optimization trend.
This paradigm's bi-level workflow leverages the learnable algorithm design policy at meta level to ensure the performance and generalization improvement on the low-level optimization task.
While MetaBBO helps advance the performance lower bound of the resulted optimization system, it is currently handcrafted and customized case by case to adapt different optimization problems, which inevitably introduces inherent subjectivity and hence restricts the performance upper bound and usability in practice.
In this paper, we address this issue by regarding MetaBBO's design loop as coding task, where we could introduce openendedness into MetaBBO with recursive self-improvement capability of advanced coding agents.
Specifically, we propose a dual-agent framework: i) a task agent continuously refines the codebase of a target MetaBBO approach through code evolution; ii) a hyper agent progressively modifies the task agent and itself to provide open-ended design behavior; iii) the evolved MetaBBO codebase is evaluated and all in-execution information is fed back to the agents for recursive self-referential improvement.
As a result, given a naive MetaBBO template, our framework automates a design evolution and finds novel variants superior to up-to-date human-made MetaBBO baselines.
Surprisingly, the experimental results also demonstrate that our framework supports fast adaption across different optimization domains.
Solid interpretation analysis further reveals interesting design principles emerge in such open-ended process.
This work serves as the first exploration on automating design of complex learning-assisted optimization algorithms.
highlights: first exploration on automating design of complex learning-assisted optimization algorithms
Meta-Black-Box Optimization (MetaBBO) is one of the highlights in the recent AI for Optimization trend.

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: World of SWECraft: Agent Collaboration at Scale via Simulated Software Worlds
papers.summary:
As teams of AI agents take on larger projects and long-standing open problems, agent collaboration offers another dimension for scaling inference-time compute.
To understand what makes such collaboration effective and scalable, we develop Software World, a framework for simulating multi-agent coworking in realistic software ecosystems.
It comes with a pipeline to create environments of real, interdependent Python packages of different topics, sizes, and dependency structures, which we call software worlds.
In a simulation, agents maintain packages in the world with a high-level goal of improving software efficiency, and they are free to discover tasks to work on and collaborate with others.
We evaluate agents' work in a world collectively by measuring speedup in hidden dependent packages.
The framework allows us to study different elements of collaboration by varying communication, ownership, and resource allocation.
We run simulations in three different worlds, totaling more than 10,000 hours of agent work across eight models.
Overall, performance improvement scales with inference-time compute, with the best model improving downstream efficiency by up to 31%.
We show that most agents can find meaningful tasks via collaboration, but some frontier models can prematurely stop looking for improvements and make little progress.
We release the simulation framework and traces to support future studies of agent collaboration at https://szj.io/sw.
highlights: We evaluate agents' work in a world collectively by measuring speedup in hidden dependent packages.

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Hippo: Training-Free Agent Self-Evolution via Hippocampal Replay
papers.summary:
Motivated by recursive self-improvement (RSI), we study how LLM agents can learn through external memory without updating model parameters.
Extracting useful experience from a single attempt is difficult: flawed reasoning can produce success, while poor execution can obscure a sound strategy.
Preserving its value over time is also difficult: our accumulation baseline without consolidation initially improves but eventually performs below a no-memory baseline.
Our key idea is to compare attempts at the same task to identify reusable decisions and refine when they apply.
We introduce Hippo, a memory framework inspired by selective hippocampal encoding and replay that learns from these comparisons when shortcomings are diagnosed.
It compares the resulting experience with existing memory to merge overlaps and resolve conflicts through explicit applicability conditions.
This allows prior guidance to be revised without storing every lesson as a separate entry.
Experiments on SWE-bench Verified, WebArena, and Mind2Web show performance gains in all three settings and substantially fewer retained experiences than the accumulation baseline.
The gains extend across the evaluated base models of varying capabilities, indicating that memory-based adaptation remains useful even for highly capable models.
highlights: Motivated by recursive self-improvement (RSI), we study how LLM agents can learn through external memory without updatin

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: EMMA: Event-Driven Multimodal Memory System with Multi-Agent Retrieval
papers.summary:
Long video understanding requires reasoning over hours of content that far exceed the context window of multimodal large language models (MLLMs).
Existing approaches compress video into fixed-length clips, yet events are fragmented and unrelated content is merged, yielding noisy retrieval.
To overcome this challenge, we propose EMMA, an Event-driven Multimodal Memory system with Multi-Agent retrieval, which organizes memory around semantic events in three stages: (1) Event segmentation: a dual-stream detector adaptively locates event boundaries by fusing visual semantic drift with spoken transitions, rather than fixed windows.
(2) Memory construction: built on the detected events, a three-level hierarchy of raw video, clip-level memory, and event-level memory stores content at progressively higher semantic abstraction.
(3) Memory retrieval: a multi-agent framework collaboratively queries this hierarchy through query decomposition, tiered search, evidence validation, and answer generation, narrowing evidence from coarse events to precise clips.
Extensive experiments on three challenging benchmarks demonstrate substantial improvements, showing the effectiveness of our event-aligned memory system.
Code, prompt templates, and reproduction scripts are available at https://github.com/BAI-LAB/EMMA.
highlights: exceed the context window of multimodal large language models (MLLMs)

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: KernelClaw: A Multi-Agent Framework for GPU Kernel Optimization with Dual-Memory Mechanisms
papers.summary:
Improving GPU kernel efficiency is crucial for efficient AI systems.
Recent work has explored leveraging large language models (LLMs) for GPU kernel generation and optimization.
However, existing LLM-based kernel optimization pipelines typically rely on opaque, implicitly learned heuristics within the LLMs to determine optimization strategies.
This leads to inefficient trial-and-error and weakly interpretable optimizations.
Our key insight is to replace implicit heuristics with expert optimization knowledge that is aware of task trajectories.
Specifically, we present KernelClaw, a multi-agent framework with a dual-level memory architecture.
KernelClaw operates by coordinating agents with long-term memory of reusable expert knowledge and short-term memory to prevent repetitive backtracking.
On KernelBench Levels 1-3, KernelClaw achieves a 100% success rate and average speedups of 6.98x, 7.89x, and 1.94x over Torch Eager on Levels 1, 2, and 3, respectively, outperforming prior baselines.
Code is available at https://github.com/0satan0/KernelMem/.

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: TimelineAgent: An LLM-based Framework for Query-Centric Event Timeline Extraction Across Multiple Documents
papers.summary:
Query-centric cross-document event timeline extraction aims to construct event timelines from multiple documents under diverse query focuses.
The task is very challenging due to the heterogeneous event modeling and reasoning requirements arising from both the intrinsic complexity of cross-document timeline construction and the diversity of query focuses.
In this paper, we propose TimelineAgent, an LLM-based multi-agent framework featuring a multi-stage reasoning workflow, where heterogeneous event features are organized into reusable skills and orchestrated through a goal-oriented protocol.
To facilitate evaluation, we construct a benchmark covering diverse query focuses.
Experimental results show that TimelineAgent consistently outperforms existing methods, offering a practical framework for complex real-world timeline construction.

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Reflection-Driven Self-Improving Language Model Agents for Adaptive RAN Slicing
papers.summary:
Adaptive control in AI-native networks remains challenging because tasks such as dynamic Radio Access Network (RAN) slicing require persistent trade-off decisions among spectrum efficiency, service quality, and reconfiguration stability.
Conventional Reinforcement Learning (RL) compresses these competing objectives into handcrafted scalar rewards, requiring exhaustive tuning for a balanced trade-off.
Language model (LM) agents provide a new path toward adaptive control because they can semantically represent complex preference relations, but prompt-based adaptation struggles to retain long-horizon interaction history due to finite context limits.
We propose a Reflection-Driven Self-Improvement (ReDSI) framework that replaces scalar rewards with semantic feedback for continuous policy adaptation.
This framework is built upon a Small Language Model (SLM) agent for fast decision-making, coupled with a bi-perspective reflection to transform interaction history into preference data, subsequently distilling long-horizon decision experience into the SLM parameters through preference-based fine-tuning.
Evaluated on a dynamic RAN slicing task, our method achieves an optimal trade-off across multiple competing objectives, outperforming standard RL baselines and existing LM-based agents by demonstrating substantially greater sample efficiency.
These results highlight a viable paradigm of self-improving LM agents for reward-free multi-objective continuous control in AI-native networks.
highlights: outperforming standard RL baselines and existing LM-based agents by demonstrating substantially greater sample efficienc
These results highlight a viable paradigm of self-improving LM agents for reward-free multi-objective continuous control

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Memory as Belief: Bayesian Evolution of Memory for Self-Evolving LLM Agents
papers.summary:
Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly rely on external memory to accumulate past experiences for continual adaptation.
However, effectively reusing memory requires accurately assessing its value, as retrieved experiences may become unreliable when transferred across task contexts.
Despite its importance, memory valuation remains largely underexplored, with existing methods relying on historical retrieval success rates that overlook the context dependency of memory usefulness and the varying reliability of estimates under different amounts of evidence.
Inspired by the Bayesian brain hypothesis, we propose BEAM (Bayesian-style Evolutionary Agentic Memory), a framework that reformulates memory value evaluation as a parameterized cognitive inference process, where memory value is represented as a context-conditioned dynamic belief rather than a passive historical statistic.
Specifically, BEAM infers memory value beliefs from current task contexts and continuously calibrates them using execution feedback as empirical evidence, transforming memory from passive storage into an adaptive cognitive mechanism for continual self-evolution.
Extensive experiments across reasoning and code generation benchmarks demonstrate that BEAM consistently improves memory utilization and enables continual self-evolution of LLM agents.
highlights: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly rely on external memory to accumulate past experiences for continual adap

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: How Data Scales in Agentic Reinforcement Learning: Laws and Synthesis Strategies
papers.summary:
Pretraining scaling laws treat training data as a one-dimensional quantity: a token count.
Agentic reinforcement learning (RL) inherits this scalar abstraction, but modern synthesis pipelines now generate \textit{tasks}, \textit{environments}, and \textit{trajectories} independently and at very different costs, turning data into a structured design space.
This raises a question pretraining never had to answer: given a synthesis budget, \textit{which axis} should be scaled?
We address this question end-to-end with three tightly coupled contributions.
First, we decompose agentic data into three cardinality axes (task, environment, trajectory), plus a reward-density control variable, and fit per-axis scaling relations on different large language models (LLMs) across math+code, SWE, web, and UI/tool application domains.
Across all model sizes, model families, domains, and RL algorithms (PPO and GRPO) we measured, the scaling exponents order as environment $>$ task $>$ trajectory.
When environment diversity is decomposed into world and environment-structure diversity, its advantage is mainly driven by the former, while the latter is just comparable to the task diversity.
Second, we use the fitted laws as a common ruler to price synthesis methods, capturing each method's efficiency as a per-axis discount factor and identifying critical synthetic-to-real ratios at which collapse begins; these ratios differ by an order of magnitude across axes.
Third, we cast budget allocation as a constrained optimization under our laws and discounts, deriving a Chinchilla-style compute-optimal recipe and validating it at held-out scale.
The empirical results demonstrate that following the recipe yields up to $1.7\times$ compute efficiency over the dominant ``scale-the-trajectories'' practice.
highlights: How Data Scales in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
Pretraining scaling laws treat training data as a one-dimensional quantity: a token count.

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Janus: a Playground for User-Involved Agentic Permission Management
papers.summary:
AI agents that autonomously execute tool calls on a user's behalf raise pressing questions about permission management: what role could users play, and what role should they play?
Despite many proposed approaches, the user's role in agentic permission management remains underexplored.
We introduce Janus, a playground system for implementing and evaluating user-involved agentic permission management designs.
Janus consists of two components: Janus-Core, a modular agentic system supporting a diverse spectrum of permission management designs, and Janus-Harness, an automated evaluation framework.
Grounded in a conceptual model that identifies key design axes for user involvement, we implement six permission assistants spanning the design space and evaluate them across three scenarios with four subscenarios each and three synthetic responders.
We demonstrate that user involvement is critical and can strengthen privacy and security and that user behavior such as permission fatigue must be accounted for in system design.
No single design performs optimally across all contexts, motivating a more principled and context-sensitive approach to deploying permission assistants in agentic systems.
Janus is publicly available to support future investigation into this dimension of agentic system design.
highlights: Despite many proposed approaches, the user's role in agentic permission management remains underexplored.

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Mobius Injection: From One-Shot Prompt Injection to Sustained Resource Exhaustion in AI Agent Infrastructure
papers.summary:
Large Language Model (LLM) agents have emerged as key intermediaries, orchestrating complex interactions between human users and a wide range of digital services and LLM infrastructures.
While prior research has extensively examined the security of LLMs and agents in isolation, the systemic risk of the agent acting as a disruptive "hub" within the user-agent-service chain remains largely overlooked.
In this work, we expose a novel threat paradigm by introducing Mobius Injection, a sophisticated attack that weaponizes autonomous agents into zombie nodes to launch what we define as Agent-based and -Oriented DDoS (AbO-DDoS) attacks.
Mobius Injection composes known indirect prompt injection and persistent agent components through a distinct structural mechanism named Semantic Closure, which induces sustained recursive execution of agent components through a single injection event.
We demonstrate that this attack is lightweight for the adversary, can evade traditional volumetric DDoS monitors and input filters calibrated for low false-positive rates, and is highly configurable, allowing for surgical targeting of specific environments or model providers.
To evaluate the real-world impact, we conduct extensive experiments across three representative claw-style agents and three mainstream coding agents, integrated with 12 frontier proprietary or open-weight LLMs.
Our results demonstrate that Mobius Injection achieves substantial attack success across diverse tasks, driving single-node call amplification up to 51.0x.
Under coordinated multi-node pressure, each infected node still drains about 123k--127k tokens on a shared five-GPU backend; benign request latency rises by abou 23x--24x, and coordinated infections eventually saturate shared capacity until benign traffic is effectively denied service.

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: SCARCE: Emergent Institutions in Long-Horizon Multi-Agent Coding Systems
papers.summary:
As autonomous agents become widely deployed, coordinating access to shared computing resources and services will become increasingly important.
Recent incidents have already revealed unplanned coordination between agents, highlighting the safety implications of these interactions.
Yet prior studies of agent negotiation often use stylized games and simulated bargaining, leaving open how these behaviors develop during sustained, long-horizon tasks.
We propose SCARCE (Shared Compute ARena for Coding agEnts), a framework in which agents solve sequences of coding tasks under individual deadlines while negotiating access to a shared execution resource.
This negotiation determines when and for how long they can inspect programs, compile code, and run tests.
We find that agents spontaneously develop informal institutions: persistent rules and commitments grounded in reputation, reciprocity, and precedent.
These arrangements, which we call institutional behaviors, carry across tasks and influence resource allocation, with agents sometimes forgoing immediate advantages to honor earlier agreements.
We develop a 21-category taxonomy of negotiation strategies and emergent norms and use it to analyze eight models and audit more than 1,500 trajectories across different environmental settings.
Among the models tested, newer frontier models exhibit more institutional behaviors than older or lightweight models.
Alongside cooperation, we observe exclusionary coalitions and rare divide-and-conquer strategies.
SCARCE provides a controlled setting for proactively and systematically auditing how these relationships emerge, shape access to resources, and affect the safety and coordination of multi-agent systems.
highlights: As autonomous agents become widely deployed, coordinating access to shared computing resources and services will become

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Conjugate Compilation: Self-Improving Agentic Co-Compilation for Speculative Decoding
papers.summary:
As LLM adoption surges, scaling model serving requires unlocking stranded GPU capacity alongside deploying more GPUs.
Speculative decoding brings two models into the serving process: a small draft model proposes tokens that a larger target model verifies.
Yet compiling these models individually leaves their shared execution outside the compiler's optimization boundary.
We introduce CONJUGATE COMPILATION, which reframes speculative decoding as a cross-model compilation problem and jointly optimizes the draft and target models within their shared execution rather than treating each in isolation.
Our key insight is that cross-model compilation should be informed by the measured performance of the co-located shared execution it produces: an optimization that improves a kernel in isolation need not improve the models when they execute together.
To expand cross-model opportunities, we devise operand layouts that interleave blocks from both models within common tiles, co-locating GEMM and non-GEMM work while preserving their mathematics.
We realize CONJUGATE COMPILATION through a self-improving agentic search system in which an LLM edits cross-model optimization plans using the compiler and GPU execution as its environment.
Each proposed plan is compiled and evaluated through its co-located shared execution, whose measured score, together with kernel-level verdicts and compiler feedback, informs subsequent proposals, while Monte Carlo tree search accumulates rewards to guide exploration.
Across six single-GPU speculative-decoding configurations on NVIDIA B300 and RTX 5090 GPUs, CONJUGATE COMPILATION achieves a geometric-mean per-round speedup of 1.37x over conventional execution.
Interleaved kernels raise this speedup to 1.45x, reaching 1.59x in the best case.
CONJUGATE COMPILATION also improves GPU utilization on average by 1.46x on RTX 5090 and 1.50x on B300.
highlights: As LLM adoption surges, scaling model serving requires unlocking stranded GPU capacity alongside deploying more GPUs.

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: MASIF: Implicit Failures for Process Observability in Multi-Agent Systems
papers.summary:
Multi-agent systems (MAS) can complete a task despite local execution errors that are corrected, bypassed, or carried forward without individually determining its outcome.
We call these implicit failures (IFs) and study them as signals for process observability beyond final task outcome.
Across 1,828 traces from nine MAS-benchmark configurations, IFs occur in 54.3% of successful and 75.2% of failed traces.
We develop taxonomies of error types and subsequent absorption mechanisms, supported by human and cross-model annotation audits.
Counterfactual replay further probes how repairing an IF changes the final outcome.
To examine the practical value of IFs, we evaluate IF-based best-of-N trace selection against existing process reward models, and introduce a novel RL algorithm, IF-GRPO, that uses IF costs to refine preferences among successful trajectories in GRPO.
Experiments show that IF-GRPO exhibits some gains in accuracy and process metrics.
Importantly, it exposes trade-offs between task performance, IF count and cost, and token-normalized IF density.
Overall, our results show that IFs provide complementary process observability into how MAS reach their outcomes, including error recovery, propagation, and IF-based process differences that final task success alone does not expose.

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: StebBench: Diagnosing Real-World Procedural Understanding in AI Agents
papers.summary:
Evaluating an agent's planning ability remains challenging for open-domain tasks, where verifying procedures through execution is often impractical.
Existing evaluations typically assess only the final plan and do not distinguish procedural errors such as missing, incorrect, or misordered actions.
We introduce STEPBENCH, a benchmark of 6,885 verified procedures crawled from wikiHow across 81 open-domain categories.
From each procedure, we derive 5 diagnostic tasks: four with deterministic answers involving withheld, incorrect, or shuffled steps, and one requiring next-step generation.
We additionally evaluate full-plan generation to examine how diagnostic performance correlates with end-to-end plan validity.
Using the same procedures across tasks lets us directly compare different planning capabilities.
For generation, STEPEVAL identifies critical failures that prevent goal completion.
Across 14 configurations of 12 models, we find substantial differences across planning capabilities, with step ordering proving the most difficult: the strongest model correctly orders only 63.0% of procedures, dropping to 33.1% for those with nine or more steps.
Incorrect-step detection also predicts judged plan validity across models, suggesting a lower-cost alternative for evaluating generation quality.
On STEPBENCH-Val, comprising 214 procedures published in 2026, comprehension scores and rankings remain stable, suggesting limited influence from memorisation.
highlights: Evaluating an agent's planning ability remains challenging for open-domain tasks, where verifying procedures through exe

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: InfraBench: Evaluating Infrastructure Agents Across Layers, Lifecycle, and Risk
papers.summary:
Managing modern computing infrastructure has become a steadily harder problem due to the ever-increasing complexity.
Recent advances in AI agents create a timely opportunity to automate infrastructure management tasks, but it remains unclear how well such agents can handle real-world infrastructure complexity.
We present InfraBench, a benchmark for infrastructure agents organized around system layers, the operational lifecycle, and risk.
The current prototype couples container, VM, and bare-metal backends with task-specific verifiers that distinguish functional repair from durability and cleanup, and analyzes retained action-trace findings for unsafe shortcuts.
We evaluate 18 agent-model configurations on 12 seed tasks, with three attempts per task.
Mean effective scores range from 45.5% to 89.2%; the strongest configuration completes 77.8% of attempts perfectly.
In the available lifecycle checks, pass rates fall from 91.5% for functional repair to 80.9% for durability and 38.9% for cleanup.
These results show why immediate recovery is an incomplete measure of operational capability.
We use this evidence to motivate a planned expansion toward 40-60 tasks centered on managed cloud infrastructure and redesign after incidents, including provider-native Kubernetes networking.
This extension is a research direction; the reported results remain those of the 12-task prototype.
InfraBench, its tasks, evaluation harness, and live leaderboard are available at infraben.ch.
highlights: Managing modern computing infrastructure has become a steadily harder problem due to the ever-increasing complexity.

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: VACS: Value-Aligned Compositional Shielding for Multi-Agent Reasoning
papers.summary:
Multi-agent reasoning systems in high-stakes domains must be both accurate and safe, yet agents often follow heterogeneous value priorities (e.g., rigor, conciseness, safety), causing conflicting recommendations.
Existing methods do not jointly provide: (i) principled inference of each agent's implicit values from behavior, (ii) compositional formal safety guarantees without full online communication, and (iii) value-aware conflict resolution with faithful explanations.
We present VACS (Value-Aligned Compositional Shielding), a four-layer framework addressing all three.
Layer 1 learns value-dimension rewards from pairwise preferences using Bradley-Terry modeling and infers per-agent value weights via deep MaxEnt IRL.
Layer 2 encodes value constraints in a Lean-inspired DSL and synthesizes compositional assume-guarantee shields for runtime safety.
Layer 3 resolves disagreement through nucleolus-based credit allocation and Hamiltonian consensus optimization under long-term value constraints.
Layer 4 extracts a critical reasoning path from co-state sensitivities and generates formally grounded natural-language explanations.
Our contribution is primarily a unified systems design with formalized interfaces and operational guarantees at the verifier-constrained decision level, rather than a complete end-to-end formal proof of all language-model internals.
In controlled proof-of-concept evaluations with role-conditioned agent panels on NEJM-AI QA, MathInstruct-Subset, and a cybersecurity incident-response benchmark (CyberSec-Eval), VACS outperforms strong baselines in accuracy (85.4%, 95.0%, and 90.0%) while reducing logical inconsistency rates to near zero.

featuredPapers.title: VideoHarness-SRSI: Structured Recursive Self-Improvement for Video Understanding Harness
featuredPapers.authors: Zihao Lin, Haoyu Dong, Haobo Xu
featuredPapers.summary:
LLM system capabilities depend not only on model parameters but also on the executable harnesses that organize information acquisition, tool use, reasoning, and memory. LLM系统功能不仅取决于模型参数，还取决于组织信息采集、工具使用、推理和内存的可执行线束。
