papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: Cross-Dialect Generalization Without Retraining: Benchmarks and Evaluation of Schema-Derived Constrained Decoding for MLIR
papers.summary:
Multi-Level Intermediate Representation (MLIR) underlies modern ML compiler infrastructure (TensorFlow, JAX/StableHLO, PyTorch Inductor, IREE), yet appears only in trace amounts in code-LM pretraining corpora.
MLIR is also extensible by design: new dialects ship per application domain, so a fine-tuned model per dialect does not scale.
We ask whether inference-time priors derived mechanically from each dialect's Operation Definition Specification (ODS) can substitute for gradient-based adaptation.
First, we release four natural-language-to-MLIR benchmarks across three dialects (MLIR-Spec-150, Linalg-Spec-30, StableHLO-Spec-30, StableHLO-Held-Out-200), totaling 410 in-scope NL-to-MLIR pairs, plus a 25-program out-of-grammar stress set, with functional references on 30 Spec prompts, under Apache-2.0 with Gebru datasheets and Croissant 1.1 metadata.
Second, we build a three-layer schema-derived constraint stack: a CFG over op signatures (C1), type-domain splits from an ODS-extracted type lattice (C2), and an SSA-scope validator driving five-retry rejection sampling (C3).
Porting it to StableHLO required no new constraint-layer code.
On structurally dominated dialects, SmolLM2-1.7B with token-level constraints matches or exceeds 15B-34B code LMs running post-hoc rejection at a matched retry budget and 8-25x the per-generation speed: on linalg it reaches 80.0% verify-valid (three runs, n=125), 21 to 44 pp above CodeLlama-34B, Granite-Code-34B, and StarCoder2-15B with non-overlapping CIs.
The comparison is between systems, not models: under the baselines' post-hoc protocol, SmolLM2 falls from 52.0% to 24.5% on arith+func.
On arith+func and the templated StableHLO-Held-Out-200 the baselines match or beat the SLM; we scope these as non-win cells.
We release benchmarks, decoder, every per-prompt generation, and a pinned reproducibility Dockerfile.
highlights: exceeds 15B-34B code LMs running post-hoc rejection at a matched retry budget and 8-25x the per-generation speed: on lin

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: VTrajEmbed: Aligning Text with Video Object Trajectories via Spatiotemporal Embeddings
papers.summary:
Fine-grained alignment between text and video object trajectories is a core challenge in multimodal understanding.
Existing embedding models excel at global retrieval, yet their single global representation entangles multiple objects and their spatiotemporal dynamics, limiting direct object-level grounding.
To address this issue, we propose VTrajEmbed, an embedding model that decomposes a video into object trajectories and aligns each trajectory embedding with text for object-level grounding through retrieval.
Our main contributions: (1)Slow-Fast Trajectory Encoding, a dual-branch architecture that establishes trajectory representations by densely sampling low-resolution frames for high-frequency motion cues and sparsely selecting high-resolution frames for scene context, aggregated by a shared LLM backbone; (2)Mask-Guided Contrastive Learning, a training objective built upon these representations that couples an intra-group loss and a batch-level bidirectional loss under a relation mask, excluding unverified relations and preventing confirmed matches from becoming false negatives; (3)Text2Traj-Bench, a trajectory-level text-video benchmark with model-assisted construction and human-verified query--trajectory relations.
Experimental results show that VTrajEmbed-5B improves text-to-trajectory and trajectory-to-text R@1 over Qwen3-VL-Embedding-8B by 15.48 and 18.05 percentage points, respectively, and achieves 49.48% average R@1 across five global retrieval benchmarks, compared with 42.86% for Qwen3-VL-Embedding-8B.
highlights: Fine-grained alignment between text and video object trajectories is a core challenge in multimodal understanding.

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: SpaceCast-Bench: Evaluating Predictive Spatial Reasoning in Vision-Language Models
papers.summary:
Existing spatial reasoning benchmarks mainly test spatial perception: reading off relations already visible in the input.
Yet real-world spatial intelligence demands predictive spatial reasoning: constructing a scene from observations, anticipating how an intervention changes it, and reasoning about the unseen outcome.
We introduce SpaceCast-Bench, the first benchmark to directly and diagnostically evaluate this capability.
Built around an observe-transform-infer framework, its 3,862 questions from 182 real-world scenes span 16 task types at three levels: static perception, local prediction, and global prediction, progressively requiring scene understanding, spatial state updating, and relational inference over unobserved outcomes.
Evaluating 21 models exposes a stark gap: the strongest model reaches only 58.0% against 87.2% human performance, while spatially specialized models remain near random chance.
Controlled analyses further reveal that bridge views are critical for integrating distributed observations, and that explicit 3D evidence benefits models more reliably than generated outcome images or videos.
Fine-tuning on our programmatically generated data lifts Qwen3-VL-4B from 34.0% to 65.7% with macro-average gains across six out-of-domain benchmarks.
highlights: first benchmark to directly and diagnostically evaluate this capability

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: VideoHarness-SRSI: Structured Recursive Self-Improvement for Video Understanding Harness
papers.summary:
LLM system capabilities depend not only on model parameters but also on the executable harnesses that organize information acquisition, tool use, reasoning, and memory. LLM系统功能不仅取决于模型参数，还取决于组织信息采集、工具使用、推理和内存的可执行线束。
Recursive harness evolution can automate their design, but how it can reliably discover generalizable systems from limited, noisy, and repeatedly reused feedback remains unclear. 递归线束的演进可以实现其设计的自动化，但它如何从有限、嘈杂和重复使用的反馈中可靠地发现可推广的系统尚不清楚。
We study this question in agentic video understanding, where rich multimodal evidence and coupled mechanisms make harness optimization challenging. 我们在代理视频理解中研究这个问题，丰富的多模态证据和耦合机制使线束优化具有挑战性。
We first introduce VHarness-BRSI, a recursive self-improvement framework that evolves video harnesses around a frozen vision-language model. 我们首先介绍VHarness-BRSI ，这是一个递归自我改进框架，围绕冻结的视觉语言模型发展视频线束。
Analyzing over 4,000 evolved candidates, we find it competitive with hand-engineered systems but identify three interconnected failure modes: validation overfitting, search-budget dilution, and the early-experience trap. 我们分析了4000多名进化的候选者，发现它与手工系统有竞争力，但确定了三种相互关联的故障模式：验证过拟合、搜索预算稀释和早期体验陷阱。
We trace all three to a common root: the same imperfect validation evidence drives both harness revisions and the proposer's search strategy. 我们将这三者追溯到一个共同的根源：相同的不完美验证证据推动了线束修订和提案者的搜索策略。
We therefore propose VHarness-SRSI, an evidence-governed framework in which every search decision rests on evidence that is transferable, sufficient, and gathered before the search commits. 因此，我们提出了VHarness-SRSI ，这是一个证据管理框架，其中每个搜索决定都依赖于在搜索提交之前可转移、充分和收集的证据。
It restricts the proposer to content-free feedback, informs exploration with instrumented warm-up experiments, and develops mechanisms in isolated probe-race branches before factorial composition and joint refinement. 它将提议者限制为无内容反馈，通过仪器预热实验为探索提供信息，并在析因组合和关节细化之前在孤立的探针-竞赛分支中开发机制。
Across four video understanding benchmarks, VideoHarness-SRSI improves the equally weighted mean held-out score by 6.2% relative to VideoHarness-BRSI and reduces the mean validation-test gap by 37.9%. 在四个视频理解基准中， VideoHarness-SRSI相对于VideoHarness-BRSI将同等加权的平均保留分数提高了6.2% ，并将平均验证测试差距缩小了37.9%。
Reliable harness evolution thus depends on how search is organized and informed, not only on how well it optimizes validation performance. 因此，可靠的线束进化取决于搜索的组织和知情方式，而不仅仅是它优化验证性能的程度。

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Group-Graph Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary:
Group-based Reinforcement Learning (RL) has significantly enhanced Large Language Models (LLMs) in agentic scenarios. 基于群体的强化学习（ RL ）在代理场景中显著增强了大型语言模型（ LLM ）。
To achieve finer-grained policy updates, recent agentic RL frameworks have shifted from trajectory-level to step-level training. 为了实现更细粒度的策略更新，最近的代理RL框架已从轨迹级转变为步骤级培训。
However, long-horizon agentic RL suffers from severe reward sparsity and delay, as feedback is often deferred for dozens of interaction steps. 然而，长时间代理RL遭受严重的奖励稀疏和延迟，因为反馈通常延迟数十个交互步骤。
While existing step-level frameworks refine training granularity, their credit assignment remains coarse-grained and still treats agent exploration as isolated, linear trajectories. 虽然现有的步骤级框架完善了培训粒度，但其学分分配仍然是粗粒度的，并且仍然将座席探索视为孤立的线性轨迹。
This oversimplified perspective ignores the inherent graph structure of state transitions, leading to high-variance state-value estimation and myopic, localized credit assignment. 这种过度简化的观点忽略了状态转换的固有图结构，导致高方差状态值估计和短视的局部信用分配。
To overcome these critical bottlenecks, we propose Group-Graph Policy Optimization (G2PO), a novel group-based RL algorithm tailored for multi-turn agentic tasks. 为了克服这些关键瓶颈，我们提出了组图策略优化（ G2PO ） ，这是一种针对多圈代理任务量身定制的新型基于组的RL算法。
G2PO explicitly transforms linear interaction trajectories into a global state-transition graph. G2PO明确地将线性交互轨迹转换为全局状态转换图。
By aggregating identical observations across different trajectories, we introduce group-aggregation state-value estimation that reduces sampling variance and trajectory-dependent bias. 通过聚合不同轨迹上的相同观测值，我们引入了组聚合状态值估计，从而减少了采样方差和轨迹相关偏差。
Furthermore, we redefine agent actions as transitions between state nodes and propose an edge-centric advantage estimation strategy. 此外，我们将代理行为重新定义为状态节点之间的转换，并提出了一种以边缘为中心的优势估计策略。
By globally standardizing Temporal Difference (TD) errors across the entire graph, G2PO explicitly identifies and prioritizes critical transitions that drive absolute task progress. 通过在整个图表中全局标准化时间差异（ TD ）错误， G2PO明确识别并优先考虑推动绝对任务进度的关键转换。
Extensive experiments on representative long-horizon benchmarks-WebShop, ALFWorld, and AppWorld-demonstrate that G2PO substantially outperforms state-of-the-art prompt-based and RL baselines, achieving remarkable success rate improvements of up to 22.2% over GRPO. 对具有代表性的长期基准WebShop、ALFWorld和AppWorld进行的大量实验表明， G2PO大大优于最先进的基于提示和RL的基线，实现了比GRPO高达22.2%的显着成功率提升。
highlights: outperforms state-of-the-art prompt-based and RL baselines

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Lean4AgenticRL: Advancing Agentic RL with Verifiable Multi-level Process Rewards
papers.summary:
Enhancing the agentic capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) to tackle complex software engineering (SWE) and general terminal-usage problems is a pressing challenge.
Current state-of-the-art LLMs often go through large-scale agentic Reinforcement Learning (RL).
However, they mostly rely on high-level outcome rewards, with minimal consideration of low-level toolcall and mid-level workflow-stage rewards, which makes the training less effective.
To overcome this limitation, we propose **Lean4AgenticRL**, which, to the best of our knowledge, is the first framework that grounds multi-level process rewards in the unified Lean4 formalization schema for open-ended agentic RL.
**Lean4AgenticRL** first builds a *problem-specific workflow* system that balances the agent's own capability and controllability during execution, laying the foundation for further verification.
Subsequently, our workflow formalization and multi-level reward annotation methods enable agent behavior verification within a general harness system.
It provides multi-level rewards to support more effective agentic RL with the workflow-stage-normalized GRPO algorithm.
Using **Lean4AgenticRL**, we train **LAR-9B/27B**, a family of models with enhanced agentic capability.
Extensive experiments indicate that our model outperforms the leading model of similar size.
**LAR-27B** achieves **77.3%** on TerminalBench-2.1.
On average, our models outperform the base model by **9.89%** and surpass the second-best model of comparable size we know by **5.07%**.
These results indicate the potential of integrating formal methods in enhancing open-ended agentic RL.
highlights: outperforms the leading model of similar size
first framework that grounds multi-level process rewards in the unified Lean4 formalization schema for open-ended agenti
Current state-of-the-art LLMs often go through large-scale agentic Reinforcement Learning (RL).

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Think More or Read More? A Token-Budget Theory of Reasoning with Shared Context
papers.summary:
Reasoning systems increasingly improve answers by incorporating additional context into the model's input, from multi-agent debate, where agents read their peers' responses, to self-refinement, where a model revisits its own drafts.
In these systems, communication consumes context as one agent's output becomes another's input.
We study the regime where token reading and generation draw on one fixed token window, so every token spent reading is a token that cannot be spent reasoning.
We develop a \textbf{token-budget theory} that formalizes this trade-off, modeling accuracy as a function of the reasoning budget remaining after reading and aggregating votes with a Condorcet jury model that permits correlated errors.
For multi-agent debate, the theory gives a closed-form prediction for the optimal number of agents.
This quantity is estimated from single-agent measurements, allowing the optimal group size to be determined without running debate, and the same accounting extends to a heterogeneous set of different models.
We empirically verify our theory and show that, at the predicted group size, our method outperforms strong baselines under the tightest calibration spend, where debate-calibrated rules can afford only one or two questions.
Self-refinement obeys the same accounting, with its own draft in place of a peer message.
The theory further predicts that communication pays only when the gain in the accuracy ceiling exceeds the reasoning room spent on reading, with this condition tightening as the window shrinks.
Across five open models and four reasoning tasks, self-consistency matches or beats deployed debate at $93$\% of $980$ matched window-and-group-size settings, with the gap being largest under tight windows and nearly disappearing at a loose one, consistent with the theory.
Under a shared window, how much room a model has left to \textit{think matters more than what it reads}.
highlights: outperforms strong baselines under the tightest calibration spend
Think More or Read More? A Token

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: GRAFT-ATHENA: Self-Improving Agentic Teams for Autonomous Discovery and Evolutionary Numerical Algorithms
papers.summary:
Language-model agents plan, execute, and evaluate scientific workflows.
However, the problem--method relationships guiding their choices remain implicit, so plausible outputs can violate the assumptions of the scientific problem.
We introduce Graph Reduction to Adaptive Factored Trees (GRAFT), which makes this problem-to-method map explicit as an expandable probabilistic structure of admissible problems, methods, and dependencies.
Because this structure follows scientific semantics, knowledge from documentation, papers, and domain experts can be encoded, while factorization keeps the structure tractable.
Semantic fingerprints of encoded problems measure their similarity, so expertise and experience guide related problems.
GRAFT-guided workflows exceeded published expert baselines in physics-informed learning, recovered blood-rheology trends, predicted Apollo Command Module hypersonic loading within 1.8\% of experiment, and established machine-checked error bounds for regularized brain-flow reconstruction and a spectral physics-informed architecture.
The representation retains evaluated outcomes and incorporates new methods, allowing scientific knowledge and experience to accumulate.
highlights: exceeded published expert baselines in physics-informed learning

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: InstAgent: A Recursively Self-Improving Agent Operating System for Heterogeneous Robot Collaboration
papers.summary:
Heterogeneous robot teams enable complex, long-horizon tasks by combining complementary sensing, mobility, and manipulation capabilities across multiple embodiments.
Yet existing systems struggle to retain execution-time corrections as reusable experience, maintain task-relevant context memory across space and time for reliable handoffs, and explicitly represent the inter-robot dependencies required for structured collaboration.
In order to address these challenges, we present InstAgent, a recursively self-improving (RSI) Agent Operating System for heterogeneous robot collaboration.
InstAgent organizes team behaviors as agentic behavior trees (BTs) that explicitly model capability assignment, inter-robot dependencies and handoff checks.
The RSI mechanism updates these collaboration programs from execution feedback and preserves successful revisions for reuse in future tasks, while shared multimodal spatio-temporal memory provides context for planning and handoff validation.
Experiments on 20 real-world multi-robot tasks with three high-level models show consistent gains in task success, first-attempt completion, and execution efficiency.

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: UniField++: A Unified Agentic Framework with Loop Reasoning for MRI Field-Strength Enhancement
papers.summary:
MRI field-strength enhancement seeks to combine the accessibility of low-field scanners with the image quality of high-field scanners.
Yet, existing methods remain prone to anatomical hallucinations, as uniform processing leaves difficult brain regions insufficiently examined and scarce paired data limit their learning of how tissue contrast and anatomical visibility change across field strengths.
To address these challenges, we propose UniField++, a two-agent framework that unifies enhancement tasks across multiple field-strength transitions, including 64mT-to-3T and 3T-to-7T.
Unified learning allows both the VLM-based planner and the flow-matching-based enhancer to draw on field-dependent image characteristics observed across tasks, rather than relying on a single transition.
Trained with radiologists' annotations of hallucination-prone regions and corresponding correction plans, the planner predicts regional risk and formulates targeted restoration strategies.
Guided by these plans, the enhancer performs loop reasoning along the flow-matching trajectory, repeatedly processing high-risk regions for additional refinement.
Together, cross-transition learning and risk-guided refinement support anatomically faithful enhancement across field strengths.
Across the evaluated tasks, UniField++ improves PSNR by an average of 2.74 dB and SSIM by 14.05 percentage points over comparison methods, with corresponding gains of 3.97 dB and 13.92 percentage points over the ablation baseline.
It also maintains enhancement quality on an external cohort with an unseen field strength and improves downstream whole-brain segmentation Macro Dice by an average of 0.1457 over the original low-field images.
Code is available at https://github.com/CUHK-AIM-Group/UniField_plusplus.
highlights: MRI field-strength enhancement seeks to combine the accessibility of low-field scanners with the image quality of high-f

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: CastFlow: Bridging Evidence Acquisition and Accurate Prediction in Agentic Time Series Forecasting
papers.summary:
Time series forecasting is a fundamental task in temporal data analytics, and large language model (LLM)-based agents offer a promising paradigm through autonomous tool interaction and evidence-grounded reasoning.
However, two fundamental challenges remain: how to acquire forecast-relevant evidence through adaptive tool interactions, and how to translate such evidence into accurate numerical predictions.
To address these challenges, we propose CastFlow, a role-specialized agentic forecasting framework that bridges general-purpose tool reasoning and specialized temporal forecasting.
Specifically, CastFlow introduces an Experience Memory that distills successful tool-use trajectories from training data, guiding a frozen LLM to orchestrate a multi-view toolkit for evidence acquisition.
A lightweight specialized LLM then performs evidence-grounded temporal reasoning to refine an ensemble forecasting prior.
To enhance this capability, we develop a two-stage training strategy combining supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, where final forecasting outcomes of the overall workflow guide the optimization of the specialized model.
Extensive experiments on ten real-world benchmarks demonstrate that CastFlow outperforms competitive baselines on nine datasets.
Our findings highlight the importance of bridging autonomous evidence acquisition and specialized temporal reasoning for accurate and adaptive agentic forecasting.
The source code is available at https://github.com/Forever-Pan/CastFlow.
highlights: outperforms competitive baselines on nine datasets

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Has GPT-6-Astra Achieved Embodied Intelligence?
papers.summary:
GPT-6-Astra demonstrates a level of competence in robotic manipulation and navigation that challenges the conventional paradigm of building specialized models for individual tasks and embodiments.
In this report, we ask not only how capable GPT-6-Astra is, but what its capabilities imply for the field.
First, we probe the limits of standalone GPT-6-Astra.
We conduct a large-scale evaluation across 12 representative benchmarks spanning tabletop manipulation, humanoids, mobile platforms, and dexterous hands.
Under a unified protocol that allows in-context learning (ICL) from training-set demonstrations and substantially increases the number of execution steps, GPT-6-Astra achieves unprecedented performance (Fig.
1).
Future research may focus on improving 1) the generality of ICL 2) cost and execution time, 3) physical-state verification, 4) recovery from irreversible failures, and 5) long-horizon preservation of progress.
Second, we study the agentic harness for embodied control.
We identify that close-loop coordination between a high-level "System 2" reasoner (i.e., GPT-6-Astra) and a low-level "System 1" controller (e.g., {\pi}0.5) is costly but effective.
Third, we examine GPT-6-Astra on real-world deployment.
Our experiments on 8 robot configurations reveal substantial gaps: 1) robot demonstrations required for ICL are expensive to collect, and 2) it is implausible to trade longer execution for higher success rates with physical constraints.
Fourth, we envision the next generation of embodied benchmarks.
We develop a prototype that 1) derives tasks from real-world needs, 2) provides no in-domain demonstrations, and 3) judges agents on a world clock that keeps running while they deliberate.
Taken together, our results suggest that GPT-6-Astra has largely crossed the threshold of embodied competence, but not yet that of practical embodied intelligence.
highlights: In this report, we ask not only how capable GPT-6-Astra is, but what its capabilities imply for the field.

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Beyond Success Rate: Interventional Evaluation of Memory in Vision-Language-Action Systems
papers.summary:
When we say that a robot uses memory, does that memory actually play a role?
Success-rate ablations alone cannot establish the use of task-relevant facts: they change information and computation together, while aggregate rates can hide offsetting gains and losses.
We propose an Interventional Memory Evaluation Protocol (IMEP) for vision-language-action (VLA) systems to address four questions: (1) Does memory provide a net benefit?
(2) Under what conditions does memory help?
(3) Do changes to memory alter task outcomes?
(4) Are these effects specific to task-relevant facts?
At the retrieval interface, we compare target-fact substitutions with fact-preserving replacements, minimal numerical perturbations, and exact replicas, while assessing decision correctness separately from motor execution success.
We evaluate within-episode, cross-episode, and agentic memory.
In cross-episode learned-bank experiments, a one-unit-in-the-last-place (ULP) intervention, including its installation procedure, changes 11.9% of seed-paired outcomes, while changing key facts produces no clear additional effect over fact-preserving replacements.
To examine when memory helps, we introduce ChainBench, where correct decisions require historical information unavailable in current observations.
The full memory configuration raises task success from 39.1% to 74.3%, matching the oracle-decision condition under shared recorded executions.
These results show that correct history can support robot decisions, but establishing whether a memory system realizes this benefit requires fact-specific evidence beyond aggregate success rates.
highlights: When we say that a robot uses memory, does that memory actually play a role?

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: RAP: A Dataset for Paper-to-Poster Generation via Declarative Markup from Human-Crafted Exemplars
papers.summary:
Making a conference poster is visual coding in miniature: an entire paper must be compressed onto a single page, which exercises summarization, visual design, and code implementation at once, using nothing beyond the paper itself.
Yet benchmarks for this task in the context of visual coding remain scarce: existing resources are small and annotated only with layout boxes, so evaluation must fall back on VLM-as-judge or human checklists rather than objective render-and-compare, and the generation methods they support design layouts from scratch, leaving human-crafted posters unusable as either a retrievable design library or as verified supervision.
We introduce RAP (Reconstruct A Poster), a dataset and benchmark for paper-to-poster generation as a visual coding task.
RAP contains 25K+ verified paper-poster pairs from various machine learning conferences held between 2022 and 2026, annotated with a three-level content taxonomy, plus a held-out benchmark of 150 test papers each paired with its human poster.
A fully automated derendering pipeline turns each poster into styled HTML/CSS of typed, refillable slots, so every sample is a paper-poster-markup triplet verifiable by rendering against the source poster.
The corpus serves both inference and training: PosterRAG, a training-free multi-agent pipeline, retrieves an exemplar and refills its slots without touching layout or styling, while an SFT+RL recipe trains a dedicated model from the same triplets.
An online demo is available at https://reconstruct-a-poster.github.io/.
highlights: We introduce RAP (Reconstruct A Poster), a dataset and benchmark for paper-to-poster generation as a visual coding task.

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: QD-Rec: Open-Ended Evolution of Recommendations via Quality-Diversity
papers.summary:
Open-ended search combined with foundation models has produced advances such as faster algorithms, new results on open mathematical problems, and self-improving agents.
We extend this paradigm to recommendation for decision-making, focusing on decisions where the set of possible choices is fixed but the reasons for choosing them are not.
In high-stakes decisions, e.g., which company to acquire or which customer to target, comparing diverse, well-reasoned options can be more useful than a single ranked list.
We formalize open-ended recommendation as building a diverse, high-quality set of recommendations, each an item together with a hypothesis, a natural-language reason why the item fits the needs of a decision maker.
We propose QD-Rec, a quality--diversity method that selects items with a contextual bandit and generates hypotheses with a foundation model from earlier ones kept in an archive as stepping stones.
A new recommendation enters the archive if it is novel or better than its nearest neighbor.
Across M&A, customer targeting, and paper and book recommendation, QD-Rec gives the highest mean quality and builds the largest archive in most settings.
highlights: A new recommendation enters the archive if it is novel or better than its nearest neighbor.

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Agentic Image Generation in the Wild
papers.summary:
Agentic image generation pairs an image generator with a search agent that retrieves references from the web, extending generation beyond the generator's training data.
Real-world requests, however, often concern entities that appeared only days ago.
We call this setting Image Generation in the Wild.
In this setting, the web offers limited visual evidence, search results are crowded with easily confused entities, and the target is rarely shown on its own.
To study this setting, we build an automated pipeline that synthesizes prompts from recent headlines and keeps only those whose real search results are highly confusing, yielding requests that are hard to solve yet natural to ask.
With it, we construct Savanna, a benchmark of 500 prompts across 16 subcategories.
On Savanna, even harness frameworks built on the frontier models retrieve a correct reference for only about half of the prompts.
We then propose Locate-Corroborate-Isolate, a paradigm in which the agent first pins down the target's identity through text search, then verifies candidate images against multiple sources, and finally crops a clean reference for the generator.
Trained on 15K trajectories that follow this paradigm, Ranger-8B achieves a search score of 67.2, outperforming harnesses equipped with frontier models.
It also achieves the best generation quality with every generator we test, and surpasses prior agentic methods on other image generation benchmarks.
We release the pipeline, benchmark, training data and model at https://github.com/RUCAIBox/Agentic-ImageGen-Wild.
highlights: outperforming harnesses equipped with frontier models
first pins down the target's identity through text search
Real-world requests, however, often concern entities that appeared only days ago.

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: LDDR: Linear-DPP Dynamic-Resolution Frame Sampling for Video MLLMs
papers.summary:
Multimodal large language models, when used for long video understanding, require selecting an informative frame set from massive and redundant candidates.
Limited by the model's visual-token budget and reasoning ability, frame selection is therefore essential to reduce input size while preserving the most relevant information for accurate video reasoning.
Existing frame-sampling methods like uniform sampling or relevance/diversity-sampling often miss important events or retain redundant frames.
On the other hand, agentic frame selection methods incur very high computational costs.
Further, these methods allocate equal tokens to all selected frames, regardless of their importance.
We therefore propose LDDR (Linear DPP Dynamic Resolution), which is a training-free and budget-aware video frame sampling framework.
It is computationally efficient and allows non-uniform token budget allocation within the candidate frame set.
Specifically, LDDR performs query-aware Determinantal Point Process (DPP) frame selection in a task-conditioned feature space, achieving a 3x runtime speedup over standard DPP baselines.
It further introduces a Group DPP importance score to guide frame retention and dynamic resolution allocation: assigning more tokens to informative and non-redundant frames while downscaling or pruning less useful ones.
We test LDDR on four popular video benchmarks spanning short, medium, and long-range videos.
LDDR achieves a 2.5-point gain in low-budget settings and a 1.6-point gain in high-budget scenarios.
These improvements are consistently observed across multiple MLLM families and sizes.
Further manual qualitative analyses are included to prove the method's effectiveness.
highlights: Existing frame-sampling methods like uniform sampling or relevance/diversity-sampling often miss important events or ret

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning-Based UAV Pathfinding for Obstacle Avoidance in Stochastic Environment
papers.summary:
Traditional methods plan feasible paths for multiple agents in the stochastic environment.
However, the methods' iterations with the changes in the environment result in computation complexities, especially for the decentralized agents without a centralized planner.
Although reinforcement learning provides a plausible solution because of the generalization for different environments, it struggles with enormous agent-environment interactions in training.
Here, we propose a novel centralized training with decentralized execution method based on multi-agent reinforcement learning, which is improved based on the idea of model predictive control.
In our approach, agents communicate only with the centralized planner to make decentralized decisions online in the stochastic environment.
Furthermore, considering the communication constraint with the centralized planner, each agent plans feasible paths through the extended observation, which combines information on neighboring agents based on the distance-weighted mean field approach.
Inspired by the rolling optimization approach of model predictive control, we conduct multi-step value convergence in multi-agent reinforcement learning to enhance the training efficiency, which reduces the expensive interactions in convergence.
Experiment results in both comparison, ablation, and real-robot studies validate the effectiveness and generalization performance of our method.
highlights: propose a novel centralized training with decentralized execution method

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Beyond Marginal Influence: Interaction-Aware Memory Selection for LLM Agents
papers.summary:
LLM-agent memory selection often uses retrieval rankings based on record relevance or individual influence.
Such rankings cannot identify sufficient subsets under redundant or jointly necessary evidence.
We study per-decision memory sufficiency: selecting a small subset that preserves full-memory behavior.
To separate search error from model error, we introduce JointCoreBench, a benchmark with nine interaction families, six workflow domains, natural-language decisions, and exact sufficient-set oracles, and JointCore, a relevance cost-ordered group-deletion baseline that tests blocks before individual records.
On 6,912 exact conditions, cost-ordered JointCore recovers a minimum-cost sufficient set in 100.0% of cases, reduces subset evaluations from 30.00 to 11.13 (62.9%), and achieves 87.8% active-memory savings.
Across four 12B-70B model families and 432 tasks per model, its unweighted mean is 10.28 versus 16.00 model queries and 50.6% versus 43.1% minimum-cost recovery relative to cost aware singleton deletion.
Both methods preserve full-memory behavior under the deterministic primary interface.
Tests with physical deletion, UNKNOWN masks, PENDING sentinels, counterfactual values, and alternative labels identify interface dependent behavior.
JointCore is an efficient benchmark baseline; the study does not establish deployment-ready memory compression.
highlights: LLM-agent memory selection often uses retrieval rankings based on record relevance or individual influence.

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: PersonaCUABench: Benchmarking Computer-Use Agents Serving Diverse Personas
papers.summary:
Computer-use agents (CUAs) are commonly evaluated against fixed task specifications, but users may omit requirements, add constraints, or require approval before consequential actions.
Completing the benchmark instruction does not guarantee serving the person who asked.
We introduce PersonaCUABench, which holds 74 tasks across 11 domains fixed and varies only who asks.
A persona agent, playing one of 44 personas in four groups, rewrites each instruction in that user's own words and answers the CUA's questions, while the CUA sees only the dialogue, never the profile or the original instruction.
Across nine backbones (3,330 runs), mean task completion falls by 36% relative to the original requests.
The losses have two sources: in 59.9% of cells that lose points, the agent engages with what the user asked for and still gets it wrong, and 11.2% are stops the user requested that the checker scores as failures.
Even when a persona request is fully completed, the user gives the top satisfaction rating in only 62.7% of cells, against 84.1% for the original requests.
CUAs should therefore be evaluated not only on task completion but also on whether they meet the requirements and constraints users express.
Code: https://github.com/MatrAIx-ai/PersonaCUABench.
Project page: https://matraix.ai/research/persona-cua.html
highlights: Completing the benchmark instruction does not guarantee serving the person who asked.

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Learning Agentic Time Series Forecasting via Trajectory Distillation and Memory-Based Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary:
Recent agentic time series forecasting (TSF) approaches use large language models (LLMs) to autonomously orchestrate analytical and forecasting tools and reason about temporal patterns using the resulting evidence.
However, many such approaches rely on powerful LLMs in training-free, prompt-driven workflows, leaving open whether smaller models can learn these interaction and reasoning capabilities.
In this paper, we introduce Cast-R1, an 8Bparameter agentic forecasting model trained through trajectory distillation and multi-turn reinforcement learning with structured memory.
First, we develop a forecasting agent harness with specialized analysis and prediction tools to generate multi-turn interaction trajectories using a teacher LLM, which are subsequently evaluated and selected for supervised fine-tuning.
Second, we apply group relative policy optimization (GRPO) across multi-turn forecasting episodes, with structured memory preserving diagnostic evidence and intermediate forecasts for state construction.
Rewards based on prediction accuracy and temporal structure guide tool selection, model routing, and forecast refinement.
A difficulty-aware curriculum combines sample filtering and progressive sample ordering during training.
Extensive experiments on multiple datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of Cast-R1.
These findings highlight the potential of forecasting-specific post-training to equip smaller LLMs with multi-turn, tool-augmented forecasting capabilities within structured workflows.
highlights: Learning Agentic Time Series Forecasting via Trajectory Distillation and Memory
Rewards based on prediction accuracy and temporal structure guide tool selection, model routing, and forecast refinement

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: CastClaw: A Human-in-the-Loop Autonomous Agent for Interactive Time Series Forecasting
papers.summary:
Practical time-series forecasting requires domain knowledge, constraints, plausibility checks, and human intervention.
We present CastClaw, an interactive forecasting system centered on an autonomous forecasting loop and supported by a forecasting-oriented harness.
Users create and refine tasks in natural language through command-line and Web interfaces.
An internal large language model (LLM) agent reads the task and evidence, selects a permitted tool action or request for human feedback, and uses checked results to decide whether to continue, revisit an analysis, switch a candidate, or stop.
The harness supplies tool integration, controlled execution, state management, historical validation, and execution limits.
npm distribution connects installation and configuration to interactive execution and forecast and report export.
Across five public electricity-price datasets, CastClaw achieves the lowest point-estimate MSE and MAE among 16 baselines.
A Nord Pool case study illustrates its inspectable decision process, while provincial electricity-load data from North China (January--June 2026) demonstrate offline task execution.
highlights: Practical time-series forecasting requires domain knowledge, constraints, plausibility checks, and human intervention.

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Predicting Task Difficulty Without Rollouts
papers.summary:
A fundamental challenge in evaluating and training autonomous agents is measuring the intrinsic difficulty of the tasks they attempt.
Estimating this quantity can be useful for environment designers creating synthetic data or benchmarks, as well as for constructing training curricula, thereby offering a way to reduce compute costs.
Such an estimation becomes increasingly important as agents (particularly LLM-based) move into longer-horizon domains, where empirical trial-and-error becomes a severe computational bottleneck.
However existing work is largely confined to static tasks and relies on evaluation metrics that, as we show, can give an incomplete picture of predictive performance.
In this paper we study ex ante difficulty prediction across 17 agentic benchmarks spanning coding, mathematics, machine learning, web navigation, function calling, and other domains.
We find that AUC can mask poor difficulty estimates, identify token-level entropy as a useful predictive signal, and demonstrate how residuals between expected and observed difficulty can expose environment flaws such as contamination and infeasibility.
highlights: A fundamental challenge in evaluating and training autonomous agents is measuring the intrinsic difficulty of the tasks

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Towards Physically Grounded Articulated 3D Assets: A Multi-Agent Pipeline and Benchmark
papers.summary:
In this paper, we study physically grounded articulated 3D asset generation---moving the goal from reproducing how objects look to capturing how they move and function.
Inspired by the literature on procedural and agentic generation, we present Artisan, a system that extends the latest method Articraft by introducing a multi-agent pipeline with physical simulation feedback, enabling comprehensive attributes beyond geometry, appearance, and physically plausible articulation, such as collision-free motion, stability under gravity, and accurate mass and material properties.
Furthermore, we construct a unified benchmark spanning four key aspects: spatial fidelity, physical plausibility, downstream task performance, and overall quality.
The benchmark encompasses 100 reference assets from ArtVIP and LightWheel, 50 stability prompts, and 50 ABO objects with reference masses, with protocols evaluating various metrics.
Through extensive evaluation of more than 10 representative models, Artisan achieves competitive spatial fidelity while attaining the lowest collision rates and highest stability rates among the evaluated methods.
Together, our system and benchmark establish insights for advancing 3D generation towards physically plausible, functionally usable assets.
highlights: Together, our system and benchmark establish insights for advancing 3D generation towards physically plausible, function

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: FLARE: Physics-Grounded Evaluation of Language-Model Agents for Feeder Restoration with Degraded Observations
papers.summary:
Restoring service after distribution-grid faults requires decisions from incomplete and conflicting information while respecting electrical constraints.
Addressing this need, we introduce FLARE (Feeder-Level Agent Restoration Evaluation), a physics-grounded benchmark for post-isolation feeder restoration.
FLARE con- tains 800 AC-feasible cases across five observation settings and allows agents to gather evidence, evaluate switches, and perform restoration actions under fixed operational limits.
We evaluate five instruction-tuned models over 78,750 episodes, including topology, distributed-generation, and loading shifts.
Mean normalized regret ranges from 0.082 to 0.148.
Although every model has zero median regret, P95 regret ranges from 0.814 to 1.000, revealing an important failure tail.
Shadow replay shows that 96.4% of 15,706 guard-rejected actions would have caused a physical violation.
FLARE enables reproducible evaluation of language-model based restoration support while emphasizing the need for external safety checks.
highlights: We evaluate five instruction-tuned models over 78,750 episodes, including topology, distributed-generation, and loading

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Scene-Designer: Learning Design Intelligence for Agentic 3D Scene Generation
papers.summary:
Generating complete, coherent, and usable 3D indoor scenes from natural language requires strong \textbf{design intelligence}: the ability to design high-quality scenes and critique their quality.
However, existing approaches either rely on general-purpose models lacking domain-specific design experience or learn from static scenes.
In this work, we introduce \textbf{Scene-Designer}, an agentic framework that learns design intelligence through complementary design and critique experiences.
We construct two datasets: \textbf{Scene-OTA-35K}, which provides Observation--Thought--Action supervision for learning scene design and efficient error correction, and \textbf{Scene-OTC-15K}, which provides Observation--Thought--Critic supervision for learning scene quality critique across physical validity, functional correctness, and layout coherence.
Based on these experiences, we propose \textbf{Scene-GRPO}, a Critic-guided GRPO framework that improves design decisions and reduces unnecessary trial-and-error corrections.
Extensive experiments demonstrate that Scene-Designer achieves superior performance in physical validity, functional correctness, and layout coherence, while the learned Scene-Critic significantly outperforms general-purpose models in scene critique.
Moreover, test-time Critic guidance further improves scene generation, showing that the Critic can provide useful guidance beyond training.
Additional analysis suggests a trend of mutual enhancement between scene design and critique abilities.
highlights: outperforms general-purpose models in scene critique

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Agentic Physics-Grounded Video Generation via Memory-Augmented In-Context Reasoning
papers.summary:
Physical plausibility is essential for realistic video generation.
Existing methods impose physical guidance before synthesis via simulations or refined prompts, but this can limit dynamic diversity, miss errors that emerge only after generation, and require repeated regeneration when inconsistencies remain.
We therefore study a generate-diagnose-repair paradigm that preserves the original generation capability and selectively repairs physical inconsistencies afterward, raising two key questions: what to repair and how to repair?
To address them, we introduce PhysRepair, an agentic video generation framework that combines causal reasoning over the observed physical failure with prior repair experience to enable localized and adaptive correction.
Specifically, Spatiotemporal Causal Constraints identify the first invalid physical state and its causally affected states, producing a repair specification that guides physically plausible local regeneration while preserving unaffected content.
Experience-augmented In-context Learning combines the ongoing repair context with relevant experience from previous repairs, allowing the agent to adapt its repair decisions across diverse physical failures and accumulate completed trajectories for future cases.
Experiments on Physics-IQ Verified across solid mechanics, fluid dynamics, optics, thermodynamics, and magnetism demonstrate that PhysRepair consistently improves the physical plausibility of generated videos over existing methods.
Our project page is available at https://xxkkxxx.github.io/PhysRepair-Website/.
highlights: first invalid physical state and its causally affected states

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Execution Before Memory: Diagnosing Memory Failures in Video World Models
papers.summary:
A memory test for a video world model should say whether the scene was set, whether the asked change was carried out, and whether the last frame shows the result.
Current tests fold these into one number, so a low score is easy to read as forgetting.
When the change is not carried out, the hidden state transition cannot appear, so the test is not really a test of memory.
We introduce MIST, an evaluation that separates the change from the memory it should leave behind.
The model first sets the scene while the change stays hidden, and only later is asked to show it, with leakage before that point kept under control.
This separation locates the bottleneck: the model sets the scene but does not carry out the instructed change.
The same gap appears in general memory evaluations.
On that basis we propose M3-Agent (Make the Missing Move), which recursively revises the details of the input instruction so that the model successfully carries out the requested instruction.
Relative to the baseline, it more than triples the MIST reveal score.
On the benchmarks, WRBench's score T rises by 26.1% and MBench-T's score U by 52.7%.
The method meets the problem from the execution side: it shows what the frozen model can do once the move is stated, and it sets a stricter baseline.
highlights: first sets the scene while the change stays hidden

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: ECHOES: Seeing Beyond the Current Image via Recursive History Compression and Privileged On-Policy Distillation
papers.summary:
Long-horizon GUI agents rely on visual history to maintain task states, but retaining historical screenshots increases visual-token usage and inference costs, while textual summaries can discard critical state information, undermining long-horizon reliability.
We propose ECHOES, which leverages training-time privileged information to guide textual history compression and strengthen long-horizon reasoning.
Specifically, ECHOES adopts a Compression-Think-Action (CTA) format to recursively update a textual history state and reason.
The same model, given privileged multi-image inputs, serves as a teacher that provides dense token-level on-policy distillation on student-generated CTA rollouts.
Our Perception-Memory Fidelity (PMF) Gap-guided OPD-RL framework dynamically balances privileged distillation and task-reward optimization, with periodic teacher updates supporting continued improvement.
We further introduce ECHOESBMK, a fine-grained diagnostic benchmark derived from real GUI agent failure trajectories to jointly evaluate visual perception and cross-modal state retention.
Experiments on four GUI benchmarks and ECHOESBMK demonstrate substantial gains in task performance and memory fidelity.
Without retaining historical screenshots at deployment, ECHOES achieves competitive performance with a favorable performance-inference-cost trade-off and exhibits positive zero-shot transfer to unseen visual planning tasks.
highlights: We propose ECHOES, which leverages training-time privileged information to guide textual history compression and strengt

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Batched Contextual Reinforcement II: Does RLVR Need Long Rollout Windows?
papers.summary:
Long rollout windows make reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) expensive, yet simply shortening them can remove the correctness signal: when every single-problem rollout truncates before an answer, group-relative accuracy advantages vanish.
As a technical continuation of Batched Contextual Reinforcement (BCR), we study how concurrent rewards relax this dependence on long windows.
Concurrent Constraint Reinforcement (CCR) places three independently verifiable problems in one capped training completion.
Correct answers completed before truncation retain credit, while a shared budget encourages shorter useful reasoning without an explicit length penalty.
We connect this mechanism to conditional reward- and update-variance analyses and study 4B and 8B mathematical reasoning models.
Against single-problem GRPO with a 32k window, CCR with an 8,000-token window reduces tokens per training step from 975,464 to 174,957 on 4B and from 793,832 to 165,788 on 8B, saving 82.1% and 79.1%, respectively.
An 8B training trace shows increasing accuracy reward alongside shorter completions.
Single-problem evaluations provide supporting evidence of retained reasoning quality.
These results identify reward-preserving training structure as a practical route to lower per-step cost in short-window RLVR.
highlights: As a technical continuation of Batched Contextual Reinforcement (BCR), we study how concurrent rewards relax this depend

featuredPapers.title: Athanor: An Agent-Native System for Autonomous Post-Training Research
featuredPapers.authors: Yufa Zhou, Yichen Wang, Jiakun Fan
featuredPapers.summary:
Recursive self-improvement, in which AI systems build stronger AI systems, is one promising route to superintelligence. 递归自我改进，即人工智能系统构建更强大的人工智能系统，是通往超级智能的一条有希望的途径。
We study a weaker form that can be measured today: frontier agents post-training a small raw base model with public data, as a test of their research potential. 我们研究了一种目前可以衡量的较弱形式：前沿代理商使用公共数据对小型原始基础模型进行后期训练，以测试其研究潜力。
We build Athanor, an open agent-native system for autonomous post-training research (AutoPostTrain) on real GPUs. 我们构建了Athanor ，这是一个用于真正GPU上的自主训练后研究（ AutoPostTrain ）的开放代理原生系统。
We give the agents full research autonomy, low-friction engineering tools, and efficient starter code.
The agents carry out the research themselves: they read datasets and evaluation results, build their training data, write and modify training algorithms, tune hyperparameters, and analyze the results to decide what to try next. 代理人自己进行研究：他们读取数据集和评估结果，构建训练数据，编写和修改训练算法，调整超参数，并分析结果以决定下一步尝试。
They work in a sandbox and cannot use external teacher models.
Athanor's services supply frozen evaluation, managed jobs, decontaminated data, a persistent research record, and a held-out suite the agents are unaware of.
In a 104-hour campaign, a team of four Claude Opus 5.5 agents, each on an eight-GPU node and given no research advice, improves Qwen3-4B-Base from 15.9 to 67.3 on a six-task development suite and from 9.2 to 48.2 on a held-out suite, against 66.5 and 47.9 for the official Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507.
To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration that a team of frontier agents can autonomously post-train a raw base model into a cross-domain generalist model that matches or surpasses the official instruct version on average.
The campaign's full record shows that the agents reach this level by recombining known methods and each other's models: SFT on public reasoning data, RL with a rollout change one agent introduced, weight merges across agents, and rounds of self-distillation.
With execution handled, today's agents already have the engineering and research ability to conquer this task.
We hope Athanor provides a foundation for scaling autonomous AI research.
highlights: surpasses the official instruct version on average
first demonstration that a team of frontier agents can autonomously post-train a raw base model into a cross-domain gene
Recursive self-improvement, in which AI systems build stronger AI systems, is one promising route to superintelligence.

featuredPapers.title: MemScope: Evolving Agent Memory Architectures through Localized Code Repair
featuredPapers.authors: Miao Su, Yucan Guo, Zixuan Li
featuredPapers.summary:
Agent memory architectures define how LLM agents store and reuse experience across tasks, but they are typically fixed after deployment, limiting their adaptability across task types.
Recent self-evolving approaches instead adapt these memory architectures using execution feedback, typically represented as evaluation scores or compressed summaries.
However, such coarse-grained feedback is insufficient for precise failure localization in current agent systems, where long-horizon task execution involves multiple interacting components.
Without a precise failure location, existing approaches lack a clear code-level target for modification, leaving the update scope weakly constrained and often leading to large-scale rewrites of an otherwise capable memory architecture.
We propose MemScope, a framework for evidence-grounded, localized evolution of an existing memory architecture.
Its tool-using Patch Agent jointly inspects raw execution traces, runtime memory state, and current architecture code to identify repair targets and apply bounded, in-place edits under provider-identity and memory-compatibility constraints.
On GAIA, the trace-and-memory inspection variant achieves 86.67% accuracy, compared with 70.00% for trace-only and 63.33% for summary-only feedback.
Under xBench tasks, the evolved memory architecture improves over its original version from 49 to 55 correct answers with DeepSeek V3.2 and from 50 to 53 with Kimi K2.7 Code.
On disjoint ALFWorld unseen tasks, success rises from 50.75% to 71.64%.
Across archived architecture-snapshot transitions, the median code-change ratio is 4.4%.
These results support fine-grained execution evidence as a basis for localized, in-place memory-architecture evolution.
highlights: We propose MemScope, a framework for evidence-grounded, localized evolution of an existing memory architecture.

featuredPapers.title: From Research Goals to Scientific Closure: Evaluating Agents Through Evidence-Supported Physics Research
featuredPapers.authors: Yijia Mao, Song Dai, Tao Chen
featuredPapers.summary:
Can AI agents organize scientific investigations that lead to well-supported conclusions?
To evaluate this capability, we introduce PhysClosureBench, a benchmark of 50 expert-verified, goal-specified research tasks spanning strong-field, attosecond, and neighboring physics areas.
Each task specifies the research objective and essential scientific constraints, while leaving the agent to organize the investigation and determine how to generate and validate the evidence needed to answer the question.
A 20-criterion Atomic Score measures local scientific accomplishment, while Research Closure (RC0--RC4) assesses how fully the investigation resolves the specified research question based on whether its indispensable evidence requirements and applicable scope conditions are satisfied.
We evaluate seven frontier LLMs, where Claude-Opus-5 achieves the highest mean Atomic Score (6.29/10) but reaches RC4 in only 32.7% of attempts.
Across the benchmark, 36.2% of attempts scoring at least 8/10 still fall short of RC4, while all seven models reach RC4 on substantially fewer tasks in all three runs than in at least one.
Case-level analysis further illustrates how misinterpretation of generated results and unresolved physical applicability limits can lead to incomplete closure.
Together, these results reveal a persistent gap between AI agents' local scientific accomplishments and their ability to achieve complete research closure.
highlights: From Research Goals to Scientific Closure
Can AI agents organize scientific investigations that lead to well-supported conclusions?

featuredPapers.title: HTN-Orchestrate: A Hierarchical Task Network Framework for Multi-Agent Orchestration
featuredPapers.authors: Yanchen Deng, Jianguo Huang, Yao Long Teng
featuredPapers.summary:
Orchestrating multiple agents on a complex task requires reconciling local subtask execution with global task planning.
Dynamic dispatch approaches provide execution flexibility but do not explicitly model subtask hierarchies or dependencies, while predefined workflows impose this structure but fix the decomposition before execution begins.
Therefore, we introduce HTN-Orchestrate, a two-layer framework that separates these responsibilities through a hierarchical task network (HTN).
The Planner maintains subtask hierarchies and dependencies, deferring decomposition until prerequisite results become available, while local Orchestrators schedule workers to execute each leaf subtask.
Results propagate upward under \textbf{AND} semantics, and accumulated findings inform a rebuilt task network when the current decomposition cannot resolve the task.
On five benchmarks spanning web research, scientific reasoning, and research workflows, HTN-Orchestrate outperforms ReAct, Agent Team, and DeepSeek Harness using the same base model, achieving 89.73% accuracy on BrowseComp and 73.44% on SUPERChem, exceeding Agent Team by 2.45 and 4.69 percentage points, respectively.

featuredPapers.title: MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering
featuredPapers.authors: Shangheng Du, Jinxin Shi, Shuaiyu Zhang
featuredPapers.summary:
Large language models (LLMs) are expanding from assisting scientific research and engineering to autonomously developing and improving AI systems, advancing AI for AI (AI4AI) as a pathway toward recursive self-improvement (RSI).
Workflow-driven machine learning engineering (MLE) systems provide a practical path toward this pursuit through complex orchestration that manages long-horizon experimentation, while recent MLE systems adopt model-directed interaction, allowing models to autonomously organize experiments and adapt optimization strategies based on execution feedback.
However, feedback from each experiment reflects several preceding decisions, and a long MLE run contains many such costly experiments.
Training must therefore select useful supervision from long interaction trajectories and learn from intermediate outcomes.
We propose a post-training method for autonomous long-horizon MLE optimization and apply it to train MLExpert, a 35B Mixture-of-Experts agentic model.
We design the Kaggle-MLE Factory to construct executable tasks and an interaction harness for model-directed experimentation.
Hierarchical agentic SFT transfers general tool-use and coding capabilities to MLE through outcome-guided supervision.
Windowed Interaction RL (WIRL) treats the multi-turn decisions between successive experiment results as an execution window and assigns it a shared outcome-based reward.
Asynchronous collection and policy correction support policy updates before the trajectory ends.
On MLE-Bench Lite, MLExpert improves the average medal rate of the base model from 37.9% to 72.7%, achieving performance comparable to larger frontier models such as Kimi-K3 and GLM-5.3.
Further experiments show that MLExpert improves performance on NatureBench Lite, agent scaffold optimization, and algorithm optimization, suggesting that the learned optimization capability generalizes to other tasks.

featuredPapers.title: INFUSE: A Unified Surface Benchmark for Indirect Prompt Injection in Agentic Systems
featuredPapers.authors: Thuy Dung Nguyen, Jingyi Guo, Rana Seda Dubauskas
featuredPapers.summary:
LLM-based agents increasingly execute long-horizon, end-to-end workflows involving shell commands, code modification, dependency installation, and interaction with remote services.
This growing autonomy expands their exposure to indirect prompt injection (IPI), where adversarial instructions embedded in external content are interpreted as legitimate task directives.
Existing evaluations, however, often focus on isolated malicious strings, single-step tool calls, or narrowly scoped agent configurations.
We introduce INFUSE, an end-to-end benchmark for evaluating IPI throughout the lifecycle of long-horizon agent workflows.
INFUSE comprises 40 realistic tasks and a structured taxonomy of 56 attack scenarios spanning five threat categories.
Attacks are injected through realistic interaction surfaces encountered during task execution, extending evaluation beyond attacks placed only in initial prompts or isolated tool interactions.
We evaluate 19 LLMs from the GPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama, Gemma, and Qwen families, producing 41,824 adversarial trajectories (26,220 without defenses) and 720 benign reference runs.
Across the benchmark, mean attack success reaches 19.6% under LLM-based evaluation and 15.4% under heuristic verification, with per-model ASR-L ranging from 3.2% to 41.9%.
Existing guard models provide limited protection, while prompt-level instructional hardening reduces mean attack success from 58.2% to 14.3%, revealing substantial but model-dependent security-utility trade-offs.
Our code is available at https://github.com/judydnguyen/infuse.

featuredPapers.title: Mosaic: Multi-Session Agentic Reinforcement Learning
featuredPapers.authors: Yilong Xu, Minrui Xu, Xinyu Zhou
featuredPapers.summary:
Most existing agentic reinforcement learning methods assume single-session trajectories, where interaction proceeds within one continuously accumulated context.
However, agentic techniques such as context compaction and subagent forking may produce trajectories spanning multiple sessions, creating a mismatch between the single-session training assumption and inference-time execution.
Therefore, we introduce Multi-Session Agentic Reinforcement Learning, a more general setting that supports an arbitrary number of sessions within a trajectory.
Under this setting, a widely adopted method is to broadcast trajectory-level advantages to all sessions, but this does not distinguish contributions from various sessions or guide session allocation within trajectories.
To address this issue, we propose Mosaic, a multi-session agentic RL method with critic-free hierarchical optimization.
At the trajectory level, it incorporates session-usage signals into advantage estimation.
At the session level, it shapes each session's advantage according to the estimated marginal contribution.
Experiments on BrowseComp with Qwen3.5-4B show that Mosaic outperforms broadcasting in both context compaction and subagent forking scenarios while using fewer sessions on average.
Further analyses show that our method achieves improvements in session utility and allocation, which we suggested is a promising target for future advances in multi-session agentic RL.
highlights: outperforms broadcasting in both context compaction and subagent forking scenarios while using fewer sessions on average

featuredPapers.title: ChaosBench-Logic: A Benchmark for Logical and Symbolic Reasoning on Chaotic Dynamical Systems
featuredPapers.authors: Noel Thomas
featuredPapers.summary:
Large language models (LLMs) excel at natural language tasks but remain brittle in domains requiring precise logical and symbolic reasoning.
Chaotic dynamical systems provide an especially demanding test because chaos is deterministic yet often misinterpreted as randomness or complexity.
We introduce ChaosBench-Logic, a benchmark that evaluates LLM reasoning across 30 diverse dynamical systems using a unified first-order logic (FOL) ontology.
Each system is annotated with truth assignments for 11 semantic predicates, and 621 questions are generated across seven reasoning categories, including multi-hop implications, cross-system analogies, counterfactual reasoning, bias probes, and multi-turn dialogues.
We define metrics for logical accuracy, implication consistency, dialogue coherence, and contradiction, and we release an open-source evaluation pipeline.
Initial experiments show that frontier LLMs such as GPT-4, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 2.5 Flash, and the open-source LLaMA-3 70B achieve 91-94% per-item accuracy, yet still score 0% on compositional items and exhibit fragile global coherence.
Dialogue-level accuracy ranges from 53.1% (GPT-4 CoT) to 75.5% (LLaMA-3 zero-shot).
ChaosBench-Logic provides a rigorous testbed for diagnosing such failures and a foundation for developing neuro-symbolic approaches that improve scientific reasoning in LLMs.

featuredPapers.title: Global Coherence: When Every Agent Is Right and the Team Is Still Wrong - A Local-to-Global Semantic Foundation for Multi-Agent Collaboration
featuredPapers.authors: Xin Heng
featuredPapers.summary:
AI agents can each make locally valid decisions yet jointly produce an invalid result.
We call this the global coherence problem: a failure of shared state, not merely of intelligence.
Our Observation-Aliasing Impossibility Theorem gives the exact boundary.
A policy can guarantee a valid action exactly when all worlds producing the same observation share an admissible action.
If k indistinguishable worlds require pairwise-disjoint actions, the best randomized worst-case success is 1/k; more reasoning, roles, messages, or samples cannot recover the missing distinction.
A stronger model can reason better within its context, but it cannot see beyond it.
The smallest sufficient context is NP-hard to find, yet counterexample-guided refinement finds a sufficient one and recertifies it as rules change.
We give local-to-global runtime semantics X = (H, C, G, F; D): topology H records overlapping scopes; category C governs state-changing actions; groupoid G keeps reversible translations; sheaf F tests whether local views glue into one world; and history D keeps only what alters legal futures.
Each preserves the needed information as state is split, translated, or changed.
Models propose; the harness owns shared state and governs commit.
Ten studies test the boundary.
On a revision benchmark, a frontier model scores 40/40 when the deciding event is visible; hidden, every arm is consistent with chance (1/3); one restored fact returns 40/40.
On TeamBench, ordinary teams exceed a shared budget in 5/5 runs, a visible live count leaves 4/5, and commit enforcement leaves 0/5.
In tau2-bench Telecom, current-state checks score 0.07 after silent reverts; the harness scores 1.00.
Refinement keeps a sufficient context through rule changes at 28% of the all-field cost.
Solvers that already own the state tie it, as predicted.
Local intelligence cannot substitute for missing global state.
highlights: exceed a shared budget in 5/5 runs

featuredPapers.title: Self-improving data synthesis enables scalable adaptation of embedding models
featuredPapers.authors: Zucan Lyu, Rui Tang, Jianlyu Chen
featuredPapers.summary:
AI agents require specialised retrieval across domains and tasks, but adapting embedding models is constrained by costly manual training-data design.

featuredPapers.title: IneqAgent: Agentic Inequality Proving in Lean with Symbolic Computation

featuredPapers.title: Co-Evolving Acting and Forecasting for Language Agents
featuredPapers.authors: Haofei Yu, Yixing Chen, Yining Zhao
featuredPapers.summary:
Training language agents is bottlenecked by the high cost of long-horizon rollouts, yet standard agentic reinforcement learning (RL) learns only from a terminal scalar reward, leaving the supervision in intermediate steps largely unused.
Prior work exploits this supervision through value targets that estimate per-step success probabilities or observation targets that fit environment response.
Both are hard to construct well: (1) value targets come from the same single scalar signal for each step in the trajectory, and (2) observation targets, such as web pages and terminal logs, are long and noisy and reach only one step ahead.
We propose CoPE, which adds a third kind of multi-step action targets.
On successful on-policy trajectories, CoPE trains the policy backbone to generate the action sequences that follows each history.
Each action is also supervised when forecast from the preceding histories, forming a temporal ensemble that the shared backbone absorbs during training, and this enables acting and forecasting to co-evolve.
The policy still acts one step at a time at inference, with no overhead.
Across five benchmarks (ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, WebShop, $\tau^2$-bench, and AppWorld), CoPE (1) achieves stronger aggregate performance than GRPO and RL baselines with predictive auxiliary targets across simulated environments, while improving overall performance on both realistic applications; (2) delivers up to $1.9\times$ and $2.0\times$ higher sample efficiency than ECHO and GRPO, respectively, on ScienceWorld; and (3) achieves these gains with a single policy backbone, without additional models, separate pretraining, or inference overhead.
The codebase is available at https://github.com/ulab-uiuc/CoPE.
highlights: We propose CoPE, which adds a third kind of multi-step action targets.

Second, we develop the 3DCodeVerse Harness, a multi-agent directed acyclic graph framework for generating and refining 3D content.

featuredPapers.title: The World Won't Wait: Evaluating and Teaching Agents Under a Live Clock
featuredPapers.authors: Ningxin Pan, Hanyu Li, Yeqing Shen
featuredPapers.summary:
Large language model (LLM) agents can solve complex interactive tasks, yet reasoning and tool calls take time.
In continuously changing environments, an otherwise correct action may arrive too late.
We introduce RealtimeBench, with 180 tasks across six game types, to evaluate agents while games continue running during inference.
Paired evaluations show that GPT-6.1-sol outperforms the faster Jev when games are paused, but falls behind when they keep running.
We propose Two-Timescale Offline Recursive Self-Improvement (TORSI): a slow teacher studies failures and tests corrections in paused games between attempts, then writes reusable instructions for a fast student.
The student acts without teacher calls during gameplay, and validation scores determine which updates are adopted.
Two rounds raise Jev's average test score from 13.51 to 24.19 on a 0--100 progress scale, improving all six game types.
The instructions also improve average scores for three other models without retuning.
These findings point toward real-time intelligence: enabling powerful LLM agents to remain effective in a continuously changing world by organizing deliberation, learning, and action across timescales.

featuredPapers.title: ARIA: Runtime Inspection and Amendment for Multi-Agent Systems
featuredPapers.authors: Bolin Shen, Yushun Dong
featuredPapers.summary:
In LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS), a local mistake can propagate as other agents build on it, turning a correctable error into a failed task.
Diagnosing completed runs or repeatedly re-executing them to search for corrections does not provide a learned policy for intervening while execution is still in progress.
We present Agent Runtime Inspection and Amendment (ARIA), a framework for learning when and how to repair ongoing multi-agent executions.
Our key intuition is to turn execution-verified repairs into reusable supervision, moving repair search into data construction and training so that a learned model can intervene at runtime without repeatedly testing alternatives.
First, we collect over 24{,}000 successful and failed trajectories across four multi-agent frameworks, six benchmarks, and eight host models.
From these trajectories, we construct the ARIA dataset, to our knowledge the first large-scale dataset pairing failed multi-agent trajectories with execution-verified repairs.
It contains 3{,}953 verified repair pairs, each specifying what went wrong, where to intervene, and how execution should continue.
Then, we develop the ARIA framework for MAS-agnostic runtime inspection and amendment, designed to integrate with any MAS that exposes execution trajectories and supports continuation replacement.
Using verified repairs as training examples, we teach a compact model to recognize when intervention is needed and how to correct an ongoing run.
The aim is to learn repair strategies that apply to related failures in new configurations, rather than merely reproduce individual corrections.
Finally, the trained ARIA model demonstrates strong repair performance in both post-hoc and runtime settings, with generalization to unseen frameworks and host models.
Our code is available at https://github.com/LabRAI/ARIA.
highlights: first large-scale dataset pairing failed multi-agent trajectories with execution-verified repairs

featuredPapers.title: ISW-Agent: Integrating LLM-Driven Dialogue with n8n Workflow for Internal Solitary Wave Remote Sensing Image Processing

featuredPapers.title: LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents
featuredPapers.authors: Qingni Wang, Changdae Oh, Yuzhe Yang
featuredPapers.summary:
Computer-use agents increasingly tackle long-horizon tasks, where running a frontier model at every step is expensive and a small open-weight model alone often fails.
Weak-to-strong escalation offers a middle ground where a weak agent acts by default and hands control to a strong one only when needed.
The core challenge is deciding when to escalate, which requires an uncertainty signal cheap enough to check at every step.
However, even after handoff, the strong agent can still get lost, but a black-box API that the strong agent is usually served exposes no internals to monitor.
To this end, we propose LEASH, a training-free framework that unleashes the strong agent only when the weak agent's latent uncertainty signals it is needed, and keeps it on a leash afterward.
LEASH has three layers: (1) initial task uncertainty for early routing, (2) step-level uncertainty for runtime escalation, and, after handoff, (3) a shadow observer for continued oversight of the strong black-box agent.
Here, we use latent uncertainty as a fuel for all three layers.
Specifically, we compare the weak model's hidden states with those from its past successful and failed trajectories, and a state that looks more like the failures signals higher uncertainty.
During weak-agent execution, our uncertainty estimator reuses activations already produced during action generation, so it needs no extra forward pass or dedicated monitor training.
Experiments on OSWorld across four contemporary model backbones show that LEASH consistently improves over standalone weak agents and outperforms random escalation by 6.55--11.94 points at matched escalation rates.
With Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, LEASH achieves 73.66% task success at $0.4117 per task, matching always-on Claude Opus 5 (72.90%) while reducing inference cost by 19.2%.
