papers.title: Dive into Claude Code: The Design Space of Today's and Future AI Agent Systems
papers.summary:
Claude Code is an agentic coding tool that can run shell commands, edit files, and call external services on behalf of the user.
This study describes its architecture by analyzing the publicly available source code and comparing it with two independent open-source AI agent systems, OpenClaw and Hermes Agent, that answer many of similar or even the same design questions. 本研究通过分析公开可用的源代码并将其与两个独立的开源AI代理系统OpenClaw和Hermes Agent进行比较来描述其架构，这两个系统回答了许多类似甚至相同的设计问题。
Our analysis identifies five human values, philosophies, and needs that motivate the architecture: human decision authority, safety, security, and privacy, reliable execution, capability amplification, and contextual adaptability. 我们的分析确定了激励架构的五种人类价值观、理念和需求：人类决策权威、安全、安保和隐私、可靠的执行、能力放大和情境适应性。
We then trace them through thirteen design principles to implementation choices. 然后，我们通过十三个设计原则来追溯它们的实施选择。
The core of the system is a simple while-loop that calls the model, runs tools, and repeats. 系统的核心是一个简单的while循环，调用模型、运行工具和重复。
Most of the code, however, lives in the systems around this loop: a permission system with seven modes and an ML-based classifier, a five-layer compaction pipeline for context management, four extensibility mechanisms (MCP, plugins, skills, and hooks), a subagent delegation and orchestration mechanism, and append-oriented session storage. 然而，大多数代码都存在于此循环周围的系统中：具有七种模式和基于ML的分类器的权限系统、用于上下文管理的五层压缩管道、四种可扩展性机制（ MCP、插件、技能和钩子）、子代理委派和编排机制以及面向附加的会话存储。
Comparisons with OpenClaw and Hermes Agent show that the same design questions produce different answers across three deployment contexts. 与OpenClaw和Hermes Agent的比较表明，相同的设计问题在三个部署环境中产生不同的答案。
Claude Code emphasizes per-action safety, OpenClaw emphasizes perimeter-level access, and Hermes renders per-action approvals across many surfaces. Claude Code强调每次行动的安全性， OpenClaw强调周边级别的访问， Hermès在许多表面上提供每次行动的批准。
At the runtime layer, Claude Code uses a single CLI loop, OpenClaw embeds the runtime within a gateway control plane, and Hermes uses one process whose role is set by its entry point. 在运行时层， Claude Code使用单个CLI循环， OpenClaw将运行时嵌入到网关控制平面中， Hermes使用一个由其入口点设置角色的进程。
At the context and extension layer, Claude Code extends the context window, OpenClaw registers gateway-wide capabilities, and Hermes provides pluggable memory and model backends. 在上下文和扩展层， Claude Code扩展了上下文窗口， OpenClaw注册了网关范围的功能， Hermes提供了可插拔的内存和模型后端。
We finally identify six open design directions for future agent systems, grounded in recent empirical, architectural, and policy literature. 最后，我们根据最近的实证、架构和政策文献，确定了未来代理系统的六个开放设计方向。

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: SPINE: Measuring LLM Sycophancy under Sustained Multi-Turn Pressure
papers.summary:
Large language models (LLMs) may abandon correct positions when users push back, exhibiting a failure mode known as sycophancy.
Existing evaluations typically use short, prespecified conversations and may therefore miss failures that emerge under sustained, adaptive disagreement.
We introduce SPINE, a benchmark in which an LLM proxy plays a persistent but mistaken user and adaptively challenges a target model for up to 25 turns.
We evaluate four commercial models (Claude Sonnet 5, GPT-5.6 Terra, Gemini 3.1 Pro, and DeepSeek V4 Pro) and three Olmo3-7b models on 100 false presuppositions and 100 unethical queries.
We define collapse as a target model abandoning the correct position and yielding to user pressure.
Our experimental results show that collapse rates increase with conversation length across post-trained models, with the overall rate rising from 0%-57% within 5 turns to 20%-97% within 25 turns depending on model and scenario.
These results show that evaluations limited to a few conversational turns underestimate sycophancy and resistance under sustained pressure remains unreliable across current models.
By analyzing models with accessible reasoning traces, we surprisingly found that the correct position often remains represented in the trace in 50%-89% of analyzed collapse turns, suggesting that the model chooses to please a user and sycophancy is not due to ignorance or the correct knowledge being overridden.
Ablations show that the SPINE protocol substantially increases the sycophantic collapse rate compared to pre-generated scripts.
Among all tactics, emotional appeals are most associated with inducing LLM sycophantic behavior, with position weakening in 44.3% of turns using this tactic.
Code, data, and transcripts will be released upon publication.
highlights: Large language models (LLMs) may abandon correct positions when users push back, exhibiting a failure mode known as syco

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: TimeWarp: Evaluating Web Agents by Revisiting the Past
papers.summary:
As web agents close the gap with humans on benchmarks, one question arises: Do today's agents perform just as well on tomorrow's web?
We introduce TimeWarp, a benchmark that emulates the evolving web.
TimeWarp consists of three web environments, each with six UI versions spanning UI design, frontend code, and workflows from different eras of the internet.
We pair TimeWarp with a set of complex, realistic tasks covering different forms of web navigation.
Our experiments reveal that vision-based agents are vulnerable to changes, while text-based agents become brittle once fine-tuned on a single version.
To address this, we propose TimeTraj, a new annotation method that uses plan distillation to collect trajectories across multiple versions.
By training agents on teacher rollouts using our BC-variant, we achieve substantial performance gains: 20.4% to 37.7% for Qwen-3 4B and 0% to 27.0% for Llama-3.1 8B models.
Our work helps study generalization across web designs and opens a new paradigm for collecting plans rather than trajectories to improve the robustness of web agents.

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: Evidence-First Agentic Verification
papers.summary:
Long-horizon, semi-verifiable agentic tasks often rely on rubric-based evaluation, but the evidence needed to assess these tasks can be spread across the environment state and the execution trace.
A judge may overlook this evidence or accept unsupported claims, including an agent's own reports of success.
When rubric verdicts serve as reinforcement-learning rewards, such errors can reinforce undesirable behavior.
We introduce Sauron, an evidence-first agentic verifier that investigates both state and trace and relies on a claim only after independently validating it against its source.
Bounded queries and joint investigation of related criteria reduce context use and redundant work, and each verdict carries an auditable receipt of its supporting evidence.
Across 2,586 human-labeled criteria from 100 personal-assistant episodes, Sauron achieves the highest F1 of five verifiers on all eight backbones tested while costing less than Gandalf, the strongest baseline.
With GPT-5.6 Sol, it reaches 0.96 F1 versus Gandalf's 0.92 at 23% lower cost, with a wider margin on process criteria.
On a paired fault-injection suite covering 13 families, several of which simulate reward hacking, Sauron detects 97% of injected failures while flagging only 2% of clean controls, outperforming baselines even when they are given the full trace.
On TRAIL, a benchmark for detecting and localizing real agent errors, Sauron leads both Gandalf and TRAIL's own judge on all three quality metrics.
highlights: outperforming baselines even when they are given the full trace
first agentic verifier that investigates both state and trace and relies on a claim only after independently validating
A judge may overlook this evidence or accept unsupported claims, including an agent's own reports of success.

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: TopoPilot: Reliable Conversational Workflow Automation for Topological Data Analysis and Visualization
papers.summary:
Recent agentic systems demonstrate that large language models can generate complex codebases from natural language prompts.
Despite this progress, they present reliability concerns for scientific visualization due to invalid operations, subtle errors, and failure to resolve underspecified inputs.
These challenges are compounded in real-world workflows that exceed the complexity of standard benchmarks.
In this work, we introduce TopoPilot, a reliable and extensible agentic framework for automating complex scientific visualization workflows.
We focus on topological data analysis and visualization as a primary use case, while designing the framework to generalize to broader visualization domains.
TopoPilot employs a two-agent architecture: an orchestrator translates user prompts into workflows composed of atomic backend actions, while a verifier evaluates workflows prior to execution.
Its modular design isolates components and supports new topological descriptors and domain-specific workflows without modifying the core system.
It also employs numerous deterministic guardrails to ensure semantic consistency and accurate execution.
To systematically improve reliability, we develop a taxonomy of failure modes and employ targeted safeguards for each class of error.
Across 1,000 simulated multi-turn conversations spanning 100 prompts, including adversarial and infeasible requests, TopoPilot achieves a success rate exceeding 95%, compared with under 50% for a baseline without comprehensive guardrails and verification.
We also show that TopoPilot outperforms Claude Code and Codex on similar prompts in terms of accuracy, completion time, and token usage.
highlights: exceed the complexity of standard benchmarks

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: REMORY: Learning Residual Memory for Context Compaction
papers.summary:
Long-horizon agents compact their history to continue within a finite context window, but a textual summary alone may not support every subsequent decision.
We introduce REMORY, a neural memory network that supplements the summary with a bounded sequence of soft memory tokens.
Given the history and summary, the network learns to generate tokens that help a frozen LLM approximate the continuation it would produce with the full history.
The tokens are conditioned on the summary and appended after it, forming an analogue of a residual connection along the sequence dimension.
On SummHay, REMORY improves source attribution at nearly unchanged insight coverage and approaches the full-context joint score using only 5.2% of the input positions.
Across long-horizon agent benchmarks, Qwen3.8-27B and GLM-5.3-Flash show consistent gains with residual memory.
Both models also exhibit substantially fewer repeated tool outputs and tool errors on BrowseComp and Terminal-Bench 2.1.
highlights: We introduce REMORY, a neural memory network that supplements the summary with a bounded sequence of soft memory tokens.

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: RewardHarness: Self-Evolving Agentic Post-Training
papers.summary:
Aligning generative models with human preferences remains a central challenge.
While RLHF is widely adopted, it relies on large-scale preference data.
This limitation is particularly evident in evaluating instruction-guided image edits, even though humans can often learn such preferences from only a few examples.
We present RewardHarness, a training-free, self-evolving agentic reward framework that reframes reward modeling as context evolution rather than weight optimization.
Instead of learning from large-scale annotations, RewardHarness aligns with human preferences by iteratively evolving a library of tools and skills from as few as 100 preference demonstrations.
Given a source image, an edited image, and an editing instruction, an orchestrator agent selects the most relevant subset of tools and skills from the maintained library, and sub-agents invoke them to construct a reasoning chain that produces a reward score.
By comparing predicted scores with ground-truth preferences and analyzing successes and failures in the reasoning process, the orchestrator automatically refines its library of tools and skills without additional human annotation.
Using only 0.05% of the EditReward preference data, RewardHarness achieves 47.4% average accuracy on EditReward-Bench K=2/3/4 and GenAI-Bench, surpassing GPT-5 by 5.3 points.
When used as a reward signal in FlowGRPO, RL-tuned models achieve 3.52 on ImgEdit-Bench.
Code and model are available at the project page: https://rewardharness.com/
highlights: Aligning generative models with human preferences remains a central challenge.

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: OxyGen: Unified KV Cache Management for VLA Inference under Multi-Task Parallelism
papers.summary:
Embodied AI agents increasingly require parallel execution of multiple tasks, such as manipulation, conversation, and memory construction, from shared observations under distinct time constraints.
Recent Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) Vision-Language-Action Models (VLAs) support such heterogeneous outputs, yet existing inference systems incur redundant computation and resource contention when serving concurrent tasks on-device.
We identify isolated KV cache management as the root cause.
To address this, we propose unified KV cache management, an inference design that treats the KV cache as a first-class shared resource across tasks and control cycles.
This abstraction enables two key optimizations: cross-task KV sharing eliminates redundant prefill of shared observations, while cross-frame continuous batching batches unfinished language requests from different frames and advances them within a per-frame decoding budget.
We implement this design in OxyGen and evaluate $\pi_{0.5}$ on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 and Jetson AGX Thor.
OxyGen achieves up to 3.7$\times$ speedup over isolated execution, delivering over 200 tokens/s language throughput and 70 Hz action frequency simultaneously on RTX 4090.
We also validate the design on Xiaomi-Robotics-0 and StarVLA across different backbones and expert configurations.
We further demonstrate the inference gains on a humanoid robot with on-board Jetson AGX Thor.
highlights: We identify isolated KV cache management as the root cause.

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: AI Discovery in Combinatorics: From Problems to Solutions and Back to Bigger Problems
papers.summary:
We introduce $qt$Bench, a benchmark of 29 open problems in algebraic combinatorics.
These problems ask for a simple combinatorial algorithm that explains given polynomial coefficients or identities.
To help AI agents search for such algorithms, we provide a scaffold for playing with combinatorial objects, countering cheating attempts, and testing candidate solutions.
To explore how far frontier AI systems can go on these problems, we collaborated with OpenAI, whose researchers obtained proposed solutions to several of them.
This highlights bigger meta-problems: is AI discovery at scale ethical?
How should these results be released?
How should proof digestion be organized?
We discuss these questions and give our views.
highlights: We introduce $qt$Bench, a benchmark of 29 open problems in algebraic combinatorics.

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: Learning Adaptive Deliberation Control for Reliable Recognition with Multi-Agent Language Models
papers.summary:
Multi-agent deliberation can improve recognition by criticizing and revising candidate answers, but fixed controls cannot respond to changes in disagreement or reasoning quality.
We present an adaptive multi-agent controller (ADMA) that learns continuous policies for proposal, challenge, arbitration, and coordination while keeping the task model frozen.
Shared trace features describe quality, agreement, and progress, while role-specific features support decentralized control during inference.
One controller trained on legal and financial reasoning is transferred without policy updates to four textual and multimodal benchmarks and two successive task-model versions.
With Qwen3.5 held fixed, ADMA-Full improves accuracy by 6.2-14.2 percentage points over Direct and by 2.8-3.0 points over ADMA-Fixed.
Paired bootstrap ranges for the Full-Fixed comparison are positive on three tasks.
Outcome decompositions show that recoveries exceed introduced errors, while process assessment records fewer false-consensus events and more supported correct outcomes.
Transfer to Qwen3.6 remains task dependent, which bounds the generality of the learned policy.
Median token and latency ratios are 14.3-18.7 and 7.8-16.5 relative to Direct.
These results show that adaptive deliberation can improve fixed-model recognition when its task-dependent gains justify the additional computation.
highlights: Learning Adaptive Deliberation Control for Reliable Recognition with Multi

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: Iterate on an LLM, Serve on an SLM
papers.summary:
As frontier LLMs gain more capabilities, the cost to run them also goes up.
At the same time, small language models (SLMs) also gain more capabilities but have largely been able to keep their cost stable, offering 5-40 times cheaper inference for the narrow, repetitive subtasks that agents decompose work into.
However, the standing limiting factor is getting the correct behavior out of a small model in a fast, efficient, and economical way.
Unfortunately, in most cases, zero-shot small models fail narrow production tasks.
Furthermore, retraining one every time the behavior changes is too slow to iterate on.
We propose doing both in sequence.
First, develop the desired behavior in prompt space, on a frontier model, with immediate feedback from live traffic.
Then, once the behavior converges, distill the recorded production behavior (not synthetic imitations of it) into an SLM through supervised fine-tuning (SFT).
We show a proper use case of this method through a scheduling agent for home-care agencies that fans out a single yes/no safety decision per caregiver-shift pair on GPT-5.4-nano.
A LoRA-tuned Qwen3-8B trained on 11.6k recorded production decisions reaches 0.913 agreement, while the teacher (GPT-5.4-nano), re-run on its own recorded prompts, agrees with itself only 72.7% of the time, pointing to the fact that the SLM may also be more consistent.
Furthermore, when the two disagreed, a blinded professional scheduler sided with the student 48-29.
Finally, we find that the SLM has approximately 2.5 times lower median latency and is a fraction of the cost.
We believe this lifecycle of quick building, live feedback, and cheap inference is a blueprint for others building similar systems.
highlights: As frontier LLMs gain more capabilities, the cost to run them also goes up.
However, the standing limiting factor is getting the correct behavior out of a small model in a fast, efficient, and eco

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: Beyond Successful Play: Diagnosing Opponent Modeling in Large Language Models
papers.summary:
Language-model agents are expected to adapt to others whose behavior changes through interaction.
Yet adaptation may rely on learned behavioral patterns rather than theory of mind (ToM): the ability to infer others' mental states, including beliefs and intentions.
We introduce a benchmark and diagnostic framework for repeated hide-and-seek against algorithmic opponents with explicitly defined recursive belief updates.
Their ground-truth beliefs and action probabilities let us distinguish adaptive play, action prediction, and belief tracking through live interaction, fixed-history evaluation, and controlled information interventions.
With structured elicitation and behavioral supervised fine-tuning (SFT), we find improved play in several tested settings, but diagnostics reveal limitations in opponent prediction and belief tracking.
We test whether supervising opponent action probabilities can address this predictive deficit in Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct.
Predictions improve when the model is told the opponent's type and parameter settings, but become less accurate when it must infer the opponent from history without this information.
Training on examples that also omit these details reduces the gap, although improvements vary across opponents.
Is this limitation specific to smaller open-weight models, or does it also appear in a frontier model?
GPT-5.4 also benefits from correct opponent beliefs: supplying them improves its predictions and choices, whereas deeper explicit belief reports and self-generated memory do not consistently improve forecasting from interaction history.
This contrast suggests that using useful belief information is easier than inferring it autonomously, even for a frontier model.
Together, our findings distinguish improved play and action prediction from reliable belief tracking, providing a framework for evaluating mentalizing and testing targeted improvements.
highlights: introduce a benchmark and diagnostic framework

papers.groupName: 重点跟进（产业界 / 端云结合）
papers.title: Memory Echo in Single-Agent Long-Term Memory: Lifecycle Evaluation and Provenance-Guided Mitigation
papers.summary:
Long-term memory supports agents across sessions.
Repeated retrieval and write-back can let one historical claim occupy multiple retrieval positions and influence current answers without independent evidence.
Existing work examines retrieval, updating, and question answering, leaving same-source record accumulation and post-correction persistence underexplored.
Motivated by research in social cognition and memory psychology on repeated exposure, retrieval, and revision, we define \emph{Memory Echo} as the excess retrieval exposure gained by historical information from the same source without additional independent evidence, and introduce MEchoBench to evaluate its emergence, correction resistance, persistence, and effect on answers.
To address this phenomenon, we introduce the Family--Provenance--Authority framework (FPA).
Specifically, FPA selects one representative per source family, conditions the eligibility of old records for the answer context on verified corrections, and constrains final answers with authoritative evidence.
In paired replay on 190 fixed questions across four memory frameworks, FPA raises accuracy from 0.825 to 0.920 with DeepSeek V4 Flash and from 0.782 to 0.916 with Kimi K2.6; mean Decision Contamination Effect falls from 0.106 to 0.030 and from 0.109 to 0.038, respectively.
These results show that agent memory can preserve traceable history without allowing repeated historical information to govern current decisions.
The code is available at https://github.com/OrcasSam/memory-echo-benchmark.

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: VideoHarness-SRSI: Structured Recursive Self-Improvement for Video Understanding Harness
papers.summary:
LLM system capabilities depend not only on model parameters but also on the executable harnesses that organize information acquisition, tool use, reasoning, and memory. LLM系统功能不仅取决于模型参数，还取决于组织信息采集、工具使用、推理和内存的可执行线束。
Recursive harness evolution can automate their design, but how it can reliably discover generalizable systems from limited, noisy, and repeatedly reused feedback remains unclear. 递归线束的演进可以实现其设计的自动化，但它如何从有限、嘈杂和重复使用的反馈中可靠地发现可推广的系统尚不清楚。
We study this question in agentic video understanding, where rich multimodal evidence and coupled mechanisms make harness optimization challenging. 我们在代理视频理解中研究这个问题，丰富的多模态证据和耦合机制使线束优化具有挑战性。
We first introduce VideoHarness-BRSI, a recursive self-improvement framework that evolves video harnesses around a frozen vision-language model. 我们首先介绍VideoHarness-BRSI ，这是一个递归自我改进框架，围绕冻结的视觉语言模型发展视频线束。
Analyzing over 4,000 evolved candidates, we find it competitive with hand-engineered systems but identify three interconnected failure modes: validation overfitting, search-budget dilution, and the early-experience trap. 我们分析了4000多名进化的候选者，发现它与手工系统有竞争力，但确定了三种相互关联的故障模式：验证过拟合、搜索预算稀释和早期体验陷阱。
We trace all three to a common root: the same imperfect validation evidence drives both harness revisions and the proposer's search strategy. 我们将这三者追溯到一个共同的根源：相同的不完美验证证据推动了线束修订和提案者的搜索策略。
We therefore propose VideoHarness-SRSI, an evidence-governed framework in which every search decision rests on evidence that is transferable, sufficient, and gathered before the search commits. 因此，我们提出了VideoHarness-SRSI ，这是一个证据管理的框架，其中每个搜索决定都依赖于在搜索提交之前可转移、充分和收集的证据。
It restricts the proposer to content-free feedback, informs exploration with instrumented warm-up experiments, and develops mechanisms in isolated probe-race branches before factorial composition and joint refinement. 它将提议者限制为无内容反馈，通过仪器预热实验为探索提供信息，并在析因组合和关节细化之前在孤立的探针-竞赛分支中开发机制。
Across four video understanding benchmarks, VideoHarness-SRSI improves the equally weighted mean held-out score by 6.2% relative to VideoHarness-BRSI and reduces the mean validation-test gap by 37.9%. 在四个视频理解基准中， VideoHarness-SRSI相对于VideoHarness-BRSI将同等加权的平均保留分数提高了6.2% ，并将平均验证测试差距缩小了37.9%。
Reliable harness evolution thus depends on how search is organized and informed, not only on how well it optimizes validation performance. 因此，可靠的线束进化取决于搜索的组织和知情方式，而不仅仅是它优化验证性能的程度。

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Get In, Decide, Prove: A Merchant-Side Readiness Benchmark for Agentic Commerce
papers.summary:
AI agents now browse and buy on people's behalf, and benchmarks measure how well the agents perform. 人工智能代理现在代表人们浏览和购买，基准衡量代理的表现。
Far less is known about the other side of the transaction: whether a merchant's website lets an agent in, publishes terms precise enough to decide a purchase, and leaves evidence of what was agreed. 对交易的另一方面知之甚少：商家的网站是否允许代理进入，发布足够精确的条款以决定购买，并留下已达成协议的证据。
This paper presents a merchant-side benchmark built on those three questions and reports a pilot of it. 本文提出了基于这三个问题的商家侧基准，并报告了其试点。
The central measurement, decision sufficiency, rates each criterion of a concrete buyer mandate (total cost, cancellation or return terms, service date, variant identity) as determinate, indeterminate, or unknown from the merchant's own published evidence. 根据商家自己公布的证据，中央测量、决策充分性、具体买家授权的每个标准（总成本、取消或退货条款、服务日期、变体身份）为确定、不确定或未知。
Readiness scores carry their evidence coverage and missingness bounds; access is reported separately for a declared bot, a declared headless browser, and a user-present browser; and each observed term is mapped to the RAILS admissibility class of the evidence that could support it in a dispute. 准备情况分数包含其证据覆盖范围和缺失范围；对于已声明的机器人、已声明的无头浏览器和用户存在的浏览器，访问权限分别报告；并且每个观察到的术语都映射到可能在争议中支持其的证据的轨道可接受性类别。
Four large merchants received the full assessment: three refused the declared profiles at their offer pages, and no mandate could be confirmed as met, because each merchant left a total or a refund term undetermined. 四家大型商家接受了完整的评估：三家商家在其优惠页面上拒绝了已申报的个人资料，并且无法确认是否符合要求，因为每家商家都留下了总额或未确定的退款期限。
An access census of 555 sites of merchants that two payment processors publicly name as clients found the home page unreadable to both declared profiles at 105 sites (18.9%). 对两家支付处理商公开命名为客户的555个商家网站的访问普查发现， 105个网站（ 18.9% ）的两个已声明的个人资料都无法读取主页。
A declared assessment of 330 merchants, scored by deterministic rules without a rater, found that evidence coverage rather than the score decides who can be ranked: 115 merchants (35%) reached the ranking threshold, rankable profiles scored a median of 89 to 90, and material terms was the one pillar well below the others, because the all-in total was decidable at 18 merchants. 在没有评分者的情况下，对330家商家进行了公开评估，发现证据覆盖率而不是得分决定了谁可以排名： 115家商家（ 35 ％ ）达到了排名门槛，可排名的个人资料得分中位数为89至90 ，而物质条件是远低于其他的一个支柱，因为总共18家商家是可以决定的。
The pilot shows that the measurements can be taken; it does not validate them or rank merchants, and the weights and the projected clearing band await validation against outcomes. 试点表明可以进行测量；它不会验证它们或对商家进行排名，并且权重和预计的清算区间正在等待对结果的验证。
highlights: AI agents now browse and buy on people's behalf, and benchmarks measure how well the agents perform.

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: LLM Value Functions for Credit Assignment in Agentic RL
papers.summary:
Reinforcement learning (RL) for large language model (LLM) agents remains challenging in long-horizon tasks with sparse outcome rewards, where assigning credit to individual actions is difficult. 大型语言模型（ LLM ）代理的强化学习（ RL ）在具有稀疏结果奖励的长期任务中仍然具有挑战性，在这些任务中，很难为个人行为分配信用。
Methods such as GRPO assign the same trajectory-level advantage to all actions, while critic-based methods require learning an additional value function that can be costly and unstable. 诸如GRPO之类的方法为所有操作分配相同的轨迹级优势，而基于批评者的方法需要学习一个额外的价值函数，这可能是昂贵和不稳定的。
We introduce LLM Value Function RL (LVRL), which uses the pretrained knowledge and in-context learning ability of an LLM to estimate policy-aware state values without finetuning a separate critic. 我们引入了LLM值函数RL （ LVRL ） ，它使用LLM的预训练知识和上下文学习能力来估计策略感知状态值，而无需微调单独的批评者。
LVRL conditions the value model on group context and calibrates its predictions using known values at the initial and terminal states, enabling step-level credit assignment from estimated value differences. LVRL根据组上下文调整价值模型，并使用初始和最终状态下的已知值校准其预测，从而实现从估计值差异的阶梯级信用分配。
We further extend this idea to learning from an expert policy through on-policy distillation (OPD), introducing LLM Value Function OPD (LVOPD), which focuses teacher supervision on actions associated with decreases in estimated value. 我们进一步扩展了这一理念，通过政策提炼（ OPD ）从专家政策中学习，引入了LLM价值函数OPD （ LVOPD ） ，将教师监督的重点放在与估计价值降低相关的行动上。
We evaluate our approach across diverse agentic benchmarks: AppWorld, BabyAI, and SWE-bench Verified. 我们在不同的代理基准上评估我们的方法： AppWorld、BabyAI和SWE-bench Verified。
Across policy scales (4B to 32B), LVRL consistently and substantially outperforms both GRPO and PPO. 在政策量表（ 4B至32B ）中， LVRL的表现始终如一且大幅优于GRPO和PPO。
On AppWorld and SWE-bench Verified, LVRL yields absolute improvements of up to 13.6 and 8.6 percentage points over GRPO. 在AppWorld和SWE-bench Verified上， LVRL比GRPO提高了高达13.6和8.6个百分点。
Notably, on tasks requiring extended exploration like BabyAI, LVRL bridges the gap from total failure to 75.0% success. 值得注意的是，在像BabyAI这样需要扩展探索的任务上， LVRL弥合了从完全失败到75.0%成功的差距。
Furthermore, LVOPD yields consistent improvements over standard distillation baselines on AppWorld. 此外， LVOPD在AppWorld上的标准蒸馏基线上产生了一致的改进。
Finally, Monte-Carlo analysis confirms that our frozen critic accurately identifies semantic pitfalls and recoveries, proving that LVRL extracts robust, policy-aware step-level credit from sparse terminal outcomes. 最后，蒙特卡洛分析证实，我们的冷冻评论家准确地识别了语义陷阱和恢复，证明LVRL从稀疏的终端结果中提取了稳健的、具有政策意识的阶梯级信用。
highlights: We evaluate our approach across diverse agentic benchmarks: AppWorld, BabyAI, and SWE-bench Verified.

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Drafting Agents, Not Just Tokens: Speculative Recursive Self-Improvement for Agentic Systems
papers.summary:
Improving an agent through successive revisions requires balancing exploration and evaluation under a limited budget. 通过连续修订改进代理需要在有限的预算下平衡探索和评估。
A narrow search can miss useful sequences of edits, while fully evaluating every intermediate version can exhaust the budget before those sequences yield a verified improvement. 狭隘的搜索可能会错过有用的编辑序列，而充分评估每个中间版本可能会在这些序列产生经过验证的改进之前耗尽预算。
We introduce Speculative Recursive Self-Improvement (SpecRSI), which drafts executable successor agents before their predecessors are fully evaluated, while requiring complete verification before adoption. 我们引入了推测递归自我改进（ SpecRSI ） ，它在可执行后继代理的前身得到充分评估之前起草可执行后继代理，同时要求在采用之前进行完整的验证。
Verification-Aware Tree Search (VATS) allocates the budget between further edits and outstanding checks using the predicted verified return of a continuation. 验证感知树搜索（ VATS ）使用预测的连续验证回报，在进一步编辑和未完成检查之间分配预算。
Group Verification Optimization (GVO) learns the improver from completed searches while keeping the real evaluator fixed. 组验证优化（ GVO ）从已完成的搜索中学习改进者，同时保持真实评估者的固定状态。
In the main scientific comparison, terminal gains exceed Janus by 33.3%--40.0%. 在主要的科学比较中，终端增益超过Janus 33.3% --40.0%。
Additional evaluations show that SpecRSI outperforms Janus in all 50 scientific backbone--task pairs and exceeds MetaRSI-v1 by 1.85%--2.38% in macro-average system score across twenty backbones. 其他评估显示， SpecRSI在所有50个科学骨干（任务对）中的表现优于Janus ，并且在20个骨干的宏观平均系统得分中超过MetaRSI-v1 1.85% - -2.38%。
Coding-validation success reaches 69.4% versus HGM's 64.3% at a 20.8% lower target-cost index. 编码验证成功率达到69.4% ，而HGM为64.3% ，目标成本指数较低20.8%。

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: APT: Feedback-Driven Agentic Post-Training for Text-to-Image Generation
papers.summary:
Post-training is crucial for improving text-to-image models, yet existing pipelines typically rely on manually curated training data and fixed training distributions. 训练后对于改进文本到图像模型至关重要，但现有的管道通常依赖于手动策划的训练数据和固定的训练分布。
We introduce APT (Agentic Post-Training), a fully automated framework that adaptively post-trains a base model according to its evolving capability profile. 我们引入了APT （ Agentic Post-Training ） ，这是一个完全自动化的框架，可根据其不断发展的能力配置文件自适应地对基本模型进行后期训练。
APT coordinates three agents to construct evaluation sets from user requirements, diagnose model-specific strengths and failure modes, and generate reinforcement learning data with an adaptive prompt distribution that emphasizes underperforming capabilities. APT协调三个代理从用户需求构建评估集，诊断模型特定的优势和失败模式，并生成具有自适应提示分布的强化学习数据，该分布强调表现不佳的能力。
By repeatedly evaluating, diagnosing, and updating the generator, APT lets the current model's behavior shape its next training tasks, forming a feedback loop inspired by recursive self-improvement. 通过反复评估、诊断和更新生成器， APT让当前模型的行为塑造其下一个训练任务，形成一个受递归自我改进启发的反馈循环。
For general-purpose settings without user-specified evaluation scenarios, we further develop an evaluation harness that enables broad and diverse evaluation set generation. 对于没有用户指定评估场景的通用设置，我们进一步开发了一种评估线束，可实现广泛而多样的评估集生成。
Experiments across multiple base models, benchmarks, and generation architectures demonstrate that APT is model-agnostic, benchmark-agnostic, architecture-agnostic, and fully automated. 跨多个基本模型、基准和生成架构的实验表明， APT与模型无关、与基准无关、与架构无关且完全自动化。

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: AgentFly: Scaling Agentic Reinforcement Learning with Unified Resource System
papers.summary:
Methods to build LLM agents have evolved from prompt engineering and supervised finetuning to agentic reinforcement learning (agentic RL). 构建LLM代理的方法已经从提示工程和监督微调演变为代理强化学习（ agentic RL ）。
However, agentic RL remains bottlenecked by its surrounding systems: agents must interact with heterogeneous environments, such as sandboxes, model services, and external APIs. 然而，代理RL仍然受到其周围系统的瓶颈：代理必须与异构环境交互，例如沙盒、模型服务和外部API。
Their allocation, reuse, and lifecycle dominate rollout cost and cap the scale at which training becomes practical. 它们的分配、重用和生命周期主导了推出成本，并限制了培训变得实用的规模。
In this work, we present AgentFly, an agentic RL framework built with a unified resource layer that treats each of these environments as a distinct, typed resource scheduled through one engine, with per-tool acquisition for multi-turn reuse, asynchronous backpressure, and rollout versus global-scoped lifecycles. 在这项工作中，我们介绍了AgentFly ，这是一个使用统一资源层构建的代理RL框架，它将每个环境视为通过一个引擎调度的独特的类型化资源，每个工具获取用于多回合重用、异步背压和推出与全局范围的生命周期。
AgentFly adopts a four-layer design: (I) agent layer that abstracts the agent, tool, and reward concepts, decomposing agentic RL into defining agents, tools, and reward functions; (II) rollout layer that composes these into agent loops and computes rewards; (III) context layer that organizes rollouts, injects contextual information, and arranges resources; and (IV) a low-level resource layer that performs resource management. AgentFly采用四层设计： （ I ）抽象代理、工具和奖励概念的代理层，将代理RL分解为定义代理、工具和奖励功能； （ II ）将其组合成代理循环并计算奖励的推出层； （ III ）组织推出、注入上下文信息并安排资源的上下文层； （ IV ）执行资源管理的底层资源层。
We provide a suite of prebuilt tools and environments, demonstrate successful agent training across multiple tasks and models, and report the first controlled cross-framework throughput comparison against agentic RL frameworks. 我们提供一套预构建的工具和环境，展示跨多个任务和模型的成功代理培训，并报告与代理RL框架的首次受控跨框架吞吐量比较。
highlights: first controlled cross-framework throughput comparison against agentic RL frameworks

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: RoboGaze: Evaluating Robot World Models via Structured Vision-Language Analysis
papers.summary:
Robot world models now generate synthetic manipulation videos, but evaluating them is hard: realistic-looking outputs often violate physical laws, temporal consistency or task logic, while conventional metrics and monolithic Vision-Language Model (VLM) judges return scores that do not say what failed. 机器人世界模型现在生成合成操纵视频，但评估它们很困难：逼真的输出往往违反物理定律、时间一致性或任务逻辑，而传统指标和单片视觉语言模型（ VLM ）法官返回的分数并不能说明失败的原因。
We present RoboGaze, a training-free multi-agent VLM evaluator that grounds the task and scene, routes each subtask to dimension-specific specialists and verifies their findings with a critic, producing temporally localized diagnostic reports that state what failed, when, why and how severely, under a schema of 6 dimensions and 30 failure types whose annotation reliability and coverage we measure.
To benchmark it, we introduce RoboGazeBench, 914 human-annotated clips from five generators, conditioned on simulated and real-world data and running from 4.9 to 148.9 s.
Across eight open-source and proprietary VLM backbones, RoboGaze outperforms every baseline; even a published agentic detector given the same schema and a slightly larger inference budget trails it by 10.1-12.3 description-F1 points, a margin that blinded human raters confirm.
On the strongest backbone it closes 83% of the gap between chain-of-thought prompting and human agreement, and its critic curbs the "cry-wolf" false positives of standard VLMs, lifting mean clean-clip accuracy from 17% to 85%.
The advantage is largest on held-out generators and long clips, and carries over to selecting generated demonstrations (80% vs.
71% precision).
highlights: outperforms every baseline; even a published agentic detector given the same schema and a slightly larger inference budg

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: AdaRSI: On-Demand Recursive Self-Improvement for Embodied Agents
papers.summary:
Pretrained vision-language-action models (VLAs) often fail midway through unseen long-horizon tasks.
Recursive self-improvement (RSI) offers a remedy, but embodied RSI methods either refine the harness around a frozen executor and so cannot add a missing motion, or train the executor on persistent failures without asking whether a failure lies in how the executor is called or in what it can do.
We ask when a self-improving embodied system should change the weights of its executor, and propose AdaRSI, an on-demand RSI framework for embodied agents.
A coding agent first improves its skills and harness, then attributes persistent failures by retrying failing sub-steps from saved states, and fine-tunes only the sub-steps that remain unreliable, with demonstrations it collects itself and experience carried over from earlier tasks.
On all 50 target tasks of RoboCasa365, with GR00T N1.5 as the executor and no human demonstrations, AdaRSI improves the VLA on all three suites and raises its success on unseen composite tasks from 4.6% to 13.8%.
Compared with fine-tuning every sub-step, it reaches slightly higher success while using only 28% of the GPU time and 22% of the self-collected demonstrations, and fine-tuning without a harness trains more yet gains far less.
highlights: first improves its skills and harness

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Agents Don't Just Agree, They Remember: Benchmarking Persistent Sycophancy in Self-Improving Personal Agents
papers.summary:
Self-improving personal agents write profiles, memories, and reusable skills that carry over from one chat to the next.
Prior works ask whether a model agrees with the user in its next reply.
Yet these agents can also write down a claim the user made, and a later chat can read that note back as trusted context.
We call this persistent sycophancy.
We introduce the Personal Agent Sycophancy Benchmark, PASB, with 1,600 tasks run on two agent frameworks, Hermes-Agent and OpenClaw, across sixteen models that span scales and generations.
Each task separates a first chat containing the claim from a follow-up chat in a fresh session, so the first chat can reach the follow-up only through a note the agent chose to write.
Downstream failure, the rate at which follow-up answers still rely on the claim, reaches 68.1% when the agent saved the claim against 35.6% when it did not.
Later generations fail less often, yet a saved note still more than doubles their failure rate.
In 38.8% of runs the saved note states the claim with more authority than the user gave it, and a saved claim still shapes answers in a different domain.
Among four mitigations, editing the stored note works better than correcting the agent in conversation, cutting same-domain downstream failure from 36.3% to 30.3% for Hermes-Agent and from 37.9% to 31.6% for OpenClaw.
A strong instruction against saving brings failure back to the level of runs that saved nothing.
Self-improving agents need controls on what they write to memory as well as on what they say.
Our benchmark is available at https://github.com/henrymao2004/agent-sycophancy.
highlights: first chat containing the claim from a follow-up chat in a fresh session
Agents Don't Just Agree, They Remember

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Co-Evolving Acting and Forecasting for Language Agents
papers.summary:
Training language agents is bottlenecked by the high cost of long-horizon rollouts, yet standard agentic reinforcement learning (RL) learns only from a terminal scalar reward, leaving the supervision in intermediate steps largely unused.
Prior work exploits this supervision through value targets that estimate per-step success probabilities or observation targets that fit environment response.
Both are hard to construct well: (1) value targets come from the same single scalar signal for each step in the trajectory, and (2) observation targets, such as web pages and terminal logs, are long and noisy and reach only one step ahead.
We propose \name, which adds a third kind of multi-step action targets.
On successful on-policy trajectories, \name trains the policy backbone to generate the action sequences that follows each history.
Each action is also supervised when forecast from the preceding histories, forming a temporal ensemble that the shared backbone absorbs during training, and this enables acting and forecasting to co-evolve.
The policy still acts one step at a time at inference, with no overhead.
Across five benchmarks (ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, WebShop, $\tau^2$-bench, and AppWorld), \name (1) achieves stronger aggregate performance than GRPO and RL baselines with predictive auxiliary targets across simulated environments, while improving overall performance on both realistic applications; (2) delivers up to $1.9\times$ and $2.0\times$ higher sample efficiency than ECHO and GRPO, respectively, on ScienceWorld; and (3) achieves these gains with a single policy backbone, without additional models, separate pretraining, or inference overhead.
The codebase is available at https://github.com/ulab-uiuc/CoPE.
highlights: We propose \name, which adds a third kind of multi-step action targets.

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Rollout-Time Intervention: Unlocking Agentic Reinforcement Learning Beyond Policy Limits
papers.summary:
Reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as a key paradigm for improving large language model (LLM) agents, enabling stronger reasoning, planning, and tool-use in interactive environments.
However, existing agent RL methods remain fundamentally constrained by an on-policy reasoning bottleneck: when tasks exceed the model's current capability boundary, effective trajectories become extremely sparse and training often collapses.
We introduce Rollout-Time Intervention (RTI), a technique designed to elicit successful trajectories beyond the policy's intrinsic exploration capacity.
RTI operates by leveraging reward-side evidence (i.e., evaluation rubrics) during rollout to convert erroneous trajectories into successful ones, providing effective learning signals for tasks that the policy rarely solves on its own.
Although intervention trajectories are inherently off-policy, we find that they can effectively guide policy optimization when trajectories with excessive distributional shifts are filtered out.
Extensive experiments across five benchmarks demonstrate that RTI consistently outperforms RL baselines, enabling the post-trained policy to approach the performance of substantially stronger contemporary LLMs and, more importantly, transcend its original capability boundary.
The code is available at https://github.com/Alibaba-NLP/qqr.
highlights: exceed the model's current capability boundary

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Memory as a Controlled Process: Learned Adaptive Memory Management for LLM Agents
papers.summary:
Large Language Model (LLM) agents increasingly rely on external memory systems to accumulate experience across tasks.
Yet nearly all existing approaches, from graph-structured memories to reflective insight stores, access memory through fixed, hand-designed heuristics.
We argue that this static view of memory is a core bottleneck for agentic learning because optimal memory behavior is fundamentally context-dependent.
The early stages of the tasks, benefit from minimal retrieval because memory is sparse; recurring goal types benefit from plan reuse rather than generic nearest-neighbor lookup; stuck agents benefit from re-retrieval with alternative queries; and across long task streams, the memory store itself must be consolidated and pruned to remain useful.
We present Memory as a Controlled Process (MemCon), a framework that models memory operations as a Markov Decision Process and learns an online policy that adaptively decides when, what, and how much to retrieve, when to inject a distilled plan, and when to consolidate or forget.
MemCon is backend-agnostic: it wraps any existing memory implementation, learns from task-by-task binary feedback with no pretraining and no additional LLM calls, and uses a lightweight tabular contextual bandit with UCB exploration that converges within tens of tasks.
Across 6 benchmarks, 3 agent frameworks, and 3 LLM backbones, MemCon consistently outperforms multiple memory baselines by up to 15.2 points in task success while reducing token consumption by 5--20%.
highlights: outperforms multiple memory baselines by up to 15

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: More Methods, Better Agents? A Reality Check on Self-Distillation in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary:
Self-distillation in agentic reinforcement learning has produced a growing number of methods.
However, existing evaluations often reuse published baseline scores under differing experimental conditions, provide few direct comparisons among contemporaneous methods, and give limited attention to training stability and computational cost.
These limitations obscure the source of reported gains and the practical strengths and weaknesses of competing methods.
Costly agent training further motivates a common basis for comparison.
To address these gaps, we compare ten representative methods against GRPO on ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, Search-QA, and WebShop across three model sizes.
Our study comprises 132 training runs totaling 12,124.4 recorded H800 GPU-hours, with repeated evaluations over eight rollout seeds for the pretrained backbones and all eleven trained methods.
Beyond final task performance, we examine training progress, stability, and measured computational cost.
Our evaluation yields three key findings.
First, gains over GRPO remain limited in scope, with no method consistently outperforming it across settings.
Second, strong final performance can mask unstable training.
Third, additional training cost does not consistently translate into better performance.
We establish this benchmark to support fair, comprehensive comparison and guide future research toward reliable and cost-effective improvements in agent training.
Project page: https://aim-uofa.github.io/Self-Distillation-AgentRL/
highlights: More Methods, Better Agents? A Reality Check on Self

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Pre-Registered Genesis Accounting for Recursive Self-Improvement: First Audited Operator-Genesis Events in a Physics-Discovery Runtime
papers.summary:
Claims of recursive self-improvement are easy to make and hard to falsify: did improvement come from re-using designer-provided mechanisms, or from mechanisms the system authored itself?
We introduce a pre-registered, two-tier accounting: M1 counts machine-generated content instances within a designer-provided vocabulary, while M2 counts machine-authored mechanism types (new operators registered into the runtime's own vocabulary, with a held-out-validation certificate).
We report the first audited M2 genesis events.
In the primary event, depth-limited compositional search over elementary operators, judged by held-out R^2 on real NIST hydrogen Balmer measurements, produced the operator sq(inv(n)) = 1/n^2 -- the Rydberg-level form -- which no standard-library transform could express (held-out R^2: -0.546 best standard transform vs.
1.0000000 composed).
A protocol flaw (independent variable built by inverting the very law under test) was caught in audit and repaired via an independent-label protocol; extrapolation to unseen levels (n=8,9 trained on n<=7) attains relative error ~10^-6, four to six orders beyond the best standard operator.
A second event independently recovered sqrt(inv(a)) -- Kepler's velocity law -- from JPL ephemeris vectors.
Also incorporated: an audited compounding channel (first domain-level measurement: 1.109x accuracy ratio on a real held-out domain) and blind, decurated genesis exams whose honest tally is zero.
The Kepler event passes line audit; the hydrogen gap reproduces on He II; the certificate is threshold-stable.
Against eleven prior systems, the contribution is the measurement and governance of machine-authored mechanisms, not the search algorithm or rediscovered physics.
Limitations: exams were curated by agents who knew the textbook answer, triggers manual, grammar observer-injected; both events demonstrate capability to author, not yet autonomous genesis.

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: D-World: An Explicit World-Language-Action Model with Recursive Self-Improvement under Dual Control
papers.summary:
Frontier large language models (LLMs) now reason about space well enough to program robots, yet the world models behind robot policies are implicit, held in network weights or predicted video, and cannot be inspected or corrected directly.
We present D-World, an explicit world-language-action model built on the Sense, Plan and Act decomposition.
A perception agent writes the scene as an executable digital twin using generated vision and geometry code.
A planning agent searches for actions in simulation and, after each executed action chunk, revises the twin's object states and named physical parameters against what the robot measured.
A parameter revision is accepted only if replaying the latest chunk does not increase any measured residual beyond its tolerance, and every chunk is checked in the updated twin before it runs.
Structural mismatches return to perception for reconstruction.
We call this measurement-grounded cycle of correction and revision recursive self-improvement (RSI), in which the LLM stays frozen while the world it acts in improves.
We model the choice of actions that both advance the task and expose model error as a dual control problem and show that the cost of incorporating evidence into the twin sets the threshold at which probing pays, so cheap local revision counteracts the turn-off of cautious controllers.
Each episode runs a real-to-sim-to-real loop, and its recorded twins can be refitted and re-rendered offline into higher-fidelity environments for post-training.
Because perception and planning communicate only through the twin and language, either can be replaced by a learned model, and since inference dominates the loop, the loop speeds up with faster models.
On a dual-arm robot, towel and toaster tasks show local revisions, such as one reducing the bread's rendered-depth residual from 22.4 to 1.5 mm, that let execution continue without reconstruction.
highlights: We present D-World, an explicit world-language-action model built on the Sense, Plan and Act decomposition.

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Self-Retrospection Distillation: Turning Post-hoc Experiences into Prior Foresight
papers.summary:
Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) turns agent experience into learning signals primarily through scalar outcome rewards after interaction.
For group-relative objectives, however, this signal vanishes when all rollouts receive the same reward, even though their trajectories may reveal useful information about what the task requires and how the agent fails.
We ask a complementary question: can hindsight teach an agent what it could have anticipated before acting?
We introduce prospective learning, which uses post-hoc experience to supervise foresight predictions from the pre-interaction view, and instantiate it with Self-Retrospection Distillation (SRD).
Intuitively, a completed trajectory reveals knowledge that would have been useful and pitfalls that should be avoided; SRD distills this privileged hindsight into trajectory-blind foresight of the same policy.
Foresight serves only as a training target and need not be explicitly generated at inference time.
Across 10 tool-integrated reasoning and long-horizon agentic tasks, SRD complements RLVR and self-distillation baselines with gains of up to 24.2 pp.
Its advantage is especially pronounced when reward contrast is scarce: when 37--98% of rollout groups are reward-uniform across model scales, yet SRD can still exploit learning signal from sampled trajectories.
In the 2B setting, where 98% of groups are all-failure, the RLVR training ends up at 0.0% success, while adding SRD reaches 60.6% under the same rollout budget.
Our results suggest that post-hoc agent experience is useful not only for evaluating or improving behavior, but also for shaping predictive representations before available interaction.
Training code can be found at https://github.com/SalesforceAIResearch/SRD.
highlights: We ask a complementary question: can hindsight teach an agent what it could have anticipated before acting?

papers.groupName: Agent / RSI / Agentic RL 主题
papers.title: Self-Evolving Visual Agent via Margin Reward
papers.summary:
Visual agents that interleave reasoning with tool invocation have posed a promising direction for multimodal tasks.
However, learning effective tool invocation usually relies on curated question-answer pairs or expert demonstrations at scale, which are expensive to acquire.
In this study, we propose Marvo, a simple-yet-effective self-evolution approach that enables learning tool invocation from unlabeled images.
Marvo consists of two agents: (1) a challenger that generates question-answer pairs from unlabeled images, and (2) a solver that learns tool invocation by solving questions through reinforcement learning.
To encourage effective tool invocation, a good training question should be difficult enough to warrant tool use, yet remain within the solver's capabilities.
To this end, we introduce a margin reward to the challenger, defined as solver's performance difference with and without access to tools.
With the margin reward, we create an adaptive curriculum that encourages the solver to learn effective tool invocation.
Across benchmarks covering agentic reasoning, visual search, mathematical, and general real-world reasoning, Marvo improves average accuracy by up to 7.1\% --- demonstrating margin reward as a preferred way to scale question complexity without human supervision.

featuredPapers.title: OpenCollab: A Multi-Agent Coding Framework with Programmable Collaboration and Controllable Runtime
featuredPapers.authors: Chun-Wah Hsu, Kai Gong, Yu Wu
featuredPapers.summary:
Multi-agent coding systems are designed to tackle complex software engineering tasks through collaboration. 多代理编码系统旨在通过协作处理复杂的软件工程任务。
However, existing evaluations typically assume configured organizations are followed faithfully, whereas reality differs. 然而，现有的评估通常假设已配置的组织被忠实地遵循，而现实情况则有所不同。
This behavioral gap, combined with differences in underlying system components, prevents clear attribution of observed gains.
To this end, we introduce OpenCollab, a multi-agent coding framework that provides a unified infrastructure for programmable collaboration and controllable runtime. 为此，我们推出了OpenCollab ，这是一个多代理编码框架，为可编程协作和可控运行时提供统一的基础设施。
Specifically, OpenCollab unifies organization design, enforces experimental control on a shared runtime, and tracks execution through fine-grained event streams.
On this basis, we define Adherence to quantify whether the declared organization is actually realized.
Our experiments reveal that agents collaborate very differently across configurations: changing any single dimension shifts Adherence, from 47.2% to as high as 97.2%.
Furthermore, extensive agentic coding benchmarks show that OpenCollab (Duo) establishes new SOTA performance compared to the mainstream harnesses such as Mini-SWE-agent, OpenHands, Codex CLI, and Claude Code, showing that a well-designed organization can outperform strong existing harnesses, while OpenCollab's single-agent configuration uses the fewest tokens across all evaluated suites.
OpenCollab establishes a unified multi-agent infrastructure for easy programmable collaboration and controlled causal evaluation.

featuredPapers.title: Know What You Don't Know: Agentic Data Synthesis by Evolving Generation Space for Closed-Loop Learning
featuredPapers.authors: Wei Yang, Qing Ping, Youzhi Luo
featuredPapers.summary:
The continued improvement of large language models increasingly depends on synthetic experience, yet effective data synthesis for interactive agents requires not only executable and verifiable trajectories, but also interactions that provide learning value for the current task agent.
Existing methods increasingly incorporate environment feedback, data validation, or learner failures, but still face a feedback-to-decision gap: observed weaknesses do not directly specify how future synthesis should change, or whether they can be represented by the current synthesis space.
To address this gap, we propose EvoSyn, a learning-feedback-driven multi-agent framework that organizes synthesis around a revisable state specifying what interaction factors can be deliberately generated and where synthesis effort should be allocated.
A role-specialized multi-agent system translates learner feedback into synthesis revisions, while a Designer allocates synthesis directions and a Planner grounds them into executable experience.
This process enables within-space adaptation toward weak or under-covered regions and synthesis-space expansion that promotes newly discovered factors into explicit generation controls.
Experiments on $\tau^2$-Bench and CAR-Bench show that EvoSyn improves average task success by 13.3 points over the strongest synthesis baseline, while producing higher-quality and structurally broader synthetic experience and discovering controllable factors missed without learner feedback.

featuredPapers.title: EvoBelief: Falsifiable World Models for Self-Improving LLM Agents
featuredPapers.authors: Janet Wang, Jiang Guo, Yi Xiang
featuredPapers.summary:
Self-evolving LLM agents typically improve how they act through accumulated experience, reflection, or skills.
Yet even procedurally capable agents can fail when their beliefs about environment dynamics are incomplete, incorrect, or outdated.
We study a complementary axis of self-evolution: evolving those beliefs during deployment.
Such beliefs can support multiple tasks, but incorrect ones can also propagate across them.
We introduce EvoBelief, a self-evolving world model that represents environment knowledge as falsifiable hypotheses.
Unexpected outcomes and decision-relevant unknowns trigger hypothesis formation.
Later observations and controlled experiments provide independent validation before a rule can guide predictions or plans within its supported scope.
Counterexamples narrow or retire rules as the environment changes.
The language model remains frozen, and each rule remains linked to its evidence and the decisions it changes.
Across four benchmarks spanning static dynamics, hidden drift, and scientific discovery, EvoBelief improves task performance and reuses learned rules across tasks.
On ALFWorld without actor-side transition memory, it improves success over the matched Frozen World Model by 23.9% and 31.3% with Claude Haiku 4.5 and GPT-5.4, respectively.
On MiniGrid, it revises stale rules and recovers after unannounced dynamics changes.
In DiscoveryWorld's Reactor Lab, it discovers and validates quantitative laws, completing 83.3% of Normal-tier and 58.3% of Challenge-tier instances, versus 0% for each evaluated baseline.
These results demonstrate self-improvement through testable, revisable environment knowledge rather than model-parameter updates.
highlights: Self-evolving LLM agents typically improve how they act through accumulated experience, reflection, or skills.

featuredPapers.title: VETR: Execution-Grounded Self-Improving Agent for Symbolic Graphics Reasoning
featuredPapers.authors: Yingbo Ma, Kuangshi Ai, Gordon Dai
featuredPapers.summary:
Visual agents for symbolic graphics reasoning depend on executable world representations, yet continued improvement remains bottlenecked by ambiguous supervision from final renders.
Recent agentic systems refine scenes through repeated interaction, but they lack mechanisms to recursively extract actionable evidence from execution traces, overlooking which proposed symbolic edits survived, disappeared, or interfered during program execution.
To address this, we propose VETR (Verified Execution Trajectories for Refinement), a framework that enables agentic recursive self-improvement over executable world representations for symbolic graphics reasoning.
Within each task, VETR retains aligned program/render records with bounded runtime observations and introduces an execution refiner that compiles observed writes and state changes into constrained alternative programs.
The refiner validates their endpoints and preservation conditions against captured runtime state; the ordinary visual verifier then assesses goal relevance.
Repair construction makes no additional language-model calls, but can require additional executions.
Evaluations on BlenderGym (280 tasks) and BlenderBench (27 released tasks) with GPT-5.6-luna and Qwen3.8-27B show that VETR consistently outperforms existing refinement strategies, including BlenderAlchemy and VIGA.
Controlled ablations evaluate the contributions of execution refinement and role-asymmetric evidence organization under fixed generator-interaction caps.

featuredPapers.title: Locate, Judge, Read: Role-Specialized Tool Agents over a Knowledge-Point Index for Open-Domain Multimodal Document QA
featuredPapers.authors: Wenlin Lin, Fanzhe Wei
featuredPapers.summary:
Question answering over large heterogeneous document collections requires first finding the right passages and then reading them, yet current retrieval-augmented agents give one model both kinds of tools and let it schedule itself.
We present KnowForge, a pipeline separated by job: a hybrid-retrieval knowledge-point index; a Locator agent that can only search; a code-scheduled bridge judge that forces the missing second hop; a typed, size-bounded evidence pool that merges every search's ranking; a Deep Reader agent that can only read text, images and tables; and a synthesizer with a format checker.
With a self-hosted Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (3B active), KnowForge reaches F1 47.5 on the full open-domain M3DocVQA (2,441 questions, 3,368 PDFs), +11.0 over the published M3DocRAG system and +7.1 over one-shot retrieve-and-answer on the same index and model, and 53.5 with DeepSeek-V4-Flash.
On MultiHop-RAG it reaches 73.5 accuracy, above the strongest published RAG and GraphRAG results (71.2); on the single-document MMLongBench-Doc it lifts the same model from 34.8 to 47.0, level with GPT-4o reading page images (46.3).
Per-job ablations on the full benchmarks attribute the gain: the Deep Reader is worth 3.8, 9.8 and 0 points on the three corpora, tracking how visual each is; merging both agents into one with all tools and twice the rounds loses 1.9 F1 because it keeps searching instead of reading; a round-budget sweep shows a step at four Locator rounds and a plateau beyond; query latency scales with model calls rather than corpus size.
We serve the three indexed benchmarks as read-only knowledge bases (free registration) and release all prompts and the runner code: https://github.com/metask-ai/knowforge-bench

featuredPapers.title: X-AgentRed: Red-Teaming Personal Agents in Evolving Multi-Service Ecosystems
featuredPapers.authors: Yeonsung Jung, Zhiyuan Wang, Zifan Wang
featuredPapers.summary:
Personal agents increasingly connect to services across the web and applications by using tools.
As the effects of their actions accumulate and interact across services, unintended or harmful outcomes can arise when agents fulfill benign user requests.
Proactively identifying these compositional failures requires systematically exploring diverse cross-service paths.
Existing red-teaming methods often simply prompt LLMs to identify potentially harmful paths from task and environment descriptions or decompose harmful objectives specified by humans or LLMs into seemingly benign action combinations.
However, generation is biased toward patterns learned during training, potentially favoring familiar tool combinations and leaving novel cross-service interactions underexplored.
To address this, we propose X-AgentRed, a self-evolving red-teaming framework that discovers harmful tool call paths through a graph of tool dependencies and expands and refines them using execution feedback.
By analyzing each tool's effects, potential harms, and preconditions for execution, the red-teaming agent constructs a directed graph that captures how one tool's effects can satisfy another's execution preconditions.
Recipes sampled from this graph are instantiated as realistic scenarios in which agents can produce harmful outcomes.
Execution feedback enables self-improvement by diversifying paths that produce harm through tool substitution and refining preconditions at blocked steps in unsuccessful paths to enable further execution.
Across four frontier agentic models, X-AgentRed achieves $1.77\times$ the harmful path rate of STAC and explores a more diverse set of tools, yielding $2.99\times$ the tool coverage on average.
highlights: Personal agents increasingly connect to services across the web and applications by using tools.

featuredPapers.title: EvoDrive: Pareto Evolution for Safety-Critical Autonomous Driving via Self-Improving LLM Agents
featuredPapers.authors: Tong Nie, Yuewen Mei, Yihong Tang
featuredPapers.summary:
Generating safety-critical scenarios is essential for validating and improving autonomous driving systems, yet it inherently requires maximizing adversariality to expose failures while preserving realism.
Existing methods usually manage this trade-off with handcrafted heuristics, confining generation to known priors and overlooking underexplored patterns.
While recent open-ended agentic evolution can push this limit, unconstrained general agents lack strict simulator grounding and tend to collapse the multi-objective tension into single-scalar maximization.
Here we present EvoDrive, the first automated, LLM-based agentic evolution framework for multi-objective scenario generation.
EvoDrive employs a simulator-grounded actor-critic architecture where a memory-driven actor iteratively proposes improvements to the generators and critics filter out implausible candidates, and a self-evolving world evaluator routes promising proposals to optimize simulation budgets.
EvoDrive further maintains a Pareto archive of evaluated candidates to preserve diverse attack-realism trade-offs and guide future evolution via simulation feedback.
Benchmark results on MetaDrive and CARLA show that EvoDrive not only significantly expands the Pareto frontier across various generators, but also produces valuable scenarios for policy training.

featuredPapers.title: Do More Agents Help? Evaluating Accuracy and Cost in LLM Multi-Agent Workflows
featuredPapers.authors: Yuhang Fu, Ruishan Fang, Jiaqi Shao
featuredPapers.summary:
Choosing whether to replace a single-agent controller requires evidence on both task performance and inference expenditure.
We present BenchAgent, a shared evaluation framework, and compare six multi-agent workflow configurations against its single-agent reference, BenchAgent Core, across ten reasoning, coding, and tool-use benchmarks.
All configurations use GPT-4.1 and common tool and scoring interfaces; Core executions share the same step limits.
We measure accuracy and recorded token use over three runs on fixed task sets, with 3,302 instances per configuration per run.
EvoAgent reaches 79.70% mean pooled accuracy versus 76.65% for Core and exceeds Core in all three runs; the other five MAS trail by 1.71-8.76 percentage points.
LLM-Debate gains 9.67 points on HumanEval but loses 1.96 points in pooled accuracy while consuming 1.39 times the tokens of Core.
ChatEval gains 22.25 points on IFEval but trails Core in pooled accuracy with 4.34 times its token consumption.
The broad comparison and targeted analyses of retained responses provide evidence for workflow selection and identify answer preservation and resource allocation as directions for subsequent multi-agent optimization.

featuredPapers.title: Hyper Algorithm Design Agent: Evolving Learnable Optimizer from Zero
featuredPapers.authors: Zipei Yu, Yue-Jiao Gong, Zeyuan Ma
featuredPapers.summary:
Meta-Black-Box Optimization (MetaBBO) is one of the highlights in the recent AI for Optimization trend.
This paradigm's bi-level workflow leverages the learnable algorithm design policy at meta level to ensure the performance and generalization improvement on the low-level optimization task.
While MetaBBO helps advance the performance lower bound of the resulted optimization system, it is currently handcrafted and customized case by case to adapt different optimization problems, which inevitably introduces inherent subjectivity and hence restricts the performance upper bound and usability in practice.
In this paper, we address this issue by regarding MetaBBO's design loop as coding task, where we could introduce openendedness into MetaBBO with recursive self-improvement capability of advanced coding agents.
Specifically, we propose a dual-agent framework: i) a task agent continuously refines the codebase of a target MetaBBO approach through code evolution; ii) a hyper agent progressively modifies the task agent and itself to provide open-ended design behavior; iii) the evolved MetaBBO codebase is evaluated and all in-execution information is fed back to the agents for recursive self-referential improvement.
As a result, given a naive MetaBBO template, our framework automates a design evolution and finds novel variants superior to up-to-date human-made MetaBBO baselines.
Surprisingly, the experimental results also demonstrate that our framework supports fast adaption across different optimization domains.
Solid interpretation analysis further reveals interesting design principles emerge in such open-ended process.
This work serves as the first exploration on automating design of complex learning-assisted optimization algorithms.

featuredPapers.title: LongHarness: Advancing Agentic Reasoning over 100M-Token Corpora via Stateful Evidence Management
featuredPapers.authors: Songtao Huang, Zhijie Zhong, Xiaohan He
featuredPapers.summary:
Corpus-level long-context reasoning requires agents to acquire and integrate evidence across document collections that exceed their context windows.
Existing agent harnesses enable incremental access to these corpora, but acquired evidence and evolving conclusions often remain entangled in a growing interaction history.
This implicit state management can lead to two coupled failure modes: unbounded exploration, where retrieval expands the interaction history without resolving decision-relevant information gaps, and evidence-state drift, where previously acquired evidence or subsequent corrections fail to inform the current conclusion.
We present LongHarness, a model-agnostic harness that makes the interaction between acquired evidence and evolving conclusions explicit.
Its core mechanism, Evidence-Conclusion Coevolution, uses unresolved conclusions to guide exploration toward missing information, while newly acquired evidence strengthens or revises the conclusions that directed the search.
LongHarness couples this process with Evidence Lifecycle Management, which keeps accumulated evidence current and traceable throughout the interaction.
Together, these mechanisms focus retrieval on remaining information needs and keep conclusions aligned with current evidence.
We evaluate LongHarness on OfficeQA Pro V1 and V2, AA-LCR, and LongBench v2 using GLM-5.3-Flash and Qwen3.8-Flash.
Compared with direct reasoning using the same backbone, LongHarness improves GLM-5.3-Flash exact match on OfficeQA Pro from 15.8% to 60.2% on V1 and from 4.4% to 61.1% on V2.
Against state-of-the-art agent harnesses, it surpasses Claude Code by 12.0 percentage points on V1 and Codex by 18.9 points on V2.
With Qwen3.8-Flash, LongHarness reaches 61.7% on V1, outperforming Claude Code by 8.3 points and Codex by 12.0 points.

featuredPapers.title: MENTOR: Learning from Failure with On-Policy Pedagogical Intervention
featuredPapers.authors: Guanlan Yue, Hang Yu, Xiaoyong Huang
featuredPapers.summary:
Reinforcement Learning from Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) is a key driver for Large Reasoning Models, but it is vulnerable to "zero-reward collapse", a training failure where a sudden increase in task difficulty causes the learning signal to vanish.
We argue that the conventional approach of discarding these failed trajectories is wasteful, as they contain valuable diagnostic information about the model's cognitive gaps, a bright side that can be leveraged for recovery.
Existing solutions, however, often regress to static, "off-policy-style" interventions like pre-defined hint libraries or perform post-hoc refinement, failing to provide the adaptive, forward-looking guidance needed to escape the collapse.
To address this, we propose a paradigm shift towards on-policy pedagogical intervention and introduce MENTOR, a multi-agent framework that acts as a live mentor.
MENTOR diagnoses the root cause of failure in real-time and dynamically generates targeted, instructional prompts to guide the learning agent's next attempt.
As a plug-and-play module, MENTOR integrates seamlessly into existing policy optimization pipelines like GRPO without modifying the training infrastructure.
Extensive experiments on math and code generation show that MENTOR effectively mitigates zero-reward collapse, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines.
Notably, it achieves massive average relative gains of up to 78.3% on Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct over its base model.

featuredPapers.title: Taking Tokenization off the Host for Agentic LLM Serving
featuredPapers.authors: Mohammad Siavashi, Pascal Schwinte, Ali Banaei
featuredPapers.summary:
Agentic workloads resend long contexts that barely change between calls.
Prefix caching now skips most of their prefill, yet every request must still be tokenized in full before the cache can even be consulted.
Tokenization, a CPU stage long treated as negligible, becomes the largest part of time-to-first-token (TTFT), and a frontend that tokenizes for a whole GPU fleet limits how many GPUs it can feed.
We present GraphTok, a GPU tokenizer that runs the entire encoding pipeline, from pre-tokenization through byte-pair encoding (BPE) merging to token-ID assembly, as one replayable CUDA graph.
GraphTok reproduces the reference token IDs bit-for-bit on GPT-2, Llama 3, Qwen 2.5, DeepSeek-V3, and Gemma 3, hands short inputs to a CPU engine where the GPU cannot win, and plugs into unmodified vLLM and NVIDIA Dynamo.
GraphTok encodes one million GPT-2 tokens in 1.7-3.2 ms including data transfers, and on Llama 3 it is 4.7-6.0x faster than gigatoken, the strongest CPU tokenizer.
On TokTier's own single-request benchmark, it is 2.6-3.9x faster than gigatoken and up to 18.1x faster than TokTier.
In vLLM with a cached prefix, it lowers mean TTFT by 2.1-2.4x.
The largest gain is capacity.
Within a 2 s P99 target, one Dynamo frontend with GraphTok sustains 518 requests/s of 121k-token traffic, the busiest-hour load of 56 GPUs, against 296 with gigatoken and 18.5 with the default tokenizer.
Across 121k to one million tokens, this is 1.75-2.5x the load gigatoken sustains, with a P99 up to 64x lower where gigatoken's tail breaks.

featuredPapers.title: Rollout-Time Intervention: Unlocking Agentic Reinforcement Learning Beyond Policy Limits
featuredPapers.authors: Chen Xi, Ding Ruixue, Wang Zhigaoyuan
featuredPapers.summary:
Reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as a key paradigm for improving large language model (LLM) agents, enabling stronger reasoning, planning, and tool-use in interactive environments.
However, existing agent RL methods remain fundamentally constrained by an on-policy reasoning bottleneck: when tasks exceed the model's current capability boundary, effective trajectories become extremely sparse and training often collapses.
We introduce Rollout-Time Intervention (RTI), a technique designed to elicit successful trajectories beyond the policy's intrinsic exploration capacity.
RTI operates by leveraging reward-side evidence (i.e., evaluation rubrics) during rollout to convert erroneous trajectories into successful ones, providing effective learning signals for tasks that the policy rarely solves on its own.
Although intervention trajectories are inherently off-policy, we find that they can effectively guide policy optimization when trajectories with excessive distributional shifts are filtered out.
Extensive experiments across five benchmarks demonstrate that RTI consistently outperforms RL baselines, enabling the post-trained policy to approach the performance of substantially stronger contemporary LLMs and, more importantly, transcend its original capability boundary.
The code is available at https://github.com/Alibaba-NLP/qqr.

featuredPapers.authors: Sida Li, Yuanxin Liu, Linli Yao
featuredPapers.summary:
